articles.title: Famed ocean liner set to rule waves as artificial reef
articles.excerpt: Famed ocean liner SS United States, the largest passenger ship ever built in America and the world's fastest, has hit…
articles.fullText:
Famed ocean liner SS United States, the largest passenger ship ever built in America and the world's fastest, has hit the sea floor near Florida in a deliberate sinking designed to transform the vessel into the world's biggest artificial reef.

Wednesday's finale to a yearlong process preparing the ship to meet its destiny, 75 years after it was first launched at sea, was presented in a livestream with aerial views of the once-grand vessel's rusted hulk, stripped of its two smokestacks, quietly, slowly settling into calm waters of the Gulf of Mexico before succumbing to the deep.

The ship, measuring nearly 300 metres from stem to stern, was surrounded by onlookers and safety crews aboard dozens of tugboats and recreational vessels that accompanied the ocean liner as it was towed out to sea for its final voyage.

By then, work crews had spent months removing all environmentally unsafe materials from the ship, including residual fuel, wiring, glass, ductwork and other non-metal items, as well as any objects that could pose entanglement hazards for scuba divers.

The crews then cut holes strategically throughout the ship's hull and its decks to ensure that it would sink in a gradual, level and uniform manner, according to a fact sheet posted online by project organisers. No explosives were used.

Passageways were also cut through the 12 decks of the interior to allow for marine life to thrive in and around the ship on the sea floor.

If all goes as planned, the aging 20th-century vessel will come to rest upright on the gulf floor at a depth of almost 55 metres off the coast of Destin, Florida, a resort town and recreational fishing haven known for its white sand beaches and emerald green waters. The upper deck is expected to end up about 15 metres beneath the surface, organisers said.

The sinking process began at about 1pm but was so imperceptibly slow that the majority of the ocean liner's hull remained well above the surface as the sun set on the idle ship, surrounded by blinking lights of nearby vessels.

After hours, during which the waterline was seen creeping up the ship's hull inches at a time, the sinking accelerated as the sea poured through the holes cut into the lower decks and flooded the interior. In the final moments, livestream footage showed the ship abruptly listing to its port side before gently rolling into the sea and disappearing.

Warren Jones, a spokesman for the organisers, said the SS United States would probably take 30 to 60 minutes to reach the seabed once the interior compartments were all completely filled with water.

The SS United States, a wonder of post-Second World War oceanic luxury and engineering that carried the rich and famous across the Atlantic at speeds still unmatched, was retired from service in 1969 amid the rising popularity of commercial air travel.

The vessel sat moored for nearly 30 years in Philadelphia, seemingly destined to be sold for scrap, before authorities in Okaloosa County, in Florida's panhandle, stepped in to purchase the ship as part of a US$13 million project.

"We worked year after year to keep that ship from going to the scrap yard," said Jones, a boyhood passenger of the ship and representative of the SS United States Conservancy, a group that sold the ship to Okaloosa County.

After obtaining permission from the US Coast Guard and other agencies, the county had the vessel towed to a shipyard in Mobile, Alabama, where it was prepared for disposal at sea.

The SS United States will be in good company, joining a collection of more than 500 smaller underwater sites created from the remains of various sunken ships and concrete structures to create a divers' haven known as the Destin-Fort Walton Beach Artificial Reefs. (Reuters)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Teachers face cert, security rules in new schools bill
articles.excerpt: School teachers in Hong Kong will be required to hold practising certificates and barred from classrooms upon conviction of national…
articles.fullText:
School teachers in Hong Kong will be required to hold practising certificates and barred from classrooms upon conviction of national security offences under an education amendment bill to be gazetted on Friday.

The Education (Amendment) Bill 2026 will apply to all teachers, including principals, in publicly funded, private and international schools as well as kindergartens.

They will need to be registered and hold a practising certificate that is valid for no more than three school years.

Teachers applying for a practising certificate will also have to meet continuing professional development requirements.

The Education Bureau said this would help teachers keep up with changing local and global education policies and ensure their knowledge and teaching methods meet students’ and society’s needs.

A bureau spokesman said the bill could boost public regard for the profession and lift teachers’ standing in society.

"As role models and key persons for nurturing students, the words and deeds, conduct and values of teachers have a profound impact on students," he said.

"Amid the complex and rapidly changing development of our society, the public and parents have increasingly high expectations of teachers' professionalism.

"The bill meets schools' actual operational needs, encourages teachers to keep pace with the times and strengthens teacher management, with the ultimate goal of safeguarding the well-being of students."

The bill also includes safeguards to prevent people convicted of offences endangering national security from teaching in schools.

The bureau has consulted the sector since September last year and the Legislative Council's education panel on February 6.

The bill will be introduced to the Legislative Council for a first and second reading on November 25.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Union says 12-hour family care leave is 'good start'
articles.excerpt: Civil Servants General Union chairman Fung Chuen-chung welcomed on Thursday a plan to give government employees up to 12 hours…
articles.fullText:
Civil Servants General Union chairman Fung Chuen-chung welcomed on Thursday a plan to give government employees up to 12 hours of family care leave a year, calling it a very desirable step forward in letting staff look after their families while also helping attract talent and raise morale.

Asked on an RTHK programme whether 12 hours was enough, he said that was “hard to say” but that the cap could be reviewed after the scheme had been running for some time.

“Every employee faces different problems at different stages of life," Fung said.

"Some may have just gotten married and had a child while some older colleagues may need to look after elderly or sick parents – it really depends on individual needs.

"But overall we feel that going from having no family care leave to having some is a very desirable step forward.”

Fung said he hoped the business sector would follow suit so that other employees can also have such leave.

Potential abuse of family care leave provisions do not worry him, he said, as supervisors can always ask for proof if they have doubts.

The leave can be taken in blocks of one to four hours and is expected to start in January.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Two dead, several injured in NYC building collapse
articles.excerpt: Two people were killed on Wednesday and at least 17 others injured, including children, after a three-story building collapsed near…
articles.fullText:
Two people were killed on Wednesday and at least 17 others injured, including children, after a three-story building collapsed near a construction site in New York, city authorities said.

Images from the scene showed firefighters sifting through a pile of rubble in front of what appeared to be a residential property with its walls torn down, exposing a bedroom and a clothing wardrobe.

The building fell into a neighbouring excavation site, trapping several people who firefighters worked to free over several hours using drones, search dogs and chainsaws.

"We do not know how many people are still in the collapse zone, and this will be a prolonged operation," FDNY Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore told reporters at the scene in Flatbush, Brooklyn late Wednesday.

She said two people had died, without disclosing their ages, and said 17 others were hurt, including seven children.

Four people were critically injured.

More than 250 firefighters and paramedics responded to the scene, the FDNY wrote on X, adding that the cause of the collapse was under investigation.

New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani praised the emergency services for their work, saying the site involved "precarious wreckage to navigate and dangerous voids beneath the surface."

"I want to ask New Yorkers to please take a moment to pray for those who passed away today and all of those who are mourning their loss," he added at a news conference.

One witness, named only as Anthony, told PIX11 News that he heard people screaming and a "bomb"-like noise as the building collapsed.

Another witness, Melissa Orna, told The New York Times: "The whole building started shaking, and then it just fell."

The city's Department of Buildings said its inspectors were on the scene "assisting with recovery operations and conducting structural stability inspections of nearby buildings."

Ahmed Tigani, commissioner of the department, said construction workers were performing excavation at the time of the collapse.

He added that developers had plans approved for a three-story building at the site and were pursuing permission for a nine-story building. (AP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Apec to spotlight Shenzhen's global fintech push
articles.excerpt: Shenzhen’s financial services sector has been increasingly shaped by the deep integration of fintech and by its expanding overseas reach…
articles.fullText:
Shenzhen’s financial services sector has been increasingly shaped by the deep integration of fintech and by its expanding overseas reach, according to a senior executive at Ping An Property and Casualty Insurance Company.

Those trends are likely to draw wider attention next week, when global leaders arrive in the southern Chinese city for the Apec summit.

Xu Hua, assistant president of Ping An Property and Casualty Insurance Company, said the company’s own history mirrors Shenzhen's fintech development.

Founded in the 1980s in Shekou – an industrial area in western Shenzhen – it has grown from a regional insurer into a service network covering more than 110 countries.

Financial services already form one of Shenzhen’s four pillar industries. Ping An Property and Casualty Insurance Company is among the companies taking part in the meeting, and its parent, Ping An Group, is one of the official sponsors.

Xu said Shenzhen’s financial industry is most characterised by the deep integration of finance and technology.

"Shenzhen is an innovation capital. It brings together a group of representative technology companies. Technological innovation comes with trial and error and risk. It faces practical difficulties such as high research and development investment, rapid technology iteration and strong uncertainty," he said.

"Wherever innovation goes, insurance must follow. Overall, technology is Shenzhen’s underlying character. What insurance needs to do is serve well as a shock absorber for the real economy, so that technology companies dare to innovate, dare to invest and dare to go global."

Xu said the company has tailor-made more than 400 million yuan in dedicated risk protection for this summit.

He believes the meeting will not only bring short-term benefits, but also have long-term value, and hopes that the exchange opportunities at the Apec meeting can be transformed into sustained project cooperation.

For cross-border operations, he called for closer cooperation with insurers, reinsurers and professional service providers so that companies can better understand local risks and coverage requirements.

In sectors such as new energy, advanced manufacturing and the digital economy, he proposed that industry partners jointly assess emerging risks and develop products that keep pace with innovation.

Xu said that in addition to helping mainland enterprises go global and providing protection services for their overseas expansion, the company has also formed close ties with Apec economies.

The sector’s scale underscores its role in the city: financial services account for nearly 15 percent of Shenzhen’s GDP, and the Shenzhen Stock Exchange had more than 2,900 listed companies as of the end of September.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Kai Tak site leader charged over bribes
articles.excerpt: The ICAC has charged a site team leader on the Kai Tak Hospital project with taking HK$75,100 in bribes from…
articles.fullText:
The ICAC has charged a site team leader on the Kai Tak Hospital project with taking HK$75,100 in bribes from five imported electrical workers.

Zeng Chusong, 52, of subcontractor Billion Best (E&M) Engineering, faces 10 counts of an agent accepting an advantage.

He appeared at Tuen Mun Magistrates’ Courts for mention on Thursday morning.

The ICAC alleges that between September and November he accepted 10 bribes from the five workers, in return for helping them get jobs on the project.

Their daily pay was HK$1,300.

Fearing they would lose their jobs, they paid Zeng between HK$9,000 and HK$23,600.

China State Construction Engineering (Hong Kong), the main contractor, had applied under the Labour Importation Scheme for quotas used by its subcontractors, including the defendant and the five workers he referred to the site.

An ICAC said it maintains a zero-tolerance policy toward corruption and will continue to collaborate with the Development Bureau and other stakeholders to prevent the recurrence of crimes similar to this case.

"Construction workers who are solicited for bribes in exchange for employment should refuse immediately and report it to the ICAC," a spokesman said in a statement.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Higher standards set for arts groups' funding overhaul
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong Arts Development Council said on Thursday that the government’s move to tie the funding mechanism for major…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong Arts Development Council said on Thursday that the government’s move to tie the funding mechanism for major performing arts groups to performance and artistic merits will encourage the industry to deliver higher performance standards.

Under the new mechanism, a baseline subvention and a performance-based grant will each occupy half of the annual allocation.

The performance-based subvention will be calculated based on major performing arts groups’ non-government revenue, along with key performance indicators, such as their audience sizes and governance.

Medium-sized arts groups could be promoted to become major ones if they continuously deliver an outstanding performance in those areas.

Better performing groups can receive more funding, while underperforming ones could lose their status.

The reform will be launched gradually starting 2027-28, before it is fully implemented in 2032-33.

Speaking on RTHK, the council's vice-chairman Chris Ip said that the move would help to cultivate arts groups.

“First, I believe after the reform, it will allow major performing arts groups, no matter the pursuit of artistic merits, administration and talents, they will have a goal to do better. This will contribute to the healthy development for arts groups and the ecosystem of the whole cultural and arts sector," he said.

"Second, I have also noticed that there is a promotion ladder for medium and small-sized arts groups to have a goal to be able to do better.”

He said that the five-year transitional period offers enough time for arts groups to plan ahead and make changes, adding that they often come up with a blueprint for the next year or two.

The overhaul comes as the government’s annual funding to nine major performing arts groups rose more than 104 percent to about HK$450 million over the past two decades, but audience sizes and attendance rates have dropped.

Executive director Celina Chin from the Hong Kong Chinese Orchestra – one of the city’s major performing arts groups – told RTHK that she believed the decrease was also observed among smaller arts groups.

She believes this was partially due to a lower birth rate, saying that families used to watch performances together, and that the sector has to look for other audience groups now.

The sector has also been adapting to changes in people’s lifestyle, she said.

"People prefer to stay home and go out in the evening," she said.

"We can see that a lot of arts groups have adjusted their admission time or the performance time of their concerts to respond to that.”

Chin added that while arts groups will face pressure under the new mechanism, it is not a bad thing, saying that they will have to change direction or make sacrifices to maintain their positions.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: CE hails spirits of national rejuvenation
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee on Thursday said the SAR government was working to enrich resources for patriotic education, providing a…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee on Thursday said the SAR government was working to enrich resources for patriotic education, providing a broader platform for the younger generation to learn about national affairs.

Speaking at a ceremony to commemorate the 160th anniversary of the birthday of Sun Yat-sen, Lee said the national hero had deep ties with Hong Kong – the birthplace of his revolutionary ideas.

The best way to commemorate Sun is to carry forward his spirit of revitalising the nation, he said, adding that the city’s first five-year plan had proposed to step up patriotic education.

“The SAR government attaches great importance to patriotic education, and is making continuous efforts to promote mainstream values centred on the affection for our country and Hong Kong and in conformity with the ‘One Country, Two Systems’ principle to strengthen people’s sense of identity with the country and Chinese culture, enhance national confidence and pride, and foster a conscious commitment to upholding national unity and solidarity,” Lee said.

The CE went on to say that the SAR government would continue to host mainland study tours for students while supporting non-governmental organisations in hosting youth exchange programmes, so that youngsters in the city could experience firsthand the nation’s history, culture, and latest developments.

He urged people to make contributions to the country’s development and the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK, region mixed as Nvidia faces crunch on Huang sack
articles.excerpt: Asian stocks wobbled at the start of regional trading on Thursday, while Nvidia shares plunged in after-hours trading on news…
articles.fullText:
Asian stocks wobbled at the start of regional trading on Thursday, while Nvidia shares plunged in after-hours trading on news that its board may oust longtime chief executive Jensen Huang.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index opened down 194 points, or 0.8 percent, at 24,121.

The tech index fell 32 points, or 0.8 percent, to 3,995 while the China Enterprises Index slipped 66 points, or 0.81 percent, to 8,105.

On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index inched down seven points, or 0.21 percent, to open at 3,673.

The Shenzhen Component Index was 28 points, or 0.25 percent, lower at 11,361 while the ChiNext Index was down 0.5 percent at 2,559.

Nvidia's board is meeting late on Wednesday to decide whether to oust Huang, a source said, as the world's dominant supplier of AI processors grapples with the fallout of allegations that he had an affair with a suspected spy for China.

The New York Times has also reported that Huang had had an affair with a company executive who reported to him.

"It looks bad from every single angle," said Jake Dollarhide, chief executive at Longbow Asset Management in Tulsa, Oklahoma.

"I believe the board won't oust him until they have an all-star, a known entity in the tech sector, to replace him. At the end of the day, let's not forget that the Nvidia chip is the centrepiece of the AI story."

Shares in Nvidia slid more than eight percent after the bell, weighing on S&P 500 e-mini futures, which slipped 0.4 percent.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei opened 226 points, or 0.37 percent, higher at 61,475 and was 390 points higher still at one stage before noon.

In Seoul, the Kospi opened 10 points, or 0.2 percent, at 5,385 and, like the Nikkei, tracked up cautiously by 38 points at one stage before lunch.

"Renewed optimism around AI drove US equities higher overnight, with positive developments around CoreWeave and Anthropic adding to enthusiasm around the sector and helping the S&P 500 and Nasdaq rally," Westpac analysts wrote in a note. (Agencies)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Andreeva stuns Sabalenka to reach WTA Finals last four
articles.excerpt: French Open champion Mirra Andreeva stormed past Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 6-0 to reach the last four of the WTA Finals…
articles.fullText:
French Open champion Mirra Andreeva stormed past Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 6-0 to reach the last four of the WTA Finals on Wednesday as Elina Svitolina kept her bid on track with a three-set win over Karolina Muchova.

Russian 19-year-old Andreeva held her nerve after falling behind 4-1 in the opening set, winning the last 11 games to seal the round-robin victory in just 62 minutes.

"Oh my God, I'm even happier than I was after my first match," Andreeva said. "I feel like I can play another two matches, I'm so full of energy. I'm so pumped up. I'm so happy."

Andreeva, whose three titles this year include her maiden major at Roland Garros, is making her singles debut in the elite season-ending event.

The world number three seemed to be feeling the nerves in the early going against second-ranked Sabalenka.

Irked that she had given up a break with a double fault, she was able to flip the switch, dealing handily with Sabalenka's big serves and pushing the Belarusian star back with her own big groundstrokes.

Andreeva crucially kept momentum on her side with a break for a 3-0 lead in the second set.

Sabalenka, trailing 0-40, saved three break points, but Andreeva gave herself another with a swinging volley winner and grabbed another break when a Sabalenka forehand flew just long.

The increasingly demoralised Sabalenka had no answer. After the Belarusian smacked a backhand into the net to give her opponent match point Andreeva polished things off with a service winner.

It was another disappointing performance for the 28-year-old Sabalenka, whose three wins this season include prestigious back-to-back victories at Indian Wells and Miami but no Grand Slams.

Making her sixth straight Finals appearance, Sabalenka can still advance if she beats Svitolina in their final round-robin match on Friday.

Svitolina roared back from a set down to beat Muchova 3-6, 6-2, 6-2.

Ukrainian veteran Svitolina lifted the WTA Finals trophy in 2018 but hadn't been back to the elite season-ending event since 2019.

She got off to a rocky start against Muchova, who broke Svitolina three times in the opening set.

Trailing 2-1 on serve in the second Svitolina found her range, winning five straight games to force a third set.

"I was not happy with the first set," Svitolina said. "I didn't play as well. I just made some adjustments, tactical adjustments.

"I think it helped me also to be more aggressive, because I was too passive in the first set," Svitolina said.

Muchova's second round-robin defeat coupled with Andreeva's victory means the Czech was eliminated from semi-final contention. (AFP)

Edited by Nazvi Careem

articles.title: Pope Leo lands in Lima for Peru homecoming
articles.excerpt: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Peru on Wednesday, a nostalgic return to the nation where he spent two decades as…
articles.fullText:
Pope Leo XIV arrived in Peru on Wednesday, a nostalgic return to the nation where he spent two decades as a missionary before being tapped to lead the world's 1.4 billion Catholics.

The 71-year-old pontiff landed in Lima on the final leg of an arduous 12-day Latin American tour, just weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer.

"He is coming home," said 32-year-old street vendor Alexander Torres in the Peruvian capital. "He will be welcomed as if he never left the country."

"The pope is Peruvian!" cried some of the faithful, who lined the streets dozens-deep along the route from the airport, as phalanxes of soldiers in red and green berets stood guard.

The pope began the day in Lujan, Argentina, drawing more than three million people for a mass that was part farewell, part homage to his late Argentine predecessor, Pope Francis.

"Thank you, Argentina, for welcoming me with open arms," he said, addressing the largest crowd of his 18-month papacy.

The faithful climbed fences, barriers, trees and lampposts to catch a glimpse of their spiritual guide.

"It was a unique, unforgettable experience," Daiana Rivero, 36, told AFP.

"The pope's visit leaves a very powerful emotion and I feel this is going to be a turning point for our country," she said.

Born in Chicago, Leo's return to Peru will take him from the deep Amazon to 3,400 meters up in the Andes.

He will also make what is sure to be an emotional return to Chiclayo, the northern city where he was bishop for a decade.

Throughout his trip to Uruguay and Argentina, the pope has not shied away from tackling sensitive political and social topics.

In Argentina, he pointedly demanded a more inclusive economy and better protections for the vulnerable – comments widely interpreted as criticism of aid-slashing President Javier Milei.

"There is room for everyone, especially the neediest: the poor and hungry, migrants, the sick and prisoners," he said, sporting a white-and-sky-blue robe – the colors of the Argentine flag – associated with the Virgin of Lujan.

In Peru he will find a deeply divided nation, still coming to terms with its violent past under Alberto Fujimori, the father of the current president, Keiko Fujimori. The late Fujimori was found guilty and imprisoned over human rights violations in his fight against Shining Path leftist rebels.

The pope will also find a society reckoning with high crime rates, deep inequalities and a rising cost of living.

"It's like when mom or dad shows up while we're fighting with a sibling – pulling each other's hair – and they step in and say, 'take it easy, calm down, give each other a hug,'" said Jessibel Quispe, a 39-year-old mother and homemaker.

"The pope coming is a message of hope and peace, that will help our politics a lot" she said. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Trump defends Iran war in Veterans Day address
articles.excerpt: US President Donald Trump has defended the war against Iran at a US Veterans Day commemoration that saw his defence…
articles.fullText:
US President Donald Trump has defended the war against Iran at a US Veterans Day commemoration that saw his defence secretary publicly admonished for a lack of decorum.

"The bravery and skill of our amazing American warriors has absolutely been incredible," Trump said in an address at Arlington National Cemetery just outside Washington.

"When this conflict is over, and it will be soon, the entire world will be a much safer and better place, more peaceful place, and a place without the kind of danger that we had to suffer."

The war, which began on February 28 with US and Israeli strikes against Iran, has so far cost the lives of 23 US service members and wounded several hundred more, according to the latest Pentagon figures.

Trump said in his remarks that the conflict was started not by Washington but by Tehran, which "has been waging war on America since 1979." He stressed that US forces were acting in order to halt Iran's capacity to build a nuclear weapon.

Trump, 80, attended a wreath-laying ceremony at the cemetery's Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, a sacred symbol for America's lost service members.

During his speech before troops, veterans and top officials in his administration, Trump namechecked Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, who was in attendance, saying he had "done a fantastic job."

Republicans in the US House of Representatives on Tuesday blocked an effort – launched by an outgoing Republican lawmaker – to impeach Hegseth for allegedly waging war without congressional authorisation and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief.

Hegseth stirred even more controversy at the ceremony: an army sentinel watching over the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier reprimanded a small group of people that included Hegseth, his wife and several aides, when some of them laughed after posing for a picture in front of the sacred site.

"All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times," the sentinel called out, halting his patrol to face the group as they walked up some stairs to leave. Hegseth turned around to look at the guard.

During his remarks, Trump brought up the issue of the 250-foot-tall triumphal arch he hopes to build just outside the cemetery, saying it would be dedicated "soon."

On Tuesday, the family of John F Kennedy asked a court to prevent its construction, arguing the massive structure would block views and cast shadows over the gravesites of the slain president and other Kennedy relatives buried at Arlington National Cemetery.

The project also faces lawsuits from a group of veterans, the city of Washington and the state of Virginia. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang: WSJ
articles.excerpt: Nvidia's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after he had two extramarital affairs, the Wall Street Journal reported…
articles.fullText:
Nvidia's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after he had two extramarital affairs, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter.

The board is preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine his future, the report added.

Huang's potential departure would leave a leadership vacuum at the roughly US$4 trillion chipmaker he co-founded and built over more than three decades to become the dominant supplier of AI chips at the centre of the global artificial-intelligence boom.

The company's shares slid about 8 percent in after-hours trading. Including Wednesday's after-hours selloff, Nvidia has lost about US$600 billion in stock market value this week since the board announced its investigation.

"Huang being removed immediately could be challenging for Nvidia since it does not have a succession plan in place... If Mr Huang broke the law or violated company policies, the board is likely to act as soon as they have proof," Gil Luria, head of technology research at DA Davidson, said.

Earlier in the day, the New York Times reported that Huang had an extramarital affair with a company executive who reported to him.

The relationship was with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, the New York Times said, citing five people who worked at the company.

When reached by phone Wednesday and asked about his relationship with Powell, Huang said, "I don't think you should be talking to me directly." He then hung up, the New York Times reported.

Nvidia and Powell did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Reuters could not immediately verify the reports.

The reports mark a sharp escalation in a controversy that began with revelations about Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a woman US intelligence has said was involved in facilitating shipments of Nvidia chips to Chinese firms.

Beijing has dismissed allegations that Alice Huang was a spy for China as "groundless speculation".

In a memo to employees on Sunday, Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife and took "full responsibility," but gave no details about the relationship.

The same day, Nvidia's board launched an investigation into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The probe is being overseen by independent directors with outside legal counsel. At the time, the board expressed confidence in Huang.

US President Donald Trump has said he had not discussed the allegations with Huang but voiced support for the Nvidia chief, calling him "an honourable guy" who had "done an amazing job for our country."

Huang faces a potential congressional subpoena if he doesn't respond to a request to provide a closed-door briefing about the allegations that he had a close relationship with the Chinese businesswoman.

Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 with Curtis Priem and Chris Malachowsky. Its early hits were graphics chips for computer games, before its CUDA software opened the processors to general computing and, later, AI. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Democrat Colom wins tight Senate race in Mississippi
articles.excerpt: Democrat Scott Colom won a stunning upset in Mississippi's US Senate race on Wednesday after days of counting, US media…
articles.fullText:
Democrat Scott Colom won a stunning upset in Mississippi's US Senate race on Wednesday after days of counting, US media projected, defeating Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith to become the Southern state's first Black senator since the Reconstruction era that followed the US Civil War.

It was one of the final outstanding races to be called since Tuesday's elections, in which Democrats overwhelmed Republicans to win control of both chambers of the US Congress.

Mississippi officials took days to count ballots in a race that was so tight that Colom at times led by only a few dozen votes.

A spokesman for Hyde-Smith confirmed that she has called Colom to concede.

Colom, a 43-year-old district attorney, became the first Democrat to win a Mississippi Senate seat since John Stennis in 1982.

Hyde-Smith, 67, who was first elected in 2018, had consistently led in opinion polls in a state that US President Donald Trump won by nearly 23 points in 2024. Trump campaigned in Mississippi for Hyde-Smith near the end of the race.

Democratic Senate leader Chuck Schumer celebrated on social media.

“Scott Colom is the only person who could’ve gotten this done,” Schumer wrote. “Along with his staff and volunteers, Scott ran the campaign of a lifetime and re-imagined what’s possible for Democrats in the South.”

Colom told Reuters in an October interview that Mississippi voters felt "betrayed" by Trump policies like the war in Iran, which has driven up fuel prices.

On the campaign trail, he focused on reaching voters through town halls as well as visits to public housing, festivals and food trucks, Colom said. "We did it the hard way, the grassroots way," he said.

October rallies with Democratic Senators Raphael Warnock of Georgia and Cory Booker of New Jersey boosted Colom's campaign.

The last Black candidate elected to the Senate in Mississippi was former slave Blanche Bruce in 1874.

In 2023, Hyde-Smith blocked Colom's nomination by former President Joe Biden to serve as a federal district judge in northern Mississippi, citing his position on transgender issues. Mississippi's other US senator, Republican Roger Wicker, supported his nomination. (Reuters/AP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Kane says England record a 'testament to dedication'
articles.excerpt: England captain Harry Kane said breaking the Three Lions' appearance record in Thursday's Nations League clash with Croatia will represent…
articles.fullText:
England captain Harry Kane said breaking the Three Lions' appearance record in Thursday's Nations League clash with Croatia will represent a "testament to all the dedication" that has gone into his career.

When Kane leads England out at Wembley to win his 126th cap, he will surpass the previous record held since 1990 by former goalkeeper Peter Shilton.

It will be the latest landmark in an incredible 12 months for the Bayern Munich striker, who in October became the first English player in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or.

The 33-year-old Kane is also England's record scorer with 91 goals.

"It's definitely up there as the biggest (achievement)," Kane told reporters on Wednesday.

"I think it showcases consistency at the highest level. Testament to all the dedication, the time people don't see that keeps me fit and healthy. This is one of the biggest milestones in my career."

Since leaving Tottenham to join Bayern in 2023, Kane has taken his game to another level.

Aside from scoring 156 goals for the German club, he has also finally laid a ghost to rest in winning the first silverware of his career, including Bundesliga titles in 2025 and 2026.

However, England have not won a major tournament since winning the 1966 World Cup on home soil.

Kane suffered fresh frustration in July as he lost in a World Cup semi-final for the second time when Argentina came from behind to beat England.

Kane said he hoped there was enough left in his legs for another tilt at the World Cup in 2030.

"In terms of what's next, I don't like to put limits – 100 goals (for England) is a milestone to reach as soon as possible," said Kane.

"We've done extremely well in tournaments, going into latter stages.

"I'm feeling really good and hopefully there will be many more years to see what I can achieve."

Other near-misses with Kane for England include two losses in European Championship finals, in 2021 on penalties to Italy and then in 2024 to Spain.

But he went on to win his first trophy with Bayern the following season.

Kane said, despite the perpetual disappointments, he kept believing one day his luck would change in terms of silverware.

"Obviously after any big loss, especially a final, you look into everything, you try and analyse it," he said.

"I don't think I ever doubted that it would come." (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: US Treasury chief relocates to base after Iran threat
articles.excerpt: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has relocated from his home in the Washington area to a military base "for his…
articles.fullText:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has relocated from his home in the Washington area to a military base "for his safety," an official source familiar with the situation confirmed on Wednesday – amid threats linked to Iran.

Bessent is the third senior official in US President Donald Trump's cabinet reported to have moved into military housing, following US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth.

Bessent has spearheaded a US push to cripple Iran's economy since the start of the Middle East war through a web of sanctions.

Bessent "will not be deterred by the Iranian regime's threats" and will continue implementing actions which are "collapsing Iran's economy," a Treasury spokesperson said.

US national intelligence chief Jay Clayton warned last month that Tehran has "substantially increased" its efforts to target Americans in the Middle East and beyond.

Bessent's relocation came after officials determined the Treasury chief's Washington home could be geolocated following publication of a photo of the property.

"Security concerns began to increase which have now forced the Secretary to relocate to a military base for his safety," the source said. "The news media has an obligation to act responsibly amid growing threats against public officials."

Washington ordered non-essential US embassy staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia last month, following increasing attacks from Tehran-backed Houthi fighters.

The US military has also removed some aircraft from two British bases in recent weeks following reported threats from Iran.

Diplomatic efforts to end the war appear to be gathering steam, with Rubio saying on Tuesday that the US squeeze of Iran's economy made further attacks unnecessary. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Man U reach verbal agreement with Pochettino: reports
articles.excerpt: Manchester United have reportedly reached a "verbal agreement in principle" with Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick as their manager…
articles.fullText:
Manchester United have reportedly reached a "verbal agreement in principle" with Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick as their manager in a bid to revive the fortunes of the struggling English giants.

Carrick's position at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation following United's worst start to a season in 40 years, leaving them languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run.

He remains in post but it is believed Carrick's future will be decided at a meeting attended by influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox in Monaco on Wednesday.

Berrada and Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing Carrick.

United States head coach Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.

It was only three months ago, however, that Pochettino signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup.

US Soccer would be due compensation should he move to Manchester, with the 54-year-old understood to have a £7.5 million release clause.

But Sky Sports reported Wednesday that United have "reached a verbal agreement in principle" with Pochettino, linked with a move to Old Trafford on several previous occasions, to become their new head coach.

Carrick was seen arriving at United's Carrington training ground on Wednesday but it appears to be only a matter of time before his turbulent reign comes to an end.

The 45-year-old had been granted a stay of execution after he was widely expected to be axed in late October following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth.

But United were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea, then scrambled a last-gasp 3-2 win against Roma in the Champions League after falling two goals down.

It appeared former United and England midfielder Carrick would be on the way out when his team twice trailed Aston Villa by two goals on Sunday.

When United scored twice in stoppage-time to rescue an improbable 4-4 draw, it was interpreted as a positive sign for Carrick as the players were still fighting for him.

But a change now appears likely, with former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe, ex-Chelsea chief Antonio Conte and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann also linked with the United job.

United have the rest of the two-week international break to resolve their managerial situation before returning to action at bitter rivals Liverpool on November 22.

Carrick has presided over United's slide to 18th place, their lowest position 10 games into a top-flight season since 1986/87 when they were 20th.

He was hired on a permanent basis in the close-season after leading United to a third-place finish in the Premier League during his spell as interim boss.

Carrick had won plaudits for steadying the ship after Ruben Amorim's volatile reign ended in the sack in January.

But, hampered by the club's underwhelming recruitment in the transfer window, Carrick's team have endured a steep decline this term.

United, who have not won the title since Alex Ferguson's final season as boss in 2012/13, only signed midfielders Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos in the summer transfer window despite the glaring need for new forwards.

Carrick has struggled to maintain discipline among his squad, dropping captain Bruno Fernandes after he criticised his manager's tactics during a 4-1 thrashing at Champions League debutants Como.

He also axed Lisandro Martinez after the United defender criticised the club's hierarchy for their lack of top-quality signings.

United fans have remained largely supportive of Carrick, focusing their anger on majority owners the Glazer family, Ratcliffe and the under-achieving players. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: CoreWeave results lift tech stocks as dollar gains
articles.excerpt: Stock markets rose on Wednesday on renewed optimism over AI following strong results from data centre operator CoreWeave, while the…
articles.fullText:
Stock markets rose on Wednesday on renewed optimism over AI following strong results from data centre operator CoreWeave, while the dollar extended a rally on expectations for at least one more Federal Reserve interest rate hike.

Wall Street's main indices enjoyed a buoyant session led by the tech-heavy Nasdaq, which finished up 1.6 percent.

"The primary catalyst for the upside action is, ironically, one of the primary catalysts for the downside action that had been seen in the AI trade," said Briefing.com analyst Patrick O'Hare.

"That would be CoreWeave, which posted better-than-feared third-quarter results and issued a reassuring outlook that has quieted some of the debt financing concerns surrounding its AI buildout plans," he added.

CoreWeave said sales would come in at US$13-US$13.3 billion this year, beating estimates and soothing worries about its ability to finance its heavy debt burden, which fuelled a sharp sell-off last month.

Shares in CoreWeave surged nearly 25 percent.

"This relief trade is carrying across the AI trade complex to include hardware, software, and semiconductor stocks," said O'Hare.

The gains in US equities came despite signalling from US central bankers that the Fed will lift interest rates in December to address persistent inflation. The US dollar rose to its highest level since May 2025 after one top Fed official floated the idea of a 0.5 percentage point interest rate increase next month.

After last week's rout fuelled by fears that Democrats would ramp up regulation of AI, tech stocks have bounced this week on bargain-buying and hopes that fears may have been overdone.

"Overall, the market is putting AI doubts to one side and is focusing on revenue potential and mega cap IPO as we move through this week," said Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB.

Semiconductor companies advanced, including scandal-plagued Nvidia, which bounced 3 percent after a two-day rout following the bombshell revelation of an affair between CEO Jensen Huang and a woman suspected of being a spy. The firm is now the subject of an FBI investigation.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 254 points, or 0.5 percent, to 52,486, the S&P 500 gained 98 points, or 1.3 percent, to 7,619 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 400 points, or 1.6percent, to 25,466.

Oil prices advanced after sinking on Tuesday on hopes for a US-Iran agreement to end their war and reopen the crucial Strait of Hormuz. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Wang Yi holds 'positive, constructive' call with Rubio
articles.excerpt: Foreign Minister Wang Yi held a "positive and constructive" call with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday, Xinhua…
articles.fullText:
Foreign Minister Wang Yi held a "positive and constructive" call with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday, Xinhua news agency reported, with Beijing expressing willingness to strengthen communication and cooperation with Washington.

The talks come roughly a week ahead of the Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, where Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump are expected to meet.

The current stability in China-US relations has not come easily, Wang said, calling it "a rational choice made by the two major countries based on respective and shared interests," the Xinhua report said.

The Xinhua report quoted Wang as saying that China, having maintained a stable and consistent policy towards the United States, is willing to strengthen communication and cooperation with Washington, properly handle differences and sensitive issues, support each other in hosting the 2026 Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting and the G20 Summit, and work to bring a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability into effect and deliver results.

Xi and Trump have met twice already this year and Rubio told reporters on Tuesday there was work underway to arrange a trilateral meeting on the Apec sidelines involving Xi, Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Rubio said Trump wants that meeting to happen and added: "We think it should be possible."

Trump said on Sunday he thought he would meet Xi and Putin in Shenzhen and discuss ending the war in Iran and denuclearisation.

He said in October that he was open to three-way arms control talks with Xi and Putin, which he said would focus on nuclear weapons.

China's foreign ministry said last month that its "nuclear strength is by no means at the same level with that of the US and Russia" and that it would be "neither fair, reasonable nor realistic to ask China to join the so-called trilateral nuclear disarmament negotiations at this stage."

The Wall Street Journal has reported that Putin has pitched using a trilateral meeting to discuss an end to Russia's long-running war in Ukraine. (Xinhua/Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Millions of Spaniards strike to protest housing crisis
articles.excerpt: Four million Spanish workers took part in a general strike on Wednesday, unions said, enduring stormy weather to set up…
articles.fullText:
Four million Spanish workers took part in a general strike on Wednesday, unions said, enduring stormy weather to set up picket lines in a protest against the country's housing affordability crisis, less than three weeks before a snap general election.

It is the first general strike since workers downed tools in 2012 against austerity measures during the euro zone debt crisis. The walkout is backed by Spain's two largest unions, UGT and CCOO, representing more than a million workers, as well as tenants' associations angry about rising rents and evictions.

Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez hopes to harness voter resentment over housing in the November 29 election to shift the political narrative away from corruption cases involving his inner circle and a deadly train crash last month. So far, his Socialist Party still trails in opinion polls.

Unions described the strike as a success even though participation was uneven across Spain, with the strongest support in coastal regions where housing pressures have been particularly acute.

Spain has a deficit of about 750,000 homes, which is set to grow to more than a million by 2028, according to the central bank.

With fewer people able to afford a home, renting has increased sharply, putting pressure on that market. The average rental price of €1,176 is equivalent to about 98.7 percent of a young person's average monthly salary in Spain, according to the Youth Council of Spain.

Angela de Miguel, vice president of Spain's main business lobby CEOE, said the strike was counterproductive because small businesses were also affected by the housing crisis, since shortages of homes made recruitment more challenging.

Speaking on state broadcaster TVE, she said the solution was to build more homes and to lower taxes in construction and the home-buying process.

The tenants' union said it expected participation in the strike to reach 5 million people by the end of the day. Spain has around 23 million workers, according to the national statistics institute.

According to UGT and CCOO, participation in the strike reached 90 percent at ports and in the automotive sector, with "total stoppages" reported at factories including Volkswagen's in Navarre and SEAT's in Barcelona.

Barcelona's metro said no trains would run outside peak commuting hours, while Madrid's metro said peak-hour usage was down 42 percent compared to the same period last week.

However, with more people able to work remotely and the increasing weight of services in Spain’s economy, the impact of the strike is likely to be less pronounced than in previous years, according to Miguel Cardoso, chief economist at BBVA Research.

Spain's fast-growing hospitality and finance industries are less unionised than the public and industrial sectors.

Police had reported 40 arrests by midday from 476 incidents linked to the general strike, including blockades of offices and industrial estates and the burning of rubbish containers.

Unions said they would file a criminal complaint against what they described as a “disproportionate” response during a police operation involving tear gas and batons that left 20 protesters injured.

The strike follows weeks of demonstrations provoked by the eviction and subsequent death of an 87-year-old woman in Madrid.

Those protests, along with parliament's rejection last month of government decrees aimed at curbing evictions and limiting rent pressures, prompted Sanchez to call the snap election. (Reuters)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Russia, Ukraine reach deal on prisoner swap
articles.excerpt: Russian and Ukrainian negotiators agreed to a major prisoner exchange at two days of peace talks in Abu Dhabi that…
articles.fullText:
Russian and Ukrainian negotiators agreed to a major prisoner exchange at two days of peace talks in Abu Dhabi that ended on Wednesday, but US mediators said differences remained on major issues, including territory.

At their first negotiations in nine months, the two countries agreed in principle to exchange prisoners of war and to determine the numbers on Thursday.

US envoy Jared Kushner said the new swap would be the "biggest humanitarian release of prisoners" in the ongoing conflict, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said its scope would be "significant."

Both Russia and Ukraine said that progress had been made in the Abu Dhabi talks and negotiations would continue. But there was little else in the way of concrete breakthroughs announced after the US-brokered meetings.

Kushner, US President Donald Trump's son-in-law, said mediators were appealing to each side's interests to end Europe's biggest conflict since World War Two and he expressed confidence they would find a pathway to peace.

Kyiv has strongly rejected Russian President Vladimir Putin's demands to surrender the whole of the eastern region of Donbas in return for peace. With talks deadlocked on land, US mediators have tried to steer discussions towards postwar security guarantees and reconstruction.

"The reality is there is no trust right now between the sides and that is to be expected after a conflict like this," Kushner said, adding that the talks had touched on territorial issues and that these would be the hardest to resolve.

"I think this was a good first step," he said.

Kushner said he and fellow US envoy Steve Witkoff will travel to Moscow on Thursday for talks with Putin, where they will raise the question of adding European partners to the talks, who Kushner said must be at the table.

The US negotiators then plan to fly to Ireland to meet with Zelensky, who is due to attend a meeting of European leaders there.

Zelensky told reporters in Dublin on Wednesday that Ukraine was focused on achieving progress on an accord this year.

"A lot will depend today on the format of the dialogue of the American and Russian sides tomorrow... I believe it is also very important for the Americans...to achieve a result this year, in my view, given what we are seeing happening," he said.

"And it seems to me that they really do want this very much."

Russia and Ukraine accused each other of launching attacks overnight, despite the Abu Dhabi peace talks.

Russia hit six electricity substations in central Ukraine, Ukrainian officials said, and an attack on a market in the Odesa region killed three people. A Ukrainian drone attack killed one person in Russia's Belgorod region, local officials said.

Ukrainian negotiator David Arakhamia said the talks had been tough, with Russia's delegation arriving with "strict directives", but the conversations provided "good momentum" towards reaching a solution by the end of the year.

Although European officials and Nato representatives met US and Ukrainian envoys in Abu Dhabi, Russia's delegation refused to meet them. Arakhamia said future peace talks must be multilateral and include Europe at the table.

Russia's chief negotiator, Vladimir Medinsky, told Russian state TV he thought a peace deal was closer after the talks but "a great deal depends on Ukraine, on the US stance, and on whether Europe comes to its senses".

Russia has repeatedly criticised European military support for Ukraine. As the Trump administration has scaled back its direct aid to Ukraine, Europe has become the leading provider of finance and military support to Kyiv.

Reaffirming Moscow's long-standing demands, Medinsky told Russian state news agency TASS that "every inch" of Russian land would be returned to Russia – an apparent reference to Putin's insistence that Ukraine surrender all of the Donbas. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: What to know about this year’s UN climate talks
articles.excerpt: It’s that time of year again: Thousands of delegates, lobbyists, and journalists are gathered for the annual UN climate talks…
articles.fullText:
It’s that time of year again: Thousands of delegates, lobbyists, and journalists are gathered for the annual UN climate talks, taking place this time in Antalya, Turkey.

COP31 officially kicked off on November 8, marking the beginning of negotiations on one of the biggest stages of the climate world. Turkey and Australia are cohosting this year’s talks, which are scheduled to wrap up on November 20.

This annual gathering can often serve as an indicator of where the world stands on addressing and adapting to the climate crisis. And this year’s talks are sure to be a doozy—expect a lot of back and forth on fossil fuels and climate finance in particular. Here’s what you should know about COP31.

In recent years, the tension always feels high when COP rolls around. (COP stands for “Conference of the Parties.”) But this year feels especially charged: The world is still grappling with the ongoing war in Iran, which has disrupted the Middle East and sent economic shock waves around the world as energy prices have spiked.

This year’s COP will be the second without a formal delegation from the US. President Trump formally withdrew the country from the Paris Agreement earlier this year and is in the process of withdrawing from the UN Framework Committee on Climate Change. That’s the treaty that allows formal participation in negotiations.

Meanwhile, things aren’t looking good for the Paris Agreement, which was established at UN climate talks 11 years ago, setting a goal of limiting warming to 1.5 °C over preindustrial levels. In a report published in September, the UN Environment Program acknowledged that global warming is set to exceed that 1.5 °C goal, “likely within the next few years.”

So as climate talks kick off, there’s an obvious, urgent question looming about how to quickly cut emissions to limit warming. There’s also the major issue of how to pay for efforts to address emissions and to help a warming world endure the inevitable damage.

Two years ago, talks ended in a goal of mobilizing $300 billion per year by 2035 to help pay to reduce emissions and adapt to climate change. (Rich nations provided $136.7 billion in 2024, according to the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development. ) And last year, the COP30 agreement included a goal of tripling the money for adaptation over that period. (Such funding has been quite flat over the past few years.)

The world got a tragic reminder of just how high the stakes are earlier this year, when a glacier collapse caused devastating flooding in the Himalayas. The flood killed approximately 1,500 people, left over 5,000 missing, and caused nearly $5 billion in damage. The UN loss and damages fund committed $20 million to helping Nepal recover (less than 1% of the total estimated cost to the country).

Another key trend to watch is how the formal negotiations engage with the topic of fossil fuels. Three years ago, the final agreement text explicitly called for a transition away from them. But it felt as if things took a step back last year, when the final agreement didn’t even mention the phrase “fossil fuels” once. This will be an interesting conversation, especially because cohosts Turkey and Australia have both faced criticism over their relationships with these fuels—Australia is a major exporter of coal and natural gas, and Turkey’s grid relies heavily on fossil fuels, including coal.

Outside the formal negotiations, COP31 president Murat Kurum, Turkey’s environment minister, is spearheading a side agenda, including two informal initiatives that will be worth watching. These wouldn’t be part of the official agreement text, but countries could sign on to signal support.

One is a pledge to make AI more sustainable; this is almost comically squishy, even as voluntary COP pledges go. The text includes explicit wording that it creates no new obligations for countries, so don’t expect anything resembling enforcement there.

The COP leadership is also pushing to make electricity a larger part of member countries’ energy use. Today, only about 23% of global energy is used in the form of electricity. Fossil fuels, like gasoline in vehicles or natural gas for heating, make up the bulk of the rest. Shifting to more electricity use, and relying on cleaner sources for that electricity, could help drive down emissions. The new pledge’s target is for electricity to make up 35% of total energy consumption by 2035.

With leadership billing this as an “implementation COP,” it would be great to see some real, tangible progress on the global challenge of addressing climate change. I’m not expecting anything groundbreaking, but we’ll be tuned in to see what the final agreement shapes up to be.

This article is from The Spark, MIT Technology Review ’s weekly climate newsletter. To receive it in your inbox every Wednesday, sign up here .

articles.title: Teacher certificate bill proposed
articles.excerpt: The Education Bureau has proposed amending the law to enhance the teacher registration mechanism by introducing practising certificate requirements, thereby…
articles.fullText:
The Education Bureau has proposed amending the law to enhance the teacher registration mechanism by introducing practising certificate requirements, thereby upholding the professionalism of the teaching force. The Government will publish the Education (Amendment) Bill 2026 in the Gazette tomorrow and introduce it to the Legislative Council for first and second readings on November 25.

The bureau noted that it has referenced teacher registration systems in various jurisdictions alongside the registration and practising certificate requirements of other Hong Kong professions. It stated that making a practising certificate a prerequisite for teaching, in addition to the existing statutory registration, could elevate public recognition of the sector and raise the social status of teachers.

The bill will establish statutory rules requiring all teachers and principals of publicly funded schools, private schools, international schools and kindergartens to hold both teacher registration and practising certificates. Each practising certificate will remain valid for a maximum of three school years.

To ensure educators keep abreast of the latest global and local educational policies, teachers must meet a mandatory continuing professional development requirement to obtain a practising certificate. This measure aims to align their knowledge and pedagogy with the evolving needs of students and society.

The bureau pointed out that as role models and key figures in nurturing young people, teachers have a profound impact on students through their conduct, values, words and deeds. Amid rapid societal changes, parents and the wider public hold increasingly high expectations for teacher professionalism.

The bureau highlighted that the bill addresses the practical operational needs of schools, encourages educators to keep pace with the times and strengthens staff management to safeguard student well-being. It also establishes safeguards to bar individuals convicted of offences endangering national security from teaching, protecting students while upholding professional integrity and public confidence.

articles.title: 3 sports events get ‘M’ Mark status
articles.excerpt: The Major Sports Events Committee today announced the award of “M” Mark status to three sports events, spanning badminton, basketball…
articles.fullText:
The Major Sports Events Committee today announced the award of “M” Mark status to three sports events, spanning badminton, basketball and squash: the LI-NING Hong Kong Open Badminton Championships 2026, the FIBA 3x3 World Tour Hong Kong 2026, and the Milwaukee Hong Kong Squash Open 2026.

The events are scheduled in quick succession, kicking off with the badminton championships from November 17 to 22. The basketball tournament, part of the HSBC BWF World Tour Super 500, will run from November 28 to 29, and the squash even from November 30 to December 6.

Committee Chairman Wilfred Ng said the Hong Kong Open Badminton Championships will bring many of the world's top badminton players to compete in Hong Kong, while the FIBA 3x3 World Tour Hong Kong will once again attract fans from around the world to watch fast-paced street basketball, and the Hong Kong Squash Open will feature a strong lineup of top-tier players, delivering a thrilling spectator experience.

“These events not only elevate Hong Kong’s international image, but also highlight Hong Kong's outstanding capability in hosting world-class events,” he added.

articles.title: School told to step up values education in vaping case
articles.excerpt: The Education Bureau on Tuesday said it reached out to a secondary school in Tsuen Wan, after a video, purportedly…
articles.fullText:
The Education Bureau on Tuesday said it reached out to a secondary school in Tsuen Wan, after a video, purportedly showing a female student vaping inside a toilet with her schoolmates, went viral online.

The video, which was posted on social media, showed several female students in school uniform taking a selfie inside a cubicle. One of them could be seen holding an e-cigarette.

Po Leung Kuk Yao Ling Sun College later confirmed they were its students. The school said it was "very concerned" about the case, and had already set up meetings with their parents.

"We are committed to nurturing students’ good character, and there are disciplinary and counselling mechanisms to provide students with appropriate support and guidance," a statement read.

Responding to media enquiries, the Education Bureau said it was aware that the school had activated its crisis management mechanism.

It reminded the school to strengthen efforts to cultivate correct values and behaviour among students.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Schools evacuated across Italy after bomb threats
articles.excerpt: Schools were evacuated across Italy on Wednesday following a series of hoax bomb threats, but Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni…
articles.fullText:
Schools were evacuated across Italy on Wednesday following a series of hoax bomb threats, but Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said there was no "concrete danger".

Similar hoax threats were reported in schools in Britain and Ireland, which reportedly prompted some evacuations in Scotland.

Meloni said she had called a government meeting with security and intelligence chiefs for Wednesday to discuss the threats.

Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara said 312 schools had received the threats but urged people not to panic, according to Italian media.

Crowds of evacuated schoolchildren could be seen outside their schools in different parts of the country.

Some said they had to evacuated quickly and left belongings inside that they could not recover before police checks.

"The principal came out into the courtyard and told us that an email had come in, a bomb threat, and right after that the building was evacuated," Sofia De Ponte, a 19-year-old student at Rome's Virgilio high school, said.

De Ponte said the police had still not arrived because "there's a long waiting list with all the schools".

"We're still here waiting," said her fellow pupil Elena Sicignano, 19.

Violetta Uboldi, an art teacher at Brera school in Milan, said children appeared happy at being evacuated.

"I think there was a cry of joy because school was over. That was the reaction," she said.

But Angelica, 16, a student at the school, said she was told by a teacher that it was not a drill "so we panicked a bit".

Italian media reports said the bomb threat was in an email purportedly from a "Mikhail Andropov, leader of the Vilayat of Misoginistan".

"I have just left in your building, inside a plastic bag, a powerful explosive with remote detonation," the email said.

The government sought to play down the incident.

"At present, based on the checks carried out, no element has emerged that would suggest there is a concrete danger," Meloni said in a Facebook post.

"The reports instead appear to be linked to a strategy aimed at generating alarm and concern, which is currently the subject of all the necessary in-depth investigations," Meloni said. (AFP)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Pope Leo wraps up Argentina visit, heads to Peru
articles.excerpt: Pope Leo is wrapping up his visit to Argentina on Wednesday with a final event expected to draw millions, before…
articles.fullText:
Pope Leo is wrapping up his visit to Argentina on Wednesday with a final event expected to draw millions, before continuing on his 12-day South America tour with a visit to Peru in an emotional homecoming for the first Peruvian citizen to lead the Catholic Church.

Leo, on a three-nation tour through November 17, will celebrate an outdoor Mass at the shrine of Our Lady of Lujan, Argentina's most important Catholic devotional site, where throngs of pilgrims have been gathering for days to see him.

Crowds were stretching for miles outside the shrine, about an hour west of Buenos Aires, with people pressing against security barriers and chanting "Leo, Leo, Leo" and waving white-and-yellow Vatican flags as he arrived in an open-air popemobile.

Some in the crowd had walked as far as 10km to arrive, as many streets, including a main highway, remained closed as a security measure.

The pope on Wednesday also visited one of the Argentina's largest penitentiaries, where he hugged several inmates and urged guards to treat detainees humanely, amid a three-day visit to Argentina that has highlighted the Church's criticism of President Javier Milei's cuts to social programmes.

The pope, who has US and Peruvian citizenship, will then begin a personal leg of the most intense overseas trip by a pope in decades, returning to the place he served as a missionary for about 20 years before becoming pope last year.

The Peru visit, expected to include emotional scenes as the pope visits old friends and spends three days in the northern city of Chiclayo, where he was bishop from 2015 to 2023, will also test how directly he is willing to wade into the politics of his adopted nation.

Crowds for Leo's visit to Argentina have been intense, with the pope drawing more than four million people across his visit so far. A Mass in Buenos Aires on Monday was the largest single event yet of his 18-month-papacy, drawing 2.5 million. (Reuters)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: The Download: preserving minds and weighing open AI risks
articles.excerpt: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in…
articles.fullText:
This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

Six wild ideas for perpetuating your mind

As we age, we forget most of what we’ve experienced, yet there’s still undeniable continuity: At 30, or 50, or 70, you will still be you.

To preserve that elusive continuity of self, some far-thinking technologists are exploring ways to keep the brain going, even beyond death. Their ideas range from freezing brains in liquid nitrogen to augmenting living ones and uploading our memories to the cloud.

Here are six possible paths for keeping your mind going, and how feasible they might be .

—Antonio Regalado

This story is from the Impossible edition of our print magazine. Subscribe now to get every issue as soon as it lands.

MIT Technology Review Narrated: Open models have real benefits. Do they outweigh the risks?

Anthropic recently released a report arguing that a powerful new model released by the Chinese company Z.ai, poses a major cyberattack risk. Its core concern was that it is freely available for anyone to download and modify.

The warning was the latest flashpoint in the debate over open frontier AI models. Critics warn that bad actors can misuse them, while supporters argue they prevent a handful of companies from controlling the technology. The debate, however, is more complicated than it seems .

This is our latest story to become an MIT Technology Review Narrated podcast, which we publish each week on Spotify and Apple Podcasts . Just navigate to MIT Technology Review Narrated on either platform, and follow us to get all our new content as it’s released.

The must-reads

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

1 COP31’s flagship pledge to electrify 35% of energy use is sinking
Only around a dozen nations are reportedly ready to sign it. ( Politico )
+ It requires quadrupling the pace of electrification. ( New Scientist $)
+ John Kerry says the US must follow China on clean energy. ( Guardian )
+ But the US skipped the talks entirely for a second year. ( NYT $)
+ What’s the future of electricity? ( MIT Technology Review )

2 The Nvidia spy scandal reportedly involves $7.5 billion of chips
Alice Huang allegedly obtained 240,000 restricted chips. ( Information $)
+ Trump was told of Huang’s spy link on Air Force One . ( NYT $)
+ Experts warn the scandal could erode America’s AI lead. ( Verge )
+ Nvidia’s slide has let Microsoft overtake it in value. ( Reuters $)

3 Studies found AI agents go rogue because they’re “incorrigible”
Their training rewards them for finishing tasks at any cost. ( NYT $)
+ This is why AI agents lie and cheat to reach their goals. ( MIT Technology Review )

4 Anthropic has scaled back its IPO valuation to $1.4 trillion
It aimed for $2 trillion before the recent AI jitters. ( Guardian )

5 Drone strikes have wiped out 3% of Yandex’s cloud customer data
Ukraine hit three of its data centers in October. ( Reuters $)
+ Ukraine’s drones are fighting data centers for fiber. ( Ars Technica )

6 Moderna says its new vaccine could prevent cancer in high-risk people
The company’s CEO calls it the “holy grail” of cancer prevention. ( FT $)
+ Hong Kong is testing a next-gen ultrasound cancer treatment. ( SCMP )

7 Scientists have slowly reversed human cells’ ages by decades
One age marker was set back as far as 60 years. ( Wired $)
+ “Reprogramming” is the buzziest de-aging idea. ( MIT Technology Review )

8 Robot vessels are hunting for mines in the Strait of Hormuz
AI helps them spot mines camouflaged on the seabed. ( BBC )

9 Life may have started inside a tiny bubble
That’s the idea behind the “lipid first” origin theory. ( Quanta )

10 As Voyager 1 reaches a light day from Earth, here’s what it’s taught us
Its discoveries rewrote textbooks in real time. ( New Scientist $)

Quote of the day

“What a dereliction of duty. He’s supposed to protect America, not China, not his friends.”

—Chuck Schumer, the Senate minority leader, accuses President Donald Trump of ignoring warnings about the alleged relationship between Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a Chinese spy.

One more thing

How refrigeration ruined fresh food

Bananas may not be chilled in the grocery store, but they’re the ultimate refrigerated fruit. It’s only thanks to a network of thermal control that they’ve become a global commodity. And that salad bag on the shelf? It’s not just a bag but a highly engineered respiratory apparatus.

According to Nicola Twilley—a contributor to The New Yorker and cohost of the podcast Gastropod—refrigeration has wrecked our food system. Thankfully, there are promising alternative preservation methods.

Read the full story on her research .

—Allison Arieff

We can still have nice things

A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line .)

+ A whisky made like wine is wowing the spirits world.
+ Britain lost in the fog makes for hauntingly beautiful photos .

articles.title: Abby Choi killed by ex-husband, court heard
articles.excerpt: The former brother-in-law of celebrity Abby Choi told the High Court on Wednesday that his brother – her ex-husband –…
articles.fullText:
The former brother-in-law of celebrity Abby Choi told the High Court on Wednesday that his brother – her ex-husband – killed her.

On the 35th day of the trial, Kwong Kong-kit was asked by his counsel who killed Choi.

Kwong, who did not respond at first, said it was his brother after the Deputy High Court Judge Brian Keith said he noted Kwong had nodded, telling him to answer the defence’s question.

Kwong also said he did not know that Choi would be killed or hurt on the day of the incident.

The former brother-in-law told the court that he attended a gathering with Choi and her husband a week prior to the incident, saying it was the last time that he had a meal with Choi.

Kwong Kong-kit, Choi’s ex-husband Kwong Kong-chi, and her former father-in-law Kwong Kau, were charged with murdering Choi on February 21, 2023 at Lung Mei Village in Tai Po, and with preventing the lawful burial of her body.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: 'Climate crisis puts world on path to destruction'
articles.excerpt: United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told world leaders at the COP31 summit in Türkiye on Wednesday that the slow international…
articles.fullText:
United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told world leaders at the COP31 summit in Türkiye on Wednesday that the slow international response to climate change so far had placed the world on a path to destruction.

Governments must fight harder to preserve the planet for future generations, he said, in comments that set the tone for two days of rapid-fire speeches by world leaders at the UN conference on Türkiye's Mediterranean coast.

"The brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us. This is the path to mutually assured destruction," Guterres said, pointing to rising emissions, global temperatures and worsening climate-driven disasters.

"But science is not telling us to surrender. It is telling us to fight harder."

Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are seeking agreement on a plan to increase the share of electricity in global energy use and revive stalled efforts to move away from fossil fuels.

The summit opened on Monday against the backdrop of wars, rampant inflation and other crises that are competing for political attention – but also amid increasingly alarming signals about the pace of global warming.
