A UN report last month found the world on course to break through the 1.5 degrees Celsius warming limit that countries had agreed to pursue under the Paris Agreement to prevent the worst effects of climate change.

Meanwhile, 2026 has also stood out with a series of extreme heatwaves across Western Europe and a glacier collapse in Nepal that triggered a catastrophic flood killing more than 1,450 people, with thousands still missing.

Former French prime minister Laurent Fabius, who presided over the 2015 Paris climate conference and leads an advisory council of former COP presidents, said on Tuesday the leaders' speeches should give political impetus to the negotiations.

"It is an opportunity for leaders to make some announcements, and more this time, to explain how they will implement, because the key word in Antalya is implementation," he told Reuters.

Wednesday's speakers are expected to include Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who was re-elected at the end of October and whose country hosted last year's climate talks.

Vice President Han Zheng, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine will also speak.

The United States, the world's largest historical emitter of greenhouse gases, has skipped the talks for the second year in a row after President Donald Trump – who has called global warming a hoax – withdrew the US from climate cooperation following his return to office in 2025.

Several other nations, including France, Germany, Japan, Italy and Canada, did not send their top leaders to the talks this year and won't be represented in the speeches.

"The world's biggest economies should be leading the response to the climate crisis, not leaving it to others," said Mohamed Adow, director of climate and energy think tank, Power Shift Africa.

COP31 host Türkiye has been pushing for countries to put a goal on electrification at the centre of a final deal, though critics say it may do little to curb warming.

The proposal targets a rise in electricity's share of total global energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035, up from a little over a fifth now, theoretically reducing greenhouse gas emissions from cars, factories and buildings.

But the proposal does not include language requiring new power to be generated by clean energy sources, and governments have yet to clarify a broader plan to transition away from fossil fuels like coal, oil and gas.

Guterres urged countries to speed their transition to clean energy sources.

He said the world’s dependence on fossil fuels was also damaging economies, not just the climate – an apparent nod to surging petroleum prices since the start of the US and Israeli war against Iran that has disrupted Middle East oil exports.

"Three-quarters of humanity live in countries that import fossil fuels, hostage to price shocks they did not create and cannot control," he said.

"Recent conflicts make clear that this is a recipe for chronic insecurity and a cost-of-living meltdown." (Reuters)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Mainland stocks edge higher, HK shares end down
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong's stock market ended lower on Wednesday, with the Hang Seng Index down 0.98 percent to close at 24,315…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong's stock market ended lower on Wednesday, with the Hang Seng Index down 0.98 percent to close at 24,315 points.

The Hang Seng China Enterprises Index dropped 1.14 percent to 8,171, and the Hang Seng Tech Index slid 1.41 percent.

On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index reversed earlier losses and closed up 0.5 percent while the blue-chip CSI300 index added 0.4 percent.

The Shenzhen Component Index closed 1.32 percent higher.

Tech shares led the gains.

The start-up board ChiNext Composite index rose 3.1 percent and Shanghai's tech-focused STAR50 index climbed 2.8 percent.

Around the region, equity markets were stuck in a narrow range with traders caught between rate hike expectations and oil-market tensions.

A hotter-than-expected consumer inflation reading in the US and hawkish policymakers drove up bets of a quicker pace of rate hikes.

"The resulting rise in global bond yields and strengthening dollar put pressure on A-share valuations," analysts at Nanhua Futures said in a note.

"This round of recent market recovery has been driven mainly by domestic measures to support markets and a temporary easing of overseas uncertainties.

"However, both the strength and durability of these factors appear limited. While market sentiment has improved somewhat, investors remain broadly cautious, and stock indexes are expected to trade in a range in the near term."

Elsewhere, oil prices rose on Wednesday after falling to two-month lows in the previous session, as the market swung between hopes of de-escalation in the Iran war and concerns over continued attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. (Xinhua/Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK ranks 11th in digital and AI competitiveness
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong is 11th in the world and fourth in Asia for digital and artificial intelligence competitiveness, according to a…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong is 11th in the world and fourth in Asia for digital and artificial intelligence competitiveness, according to a ranking unveiled on Wednesday.

The International Institute for Management Development's World Digital and AI Ranking 2026 covered 70 economies.

Hong Kong ranked second for workforce development, fifth for efficiency and 10th for technology and infrastructure.

It came first worldwide in technological framework, practices, and education and training at the sub-factor levels.

The government said the result recognised Hong Kong as one of the world's most competitive economies in digital and AI development.

"Following the directions set out in the First Five-Year Plan for Economic and Social Development of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government is fully committed to developing Hong Kong into an international I&T centre," a spokesman said in a statement.

"Among other things, Hong Kong will enhance the institutional framework for I&T development, expedite the alignment with key national strategies in technology, and develop the new 'three major I&T parks and five key research and development (R&D) institutions' paradigm."

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Hong Kong opens international police academy
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong has opened a new international police academy aimed at strengthening cross-border law enforcement cooperation and training local and…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong has opened a new international police academy aimed at strengthening cross-border law enforcement cooperation and training local and overseas officers, according to Chief Executive John Lee.

Speaking on Wednesday at the inauguration ceremony of the Hong Kong International Academy of Policing, Lee said professionalism and operational excellence had helped make the city one of the world’s safest.

He said the academy marked a new phase in which the force would build on its local strengths to expand international collaboration in leadership development and training.

"The academy will deepen international police exchanges. It will do so through training programmes, police leadership forums and other outreach initiatives. The target is to train some 1,000 officers each year, including about 200 overseas law enforcement personnel," he said.

"Training is the academy's core function, but its significance goes further. By bringing law enforcement leaders together, it will strengthen Hong Kong's international partnerships.

"Stronger partnerships will, in turn, reinforce Hong Kong's role as a 'super connector' and 'super value-adder' — a place that links people and expertise across jurisdictions."

Lee said security challenges are increasingly complex and borderless, citing cybercrime, financial fraud and terrorism as clear examples.

"No jurisdiction can stand alone. Strong international connectivity is therefore vital to global security and prosperity," Lee said.

The academy, he said, is intended to improve cooperation in three areas: infrastructure and operational networks; rules, mechanisms and procedural standards; and people-to-people ties that build lasting trust with partner jurisdictions.

It has set an ambitious schedule, with more than 20 major international training programmes and forums planned by the end of next year.

They include ConvergeHK, a new senior leadership policing forum on shared security challenges, which is expected to draw police leaders from Asean, Belt and Road and Middle East countries next April.

Lee said he was confident the academy would become a hub for international exchange and a strategic investment in shared security, attracting law enforcement agencies from around the world to work towards a safer future.

The Hong Kong International Academy of Policing will share premises with the Hong Kong Police College currently located in Wong Chuk Hang.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Spotlight on tech innovation as SZ gears up for Apec
articles.excerpt: Shenzhen is promoting its high-tech sector to showcase the nation’s ambitions in innovation and global competitiveness as the city prepares…
articles.fullText:
Shenzhen is promoting its high-tech sector to showcase the nation’s ambitions in innovation and global competitiveness as the city prepares to host Apec.

The city has designated four foundational economic pillars, with the high-tech industry serving as Shenzhen’s primary economic engine and growth driver.

According to municipal government data, the added value of Shenzhen’s strategic emerging industries reached 1.67 trillion yuan last year, accounting for 43 percent of the city’s GDP.

Shenzhen is also home to more than 25,000 high-tech enterprises, ranking among the highest in the country.

Peter Ruan, founder of Shenzhen smart-glasses company GetD, said Chinese products are among the world’s most advanced technically and offer strong value for money.

He added that development is booming because Shenzhen has a complete industrial chain and its research and development staff are diligent and efficient.

Ruan hopes to use Apec as an opportunity to spotlight the "speed of Shenzhen" in the tech field to the world.

"In developing these glasses, we often work through the night, until late. To produce our newest model of glasses, we worked until seven in the morning," he said.

"This is the Shenzhen spirit. The can-do spirit. This Apec summit is a very important meeting for Shenzhen. I hope the international community can see Shenzhen’s development and speed."

Meanwhile, semiconductor company SLKOR said the city has a sound industrial ecosystem and is not afraid of international competition.

The company was founded about 10 years ago in Huaqiangbei, a major electronics commercial district in Shenzhen.

CEO Song Shiqiang said his firm's products can already be exported overseas, and sales are expected to exceed 100 million yuan this year.

He also said that Huaqiangbei, known as "China’s No. 1 Electronics Street", has transformed in recent years, and shed its image as a marketplace for copycats and knockoffs.

"Huaqiangbei has now developed into China’s Huaqiangbei, even the world’s Huaqiangbei. Its industrial chain can cover upstream and downstream, and its ecosystem is developing well," he said.

"According to statistics from the Huaqiangbei Subdistrict Office, Huaqiangbei has now completely shed its copycat image and it has its own capacity for independent innovation."

According to Shenzhen authorities, the Huaqiangbei commercial area draws average daily foot traffic of 750,000, which includes about 8,000 foreign visitors.

Bilingual Chinese and English signage has been installed around commercial areas ahead of Apec to accommodate visitors.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Five plead not guilty in renovation-bribery trial
articles.excerpt: The District Court on Wednesday heard that five men allegedly conspired to offer bribes in a bid to secure a…
articles.fullText:
The District Court on Wednesday heard that five men allegedly conspired to offer bribes in a bid to secure a major renovation project of a residential building in Kwun Tong.

The five defendants, charged with conspiracy to offer advantages to an agent between September 2022 and January 2023, all pleaded not guilty.

In the opening submissions, the prosecution said three of the defendants – Chong Chun-to, Lam Suet-pin and To Hon-sum – were believed to be key members of a syndicate.

The other two are then chairman of the owners' corporation of Hing Tat Mansion, Cheung Kin-wah, and then member Zhan Qingbo.

The prosecution alleged that Chong, Lam and To sought to offer bribes worth HK$2 million to Cheung, Zhan and other members of the owners' corporation in trying to win the HK$20 million contract.

In exchange, the chairman and member of the owners' corporation were asked to use their positions to have designated firms appointed as the building’s property management company and building works consultant – crucial steps in securing the contract.

The court also heard Chong, Lam and To asked Cheung and Zhan to praise companies linked to them within the owners’ corporation while belittling other contractors that offered lower prices.

The prosecution said the defendants had carefully planned to manipulate the tender process.

It said corruption and big-rigging activities in building renovation works would not only harm homeowners’ interests but also pose a threat to public safety.

The trial continues on Thursday.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Lawmakers support NM bill as second reading resumes
articles.excerpt: Lawmakers have voiced their support for a bill that aims to fast track the development of the Northern Metropolis, as…
articles.fullText:
Lawmakers have voiced their support for a bill that aims to fast track the development of the Northern Metropolis, as the second reading for the dedicated legislation resumed on Wednesday.

Andrew Lam from the Election Committee noted that society had a strong consensus towards accelerating the mega project development in terms of speed, quality and efficiency.

“The government, with the determination to break the shackles of the traditional systems, through special handling and the mindset of removing barriers and easing restrictions, established a brand new legal framework for the Northern Metropolis’ land development, infrastructure works, noise regulation, as well as cross-boundary flow of elements," he said.

The DAB’s Yiu Ming suggested the government step up the public’s right to know and oversight by reporting to lawmakers of the latest developments more frequently.

“I think that the government, after the legislation is implemented, should regularly publish quantitative indicators, such as the average handling time for different types of projects," he said.

"At the same time, as the scale of the Northern Metropolis is enormous and involves large-scale land disposal, I suggest the government increase the frequency of reporting to the Legislative Council from once per year to once every six months.”

Tam Chun-kwok said the mega hub served as the new engine of the city’s future development, carrying important functions such as innovation and technology industries, higher education, modern logistics and high-quality living environment.

The project would be the main platform for the integrated development of education, technology and talent, he said, as well as for the SAR to integrate into and serve the nation's development.

The Bills Committee finished scrutinising the legislation in 12 meetings that took nearly 30 hours before the bill was tabled for the second reading debate.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK urged to chase long-term 'patient capital'
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong should go after money that stays put, not cash that flees at the first wobble, the Financial Services…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong should go after money that stays put, not cash that flees at the first wobble, the Financial Services Development Council said on Wednesday, in a push to tighten the city's hold as Asia's wealth-management hub.

The council has set out ways in a new report to attract this “patient capital” from pension funds and insurers at home, on the mainland and overseas.

The council's Vice-Chairman, Ding Chen, said the report aims to turn Hong Kong into a long-term capital hub.

"The central objective of this report is to make Hong Kong not only a place where capital is raised, and traded, but also place where capital is managed, invested, and reinvested over a longer period of time," she said.

The report says there should be more products investors can buy, including bonds and a wider range of stocks, with tighter risk controls.

It also calls for more cross-border channels, especially for pensions and insurance.

Rocky Tung, the council's executive director, said this stickier money could be "the stabilising force" amid market swings, which supports new financial products and backs growth that lasts.

"There is a lot of investment coming in and out of a market or an economy, and they are here only for the short run," he said.

"And with that in mind, if there is anything less than ideal, they would pull the money out of the market and subsequently the economy. So that will create a lot of turbulence and it will exaggerate the economic cycle.

"With patient capital, they have the mindset of a long-term vision, they are going to be the stabilising force."

The report noted that mainland insurers held 41.3 trillion yuan in assets at the end of last year, but only 5.4 percent of that is invested outside the mainland — well below the 15 percent they are allowed.

Mainland pension savings stood at 15.66 trillion yuan in 2024.

The report said that as populations age, demand for more diversified cross-border investment and a better match between assets and long-term liabilities would bring unprecedented growth opportunities for Hong Kong's patient capital.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Bus hits dozens of vehicles near Seoul
articles.excerpt: A commuter bus struck more than 30 vehicles stopped at a traffic light during the morning rush hour on Wednesday…
articles.fullText:
A commuter bus struck more than 30 vehicles stopped at a traffic light during the morning rush hour on Wednesday in Seongnam, just south of Seoul, injuring dozens of people, fire officials in South Korea said.

At least 57 people were being treated for injuries, including nine who were seriously hurt, although none were in life-threatening condition, according to the fire department of Gyeonggi Province, which governs Seongnam.

The bus collided with 32 vehicles before slamming into a median strip, fire officials said.

Photos from the scene showed the bus perched on a median strip with a shattered windshield and other damaged cars.

Police were questioning the bus driver, who tested negative in a breathalyser test and told investigators that the brakes had failed, according to Park Chang-gon, an official from Seongnam’s Bundang district police station. (AP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: 'One Stanley steel work different from approved plans'
articles.excerpt: Development minister Bernadette Linn said on Wednesday that the Buildings Department has found that steel reinforcement work at a house…
articles.fullText:
Development minister Bernadette Linn said on Wednesday that the Buildings Department has found that steel reinforcement work at a house in a luxury residential development in Stanley did not match the approved plans.

The investigation was carried out after the residence at One Stanley was alleged to be built with fewer steel bars than approved.

“The Buildings Department has largely completed its investigation, and found that some wire mesh and steel configurations were inconsistent with the approved plans,” Linn said during a Legco meeting.

“The discrepancies were never reported to the authorities.”

She said the department will consult the Department of Justice on possible prosecution.

Linn also said checks would be carried out elsewhere at the luxury development.

“The Buildings Department has ordered random inspections for 15 other houses and 12 units at six residential blocks in the same housing estate, requiring the developer to appoint independent, accredited laboratories, and under the supervision of authorities, to carry out relevant tests.”

She said enforcement actions will be taken if violations are found.

In light of the case at One Stanley, the secretary for development said contractors will have to take photos or videos of steel reinforcement work prior to concrete pouring at projects, and submit the record to the authorities.

She expects relevant measures to be implemented in phases by January, adding that discussions with the industry are currently under way.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Govt staff to get 12 hours of family care leave
articles.excerpt: Government employees will be able to leave work for a few hours at a time to look after family, under…
articles.fullText:
Government employees will be able to leave work for a few hours at a time to look after family, under a new leave arrangement of up to 12 hours a year expected to start in January.

Staff can use it to take a relative to a medical appointment, care for someone who is ill, attend a child's school activity, or deal with a sudden matter at home.

In a paper submitted to a Legislative Council panel, the government said the leave would be taken in blocks of one to four hours, and unused hours cannot be carried over.

In most cases, staff would only need to file a form with a reason beforehand, with no supporting documents required.

If something crops up suddenly, they can get verbal approval first and submit the form afterwards.

Approving officers could still ask for proof if they suspect abuse.

The scheme was announced in this year's Policy Address and would be the fourth type of family-related leave for government employees.

The Civil Service Bureau is still settling the details and will consult staff sides before it is rolled out.

Since April 2024, more than 7,500 marriage-leave and 23,000 compassionate-leave applications have been approved.

About 15,600 parental-leave applications have been approved since that leave began in April last year.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: 'New light festivals must boost night economy'
articles.excerpt: Tourism representatives have welcomed the replacement of the city’s decades-old multimedia light show, but say the new light festivals taking…
articles.fullText:
Tourism representatives have welcomed the replacement of the city’s decades-old multimedia light show, but say the new light festivals taking its place must deliver a genuine boost to the night economy.

A Symphony of Lights, a nightly fixture over Victoria Harbour for 22 years, will hold its final performance next Wednesday.

It will be replaced by light festivals staged at various locations at different times of the year.

Speaking on an RTHK radio programme on Wednesday, Sara Leung, a consultant with the Federation of Hong Kong Trade Unions in Tourism, said the long-running show may have grown stale for some residents and visitors.

She said change could be positive, noting that the tourism ecosystem is constantly evolving.

"I think the new show is a good concept because it will be hosted in different districts, which lets visitors get to know Hong Kong better," she said.

"But the most important thing is that whatever fireworks show or event you organise, it can drive business for the local districts and shops. I think that is the most meaningful thing."

Leung added the harbour itself was a draw for visitors and suggested authorities consider incorporating more local elements, such as restoring retired fishing boats, to give it a new character.

Meanwhile, lawmaker Perry Yiu, who previously represented the tourism functional constituency, said the show had helped draw attention to Victoria Harbour over the years, but a major overhaul would be costly and logistically difficult because it would involve dozens of buildings.

He said different offerings, such as fireworks and drone shows, could help make the harbour’s night scene unique and in turn boost catering, retail and the economy.

"The most important thing is to spend little and get good results, have sustainability, be more distinctive, and incorporate different festivals and seasons with different themes, so people feel fresh each time. That is most important," he said.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: 'Northern Link savings won't compromise quality'
articles.excerpt: The Northern Link’s lower cost estimate will not come at the expense of construction quality or safety, according to the…
articles.fullText:
The Northern Link’s lower cost estimate will not come at the expense of construction quality or safety, according to the Commissioner for Northern Metropolis Railways Raymond Ip.

The government and the MTR on Tuesday signed the full Northern Link project agreement, and the Executive Council approved the financial arrangements for the second part of the plan.

With both the main line and spur line now in construction, the project is estimated at HK$86.2 billion – 28 percent below the original forecast – and is set to launch by 2034.

Speaking on an RTHK radio programme on Wednesday, Ip said the lower price tag came from changes to design, approval and construction methods.

He said merging the main line and spur line into one project produced a "double reduction" effect: the spur line’s construction period was brought forward by two years, and overall costs fell by 28 percent.

Ip also spoke about what he described as a well-established monitoring mechanism.

"For example, over the past few years, we have optimised the project monitoring and communication platform. Between us and MTR Corporation, we have also strengthened monitoring and auditing," he said.

"In addition, there are proactive reporting and early warning mechanisms. Furthermore, before commissioning, the relevant departments will also carry out what we call safe and sound testing and acceptance procedures."

Ip added that a one-stop Railway Checking Unit and an electronic central approval platform cut the approval time of construction plans by 30 to 50 percent, while the Northern Metropolis Development Bill would further simplify procedures such as construction noise permit applications.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Pope warns against worship of money and popularity
articles.excerpt: Pope Leo drew a crowd of about a million on Tuesday for the third strong turnout of his 12-day South…
articles.fullText:
Pope Leo drew a crowd of about a million on Tuesday for the third strong turnout of his 12-day South America tour, as he urged young people at a nighttime vigil in Argentina not to be consumed by the pursuit of money or social media popularity.

Throngs stretched for miles down the Avenida del Libertador, one of Buenos Aires' main boulevards.

Many waved cell phones, screens shining in the darkness, as Leo was driven slowly through the crowd in an open-air popemobile.

Chants of "This is the pope's youth!" rang out as the vehicle stopped frequently so security officials could bring forward babies for Leo to bless.

In a speech, the pope warned young people against worship of modern-day "idols" such as success or physical appearance, and lamented that some youth "go so far as to lie, betray or humiliate someone on social media".

"Do not bow down before anything that cannot give you life," he said.

Leo, on an ambitious three-country tour through November 17, led the vigil after returning from a day trip to Cordoba, Argentina's second city, where he drew 650,000 people to an outdoor Mass earlier on Tuesday.

The pope led a Mass on Monday at the Avenida del Libertador that drew 2.5 million people, in the largest event of his 18-month-old papacy.

Leo is the first pope to visit Catholic-majority Argentina since 1987.

The pope, who is also visiting Uruguay and Peru on the tour, is seeking to reinforce a region that has long been a Catholic stronghold but where the Church has been losing ground to fast-growing evangelical denominations.

Leo has emerged as a forceful voice on the world stage, lamenting what he sees as a failure of global leadership.

In Argentina, he has directly challenged President Javier Milei, a libertarian and close ally of US President Donald Trump.

On Sunday, Leo urged Milei, who has pushed an austerity agenda, not to target Argentina's poorest.

Milei has said spending cuts were necessary to bring inflation under control.

Valentin Gomez, 21, a student attending the Mass in Cordoba, praised Leo's focus on those in need.

"In these difficult times we are living through, he is greatly needed," Gomez said.

"Someone who is truly concerned about the poor."

Argentine Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno said Cordoba was chosen as a stop on the pope's tour because of its location in the centre of Argentina, allowing pilgrims to travel easily from neighbouring provinces. (Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK, mainland stocks open lower
articles.excerpt: Global bonds tumbled and the greenback stayed firm after a hot US inflation print and hawkish central bank rhetoric raised…
articles.fullText:
Global bonds tumbled and the greenback stayed firm after a hot US inflation print and hawkish central bank rhetoric raised the risk of an outsized half-point rate hike from the Federal Reserve next month.

Hong Kong and mainland stocks, meanwhile, opened lower on Wednesday.

The Hang Seng Index was down 202 points, or 0.83 percent, at 24,354.

On the mainland, the benchmark Shanghai Composite Index opened 0.22 percent lower at 3,655 whereas the Shenzhen Component Index fell 0.32 percent at 11,205.

In Japan, the Nikkei share gauge climbed for a third straight session as data and earnings reports restored some optimism to the battered AI sector. The benchmark Nikkei 225 advanced 0.8 percent to 60,942 as of the midday break.

The Kospi in Seoul rose 0.4 percent during morning trade. (Reuters/Xinhua)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Chelsea held in Women's Champions League, City win
articles.excerpt: Chelsea were held to a goalless stalemate by Hacken in the Women's Champions League on Tuesday, while Manchester City earned…
articles.fullText:
Chelsea were held to a goalless stalemate by Hacken in the Women's Champions League on Tuesday, while Manchester City earned a first win of the competition.

The London club hit the woodwork twice in Sweden as an inspired showing by Hacken goalkeeper Jennifer Falk also helped keep the visitors at bay.

Chelsea are third in the league phase table after four matches, one point behind defending champions and pacesetters Barcelona, although the perfect Catalans hold a game in hand.

However, several teams, including Lyon and Arsenal – both of whom are just a point behind Sonia Bompastor's side – could leapfrog them this matchday.

"It's a frustrating result," Blues boss Bompastor told Uefa.

"We came here with the ambition of winning the game... But tonight it didn't go that way. We need to learn from this."

Women's Super League champions Man City enjoyed a 4-1 success at Inter Milan to earn a first win in the league phase after drawing their first three outings.

A first-half Aoba Fujino brace cancelled out Elisa Bartoli's opener for the hosts by half-time.

Kerstin Casparij and Grace Clinton were on target after the break to send City up to seventh in the table.

Paris Saint-Germain fell to a first defeat as Bayern Munich held on to win 2-1 at the Parc des Princes and climb to second in the table, ahead of Chelsea on goal difference.

Klara Buehl's strike five minutes from half-time proved the winner as she added to PSG goalkeeper Katarzyna Kiedrzynek's early own goal to put the Bavarians in a comfortable position.

Paulina Dudek halved the deficit from the spot midway through the second period but Bayern held on.

PSG lie in ninth place on five points.

In the Spanish capital, Real Madrid downed visitors Paris FC 3-0 thanks to three second-half strikes.

A first win of the league phase sent Pau Quesada's side eighth in the table on six points, while Paris FC lounge 16th on two points.

Arianna Caruso broke the deadlock in the 55th minute and Lineth Beerensteyn thumped home soon after.

Linda Caicedo made the points safe with nine minutes remaining as she finished smartly from Felicia Schroeder's reverse pass.

"It was really important to pick up the three points today because we hadn't won any of our first three games," Caruso said. "We have to try to finish among the top teams."

Roma held on to beat Swiss side Servette 2-1. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Thune, Jordan emerge as Republican minority leaders
articles.excerpt: Republicans chose US Senate Majority Leader John Thune and House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan on Tuesday to lead them…
articles.fullText:
Republicans chose US Senate Majority Leader John Thune and House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan on Tuesday to lead them against a Democratic-controlled Congress that will take power in January for the final two years of Donald Trump's presidency.

A week after Republicans lost their majority in a stinging midterm election defeat, Senate Republicans chose Thune by acclamation at a closed-door meeting for the task of trying to thwart Democratic initiatives that do not meet with their approval, including by wielding the Senate filibuster.

"We're not going to be running this place next year," Thune told reporters. "But you can be assured we will be very, very active in asserting conservative priorities in all of the legislating... that goes on here."

Jordan's election as House minority leader elevates a combative Trump ally to the forefront of the party’s fight to defend the US president’s agenda in the lower chamber. Jordan defeated House Majority Leader Steve Scalise in a secret ballot. House Speaker Mike Johnson opted not to stand for the leadership position.

The House and Senate leadership elections will help to determine what role Republicans intend to play as the minority party in Congress during the final two years of Trump's presidency.

Democrats will need Republican support to move major initiatives in the 100-member Senate, where the filibuster rule requires 60 votes for most legislation. Their majorities in both chambers also fall well short of the two-thirds of votes needed to override presidential vetoes.

Thune, 65, a South Dakota Republican known for his consensus-building leadership style, is respected by Republicans and Democrats alike. But he has run afoul of Trump's MAGA supporters who say he did not move aggressively enough to enact Trump's policies on immigration and election reform.

After the midterm elections, Thune vowed that Republicans would work with Trump to block "Democrat extremism" and work against any attempt by Democrats to unwind Republican achievements, including border security and judicial appointments.

Jordan, 62, was first elected in 2006 to represent a deeply conservative rural district in northern Ohio and was a founder of the House Freedom Caucus, a group that former Republican House Speaker John Boehner labelled "legislative terrorists."

Before entering politics, Jordan honed his pugilistic style during a career as a high school and university champion wrestler, and later as a wrestling coach at Ohio State University. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Rubio sees 'no need' to attack Iran as talks rumble on
articles.excerpt: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday said he saw no need to resume major combat operations against Iran…
articles.fullText:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday said he saw no need to resume major combat operations against Iran because economic sanctions and other restrictions were working so effectively.

"The economic campaign (against Iran) is so devastating that right now there is no need for major combat operations," Rubio said after a meeting of G7 foreign ministers in Paris. "That's what I told our allies here today."

US President Donald Trump "has concluded that for the time being there is no need for major combat operations because we are achieving the same objective by economic means," Rubio said.

But if Iran were to cross "red lines" then the "US military stands ready," said Rubio, warning of a "terrible price" for Tehran.

European members of the G7 had pressed Rubio at the meeting of foreign ministers of the group in Paris to avoid any new escalation against Iran.

In a surprise move, Qatar's Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani joined talks on the G7 sidelines with four European top diplomats and the Saudi foreign minister hours after meeting Trump to discuss ending Washington's war with Iran, Paris said.

Trump had said after meeting Al Thani – a key mediator who is also Qatar's foreign minister – that there was momentum towards ending the war, which erupted on February 28 with the killing of supreme leader Ali Khamenei.

"The economic pain that is being inflicted on Iran right now and on that regime is extraordinary and it is growing every day," said Rubio, saying Iranian oil supplies were drying up due to US blockades.

"This radical regime of lunatics is imposing this on their own people," he said, referring to the Islamic republic's clerical leadership.

But Rubio also appeared downbeat about the prospects of a deal with Tehran, saying Iran currently did not appear realistic about negotiations.

"Iran would love a deal. The problem is, the conditions they continue to place are absurd. They're not even serious. But that could change," he said.

But he added: "Eventually, you have to eat, you have pay your own fighters, your own security forces. I think as time goes on that will have an impact... Eventually economic realities penetrate the skull of the most radical lunatic."

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot, who chaired the meeting in Paris, warned that the risk of a new escalation between the United States and Iran "has not been completely ruled out."

"Otherwise, we would not have devoted so much time and energy over the past two days to addressing these issues" with Rubio and the Qatari premier, Barrot said.

British foreign minister Ed Miliband urged an "all-out diplomatic effort" to end the conflict, warning a stalemate of "no war, no peace" was causing economic damage.

"The status quo is bad economically for us and it's not a stable equilibrium," said Miliband, urging a full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz energy transit hub. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: US Republicans derail bid to impeach Hegseth
articles.excerpt: Republicans in the US House of Representatives on Tuesday blocked an effort to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth over the…
articles.fullText:
Republicans in the US House of Representatives on Tuesday blocked an effort to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war, handing US President Donald Trump a victory days after his party's crushing midterm election defeat.

The House voted 211 to 204 to send the impeachment resolution to the Judiciary Committee, effectively derailing a planned vote on Wednesday on whether to bring formal charges against the embattled Pentagon chief.

The resolution was introduced by Republican Thomas Massie, a Trump critic who was the only member of his party to oppose the procedural manoeuvre, according to US media.

The impeachment drive had threatened to deepen Trump's troubles after Democrats swept last week's midterms, with anger at the sputtering Iran war and soaring fuel prices helping drive voters to a historic rejection of Republicans.

Republicans still hold a narrow House majority until January, when Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress. And 11 Democrats missed the vote.

Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell, in a post on X, hailed the vote as a "TOTAL VICTORY!"

"We look forward to ending this sham impeachment in the committee room, where facts will continue to prevail and this distraction can be put to rest."

Hegseth earlier on Tuesday dismissed the impeachment effort as a "farce" and defended his record leading the Iran war and other military operations under Trump.

"It's a farce, and it's a stunt, and everybody knows it," he said at a Pentagon press conference, branding the accusations "slander" and "sabotage."

Moments after Hegseth's televised appearance, Trump signalled his support.

"Pete Hegseth gets an 'A' PLUS, PLUS, PLUS," the 80-year-old president wrote on his Truth Social platform.

Vice President JD Vance also backed the defence secretary, saying he had "obviously not" committed impeachable offences.

Massie's eight articles of impeachment accused Hegseth of illegally waging war without congressional authorisation and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief.

Several related to the eight-month Iran war, accusing him of violating the War Powers Resolution, which places limits on US military interventions without congressional authorisation.

Other allegations involved the 2025 conflict with Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis and strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific, which Massie branded "extrajudicial killings."

He also accused Hegseth of suppressing free speech by trying to punish Democratic Senator Mark Kelly over a video urging military and intelligence personnel to refuse illegal orders.

Hegseth defended the operations in Yemen, Iran, Venezuela and against alleged drug smugglers, while seeking to equate the impeachment effort with an attack on US troops.

"I stand behind every one of these operations. I was proud to execute them, and I would do it again tomorrow," he said.

The decision to send the resolution to committee halts the immediate impeachment drive but does not prevent Democrats from reviving the effort after taking control of Congress in January.

Massie, who lost his Republican primary to a Trump-backed challenger, will leave Congress at the end of his term. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Iran rejects France cyberattack allegations
articles.excerpt: Iran on Tuesday said French accusations that it was responsible for cyberattacks on supermarket fridges last month were "baseless". "Iran's…
articles.fullText:
Iran on Tuesday said French accusations that it was responsible for cyberattacks on supermarket fridges last month were "baseless".

"Iran's foreign ministry categorically rejects the French government's baseless and one-sided accusations against Iran regarding alleged cyber activities in France," the ministry said in a statement.

It added that it "strongly condemns this hackneyed policy of levelling accusations against the Islamic republic".

Hundreds of French supermarkets were hit in the October 11 and 12 cyberattacks, which raised the temperatures in their refrigerators and freezers, forcing many to throw away entire inventories of perishable food.

Similar incidents were then reported in at least 11 other European countries in early November.

Along with summoning Iran's ambassador and seeking European-level sanctions, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said on Tuesday that Paris would "rule nothing out and will take all measures – including those we may not disclose publicly – that we deem proportionate and necessary to deter any further attacks".

Tehran meanwhile said it would "not hesitate to take necessary and appropriate measures to safeguard its national interests and security in the face of unlawful foreign activities".

It added that France "is merely projecting its own governance failures" with these accusations.

Later in the day, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi blamed the French government for the incident.

"Unable to manage fridges let alone addressing grievances of its people, French government is shifting blame for its failures onto others," the top diplomat said on X.

Also on Tuesday, the European Union said it would look to provide a "swift and united response" pending discussion with member states after France's announcement. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Bulgaria motorway pileup kills 11, injures dozens
articles.excerpt: Eleven people died and dozens were injured on Tuesday in a mass pileup in thick fog on a motorway in…
articles.fullText:
Eleven people died and dozens were injured on Tuesday in a mass pileup in thick fog on a motorway in southeastern Bulgaria, whose roads rank as the most dangerous in the EU.

Crashes snared around 50 cars and trucks heading in both directions of the highway linking the capital Sofia to the Black Sea city of Burgas, regional governor Georgi Chalakov told the BTA state news agency.

Images showed overturned and smashed cars and trucks mangled together, as well as burnt-out vehicles, at the scene of the accident near the city of Yambol.

Interior Minister Ivan Demerdzhiev said in a statement that a sudden change in weather conditions was the main reason for the pileup.

Visibility was around 70-80 metres immediately before the incident, but dropped to approximately 10 metres within a short period, according to information available to the ministry.

"We are actively working on equipping the toll system gantries with display screens to warn drivers," he said.

The motorway section should have been closed early on Tuesday, Bogdan Milchev, chairman of the Road Safety Institute NGO, told public radio station BNR, blaming the government.

Ten people died at the scene, while another person died after being admitted to hospital, the health ministry said in a statement, revising an earlier statement that had said 11 people died at the scene.

In total, 51 people were admitted to hospitals in nearby cities, with 13 of them critically injured, it added.

The government dispatched two aircraft equipped with stretchers and medical teams, as government officials rushed to the scene, while Prime Minister Rumen Radev cancelled his appointments for later on Tuesday.

The government wants Wednesday to be a day of national mourning, while President Iliana Iotova, rushing back from abroad, also expressed her condolences.

Bulgaria saw 71 road fatalities per million inhabitants in 2025, the highest rate in the European Union, according to European Commission figures.

Victims blame the Balkan nation's high number of traffic deaths on reckless driving, poorly maintained roads and an inefficient justice system.

Romanian Foreign Minister Dan Neculaescu said one Romanian was among the injured and expressed "deepest condolences" to the victims and their families in a post on X.

European Council chief Antonio Costa also said on X he was "deeply saddened to learn of the tragic traffic accident in Bulgaria this morning." (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Anthropic targets valuation of up to US$1.4 trillion
articles.excerpt: Anthropic plans to raise up to US$64 billion in its upcoming initial public offering, the artificial intelligence giant said in…
articles.fullText:
Anthropic plans to raise up to US$64 billion in its upcoming initial public offering, the artificial intelligence giant said in a filing on Tuesday, putting the company's total valuation at up to US$1.4 trillion.

The maker of AI agent Claude said in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission that it aims to sell 825 million shares of Class A common stock at a Wall Street debut price estimate of "between US$70.00 and US$78.00" per share, amounting to US$64.3 billion.

Anthropic had been expected to raise up to US$100 billion in its IPO, which would have made it the largest IPO on record.

The stock market debut is being seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last.

And it comes as Wall Street is busy digesting the impact of the US midterm elections, in which Democrats won majority control of both chambers of Congress and are vowing to put the brakes on US President Donald Trump's agenda.

Anthropic has been aiming to hold its initial public offering the week of November 16.

On Monday the company announced it would release updated versions of two of its most powerful AI models, Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, which it said can perform 30 percent faster than previous versions.

Growth has been staggering at the company. Anthropic's revenue reached US$17 billion in the third quarter, up from just US$1.4 billion a year earlier, a securities filing showed earlier this month.

On Tuesday, the company said its annualised projection, known as the run-rate revenue, "was approximately US$81 billion as of October 31, 2026, up US$10 billion from September 30."

Estimates in recent months had forecast Anthropic's valuation at up to a staggering US$2 trillion, but the estimates have slipped along with a slide in AI stock prices on Wall Street.

Several US media outlets including The Wall Street Journal and The New York Times on Tuesday estimated the valuation of the company at between US$1.3 trillion and US$1.4 trillion. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: US stocks fall on hot inflation report
articles.excerpt: US stocks closed lower on Tuesday, as a hotter-than-expected inflation reading hardened expectations for a rate hike from the Federal…
articles.fullText:
US stocks closed lower on Tuesday, as a hotter-than-expected inflation reading hardened expectations for a rate hike from the Federal Reserve next month and fuelled concerns the US central bank may be more aggressive in raising rates.

The US Labour Department said the Consumer Price Index increased 0.4 percent last month, its third straight gain of 0.4 percent or more and above the 0.3 percent estimate of economists polled by Reuters, after advancing 0.6 percent in September.

The data came after Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the central bank should raise short-term borrowing costs in December even if data showed inflation cooled last month, and should consider an upsized half-point rate hike if the inflation picture worsens.

Markets are now completely pricing in a rate hike of at least 25 basis points at the Fed's December meeting, according to CME FedWatch, up from 84 percent on Monday, while expectations for a 50 basis point increase climbed to 11.8 percent after garnering no consideration at all in the prior session.

The 2-year US Treasury yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Fed, surged nearly 18.9 basis points to 4.736 percent and was poised for its biggest daily gain since April 9, 2025, after US President Donald Trump launched sweeping global tariffs.

The jump in yields has come even as oil prices have eased to two-month lows as US officials have downplayed any imminent military actions against Iran.

"What kind of has the market spooked a little bit is this idea of, 'Well, we were already pricing in a December hike... but maybe it's not 25, maybe it's 50, and maybe the Fed's more worried about inflation than I am, so let's sell some stocks,'" said Jason Ware, chief investment officer at Albion Financial Group in Salt Lake City, Utah.

"From our perch, that is irrational. The thing that has pushed CPI up over the last six months and has the Fed a little bit more concerned and therefore has restarted hiking rates is because we've seen oil, energy and diesel push through in terms of inflation. If we have oil now going the other way ... this is all going to settle down."

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 157 points, or 0.3 percent, to 52,231, the S&P 500 lost 29 points, or 0.4 percent, to 7,520 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 187 points, or 0.7 percent, to 25,065.

The S&P 500 and Nasdaq had risen for two straight days, bouncing back from sharp losses last week sparked by concerns about the potential for government regulations slowing the AI buildout.

But the S&P 500 technology sector dropped 1.4 percent on Tuesday as the worst-performing of the 11 major sectors, weighed down by another drop in Nvidia, which fell 5.4 percent and has tumbled 9.6 percent over the past two sessions. The company's stock reflects mounting concerns over CEO Jensen Huang's future at the chip company after it initiated an internal probe into spy claims involving Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang. China has dismissed the spying allegations as a smear campaign.

Investors are also bracing for Anthropic's expected public listing later this month. The AI lab revealed that its initial public offering is expected to raise as much as US$64.4 billion, giving the company a fully diluted valuation of up to US$1.4 trillion.

A listing by Anthropic could also force other AI heavyweights to compete harder for investor dollars and cause portfolio repositioning by investors.

Neocloud firm CoreWeave shares closed down 0.5 percent but were up about 2 percent in extended trade after it topped Wall Street's revenue estimates on strong demand for its cloud services, easing some recent concerns about the sustainability of the AI boom and the company's debt burden. The stock is down 32 percent on the year. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: North Korean affordability crisis: monthly salary can’t buy even a bag of rice
articles.excerpt: Workers start every month deep in the red as inflation guts official wages and forces reliance on side hustles.
articles.fullText:
[Editor's Note] To protect the safety of sources inside North Korea who could face severe punishment by authorities if identified, the family featured in this article is a composite model based on reporting from exclusive interviews conducted by RFA Korean journalists with two separate households inside North Korea. One household is a couple working at a state-run factory who shared their wages and living expenses with RFA; the other is a family with middle school and primary school children who detailed their household expenditures. All wages, prices, and expenditure details cited in the article are based on facts confirmed in those interviews. Mr. Kim and Ms. Lee are pseudonyms.

Last month’s take-home pay for Mr. Kim – a 45-year old man who works a government-assigned job in a state-run food processing plant in South Pyongan province – was 20,000 won (about 30 US cents). Although his official wage is set at 50,000 won a month, 30,000 won was deducted upfront as “social support” for state construction projects, education funds, and agricultural supply purchases.
Because production levels and management vary widely across industries and state enterprises in North Korea, worker compensation differs significantly. While well-managed, profitable factories pay higher wages, struggling facilities cannot guarantee even baseline monthly compensation.
Mr. Kim was fortunate to receive any pay at all this month – raw materials arrived on time, keeping his factory’s assembly line running. Workers at other plants were not as lucky. They received nothing when supply shortages ground operations to a halt.
Even though he is one of the lucky ones who got paid, a 20,000-won income cannot buy a single kilogram (2.2 pounds) of white rice – currently priced at over 40,000 won per kilogram – or even a kilogram of corn, which costs around 25,000 won.
Based on October price and wage data verified through sources inside North Korea, RFA compiled a monthly budget for a composite four-member household—comprising factory worker Mr. Kim, his wife Ms. Lee, and their two school-aged children—to illustrate the reality of monthly living expenses.
The reported commodity prices were gathered from South and North Pyongan, South and North Hwanghae, and Kangwon provinces.
A simulated November household budget for a fictional family of four in North Korea shows a monthly deficit of about 1.3 million won (about $18), based on October prices in southern North Korea reported by RFA sources.
(RFA Korean) Starting each month ‘in the red’
With two children attending school, the Kim household budget starts in the red every month.
Schools demand children bring “assignment quotas” of waste paper and scrap metal for recycling – it is a mandatory patriotic offering. Collecting the materials takes a lot of time and effort, so most students pay in cash instead – to the tune of around 30,000 won per month. With two kids, that’s 60,000 won, already triple Mr. Kim’s salary.
On top of that, home utilities cost roughly 5,000 won per month. Even though water and electricity can and do cut out at any given moment, they still have to pay the bill.
Thus the Kim family is already 45,000 won in the hole before factoring in the cost of food.
In some factories, 5 to 10 kilograms (about 10-20 pounds) of corn is said to be supplied to working employees once a month, while in North Hamgyong Province, the rice or prepared food items that were previously provided have been completely cut off. Circumstances differ depending on the region, factory, and enterprise, but at any rate, what families are provided through their workplaces is a mere fraction of what they need to eat each month.
According to the daily food recommendations set by North Korean authorities – 750 grams of corn for workers, 550 grams for housewives and 450 grams for students, the monthly food requirement based on three meals per day for the Kims is about 66 kilograms.
1.65 million won corn deficit. Rice? Keep dreaming
How much money does the Kim family need just to scrape by each month?
According to sources, as of October, the price of white rice traded in North and South Pyongan provinces is about 40,000 won per kilogram, and corn is around 25,000 won. In North Hamgyong and Ryanggang provinces, 1 kilogram of white rice has already exceeded 50,000 won.
If the family relied entirely on white rice, their monthly food bill would reach 2.64 million won—equivalent to 52 months of Mr. Kim’s nominal salary of 50,000 won. Rice is therefore a luxury that only the wealthiest North Koreans can afford. Like most North Koreans, the Kims will get by on a diet of mostly corn. A monthly supply costs a total 1.65 million won, which is 33 times Mr. Kim’s nominal monthly income.
Workers at the Ryuwon footwear factory produce various types of Ryuwon-trademarked shoes in Pyongyang, North Korea, Sept. 25, 2020.
(Jon Chol Jin/AP) Jiro Ishimaru, head of the Osaka-based ASIAPRESS media outlet that covers North Korea, explained, “Currently, with a North Korean worker’s salary, rice is out of the question, and they barely live centered around corn.” Asiapress tracks commodity and food prices in various regions through its contacts in North Korea.
“ In the case of working at a state enterprise, it varies by rank and industry, but roughly the monthly pay provided by the state is between 35,000 won and 100,000 won,” he said. “Even if a well-performing state enterprise pays double the salary at 200,000 won, with that money you cannot even buy 5 kilograms of white rice, and there is no such thing as rations. With such wages, people are barely able to live on a diet centered on corn.”
Under these constraints, balanced meals with adequate protein remain an unaffordable luxury. Pork sells for 270,000 won per kilogram—more than 13 times Mr. Kim’s take-home wage – pollack costs 100,000 won per kilogram, and eggs sell for 10,000 won each.
Other important food-related items are also out of reach. Bottled water runs between 5,000 and 10,000 won per liter, and a 10-liter container of imported Russian cooking oil costs 200,000 to 250,000 won. Although prices vary by quality and region, such items remain entirely unattainable on a 20,000-won salary.
Adding basic daily necessities, staple food supplies like condiments, and transportation expenses, the growing deficit is only made worse when unexpected expenses arise.
So the family somehow needs to earn more money to get by.
Side hustles to feed the family
Like most other families, the Kims need side hustles to bridge the gap between Mr. Kim’s income and their monthly living costs. Ms. Lee used to trade goods in the marketplace to earn money, but then the government started cracking down on informal market activity. Now she has turned to day labor, hauling heavy loads or doing manual labor at construction sites. According to sources, the daily wages people earn from this sort of work can be about 100,000 - 200,000 won. In one day of manual labor, she earns double what her husband earns working a full month at the factory.
However, informal work is irregular. Even if Ms. Lee secures 15 days of labor a month and brings in 1.5 million won, her earnings still fall short of covering the 1.65 million won needed just to buy monthly corn supplies.
Ishimaru explained that there are other types of jobs that people can get to bridge the gap.
“Since official salaries alone are not enough, as all our contacts tell us now, assembling products at home—like wigs or eyelashes—serve as side jobs,” said Ishimaru. .
In October 2023, when North Korean authorities drastically increased the legal monthly wages of state enterprise workers, office staff, and civil servants by at least 10 to over 20 times, most North Korean residents welcomed it. Expectations were high that they could eat three meals a day and enjoy basic living, but in just 3 to 4 years, massive inflation caused by shortages, and currency devaluation hit the public economy hard.
RFA sources reported that most workers do not expect wages to serve as a means of livelihood, pointing out the severe gap between state-fixed wages and individual day labor. They criticized North Korea as “socialist in appearance, but more capitalist than actual capitalism.”
Winter brings high coal costs
In November, an even bigger crisis is facing the Kim household: heat. Coal prices have skyrocketed to 800,000–900,000 won per metric ton, more than quadruple the cost just six years ago.
In North Korea, a four-member household usually needs at minimum 1 to 1.5 metric tons of coal to get through winter. To actually be warm, they need at least 3 metric tons, but the Kims decided to stick to minimal heating. Preparing firewood for the winter should have started back in the summer, but Mr. Kim, burdened with monthly budget deficits and struggling just to put food on the table, had no time to spare.
North Korea's Kaephung county is seen from the observatory of the Aegibong Peace Ecopark in Gimpo, South Korea, Nov. 29, 2024.
(Lee Jin-man/AP) Families must also prepare food supplies to get them through the winter, and this has traditionally been done through kimjang, where families gather together and make large amounts of kimchi – enough to last through the colder half of the year.
Sources told RFA that the vegetables that go into kimchi are expensive: napa cabbage currently costs 9,000 to 10,000 won per kilogram, while radishes cost 7,000 to 8,000 won per kilogram. While a family of four typically needs around 300 kilograms of cabbage for the season, the Kim household plans to prepare a minimal batch of 30 kilograms of cabbage kimchi and 10 kilograms of radish kimchi without extra seasonings. Even this reduced batch costs at least 340,000 won, driving the family deeper into debt.
Sources estimate that a four-person household in North Korea needs approximately $80 to $100 USD (roughly 5.9 million to 7.8 million North Korean won) per month for baseline survival, yet ordinary residents operate on less than half that amount. Even if Ms. Lee works day labor and side jobs all month to earn 3 million won, the family still reaches only half of the required subsistence threshold.
RFA asked Ishimaru how ordinary North Korean families manage to survive under persistent deficits.
“I’m really curious too. Truly curious,” Ishimaru said. “Residents in provincial cities live under very difficult conditions. Everyone assesses that life was much more comfortable before 2019, … when individual economic activities were possible.”
To make matters worse, sources project that as usual, grain prices will rise again starting in December as the worst months of winter roll in. Mr. Kim will continue working at the factory to receive 20,000 won. To cover the deficit budget of their 4-member family, his wife Ms. Lee will have to find unofficial work at 100,000 won a day for at least half the month of December to make ends meet, even on their family’s tightened budget.
Edited by Noh Jung Min in Korean and by Charlie Dharapak and Eugene Whong in English.

articles.title: Sex offence laws set for amendment
articles.excerpt: The Government will publish an amendment bill on sexual offences in the gazette on Friday and introduce it into the…
articles.fullText:
The Government will publish an amendment bill on sexual offences in the gazette on Friday and introduce it into the Legislative Council on November 25 for first and second reading, with the target of completing the legislative exercise within the current term of the administration.

The Security Bureau said today that the Sexual Offences Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026 is aimed at strengthening protection for victims of sexual offences, and modernising the laws on sexual offences in Hong Kong to keep pace with the times.

It noted that many of the sexual offences in Hong Kong are based on similar provisions in the laws of England enacted in 1956 and have certain inadequacies.

For instance, some offences are gender-specific, resulting in a narrow scope; some provisions carry distinctions based on sexual orientation; some offences lack consistency on treatments across genders; the provisions and penalties of some sexual offences are not fully commensurate with the gravity of the relevant acts; and some terminology used in some provisions is outdated.

The Government considers it necessary to review and improve the laws to address the inadequacies of the current provisions and respond to changes in social perceptions related to sexual offences.

The legislative amendment proposal is based on the coverage and recommendations of the Law Reform Commission in its review as well as on the study of developments in relevant legislation in other major common law jurisdictions.

The scope covers non-consensual sexual offences, sexual offences involving children and people with mental impairment, miscellaneous sexual offences, and the strengthening of protection for victims of sexual offences.

In a one-month public consultation exercise this year, a total of 6,228 written submissions were received, with 99.3% showing support and offering positive comments. The bureau considered this to fully reflect that the legislative amendment proposal has gained wide support from the community.

The bureau added that the legislative amendment proposal has also incorporated suggestions received by the Government during the public consultation exercise, including the creation of a new offence to deal with perpetrators' criminal acts of prolonged and repeated sexual abuse against children. Through the refinement of provisions, the cyber-related crime of “cyberflashing” will also be criminalised.

articles.title: HK 11th on digital competitiveness
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong has been ranked 11th globally and fourth in Asia in the World Digital & AI Ranking (WDAIR) 2026…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong has been ranked 11th globally and fourth in Asia in the World Digital & AI Ranking (WDAIR) 2026 index, published by the International Institute for Management Development (IMD).

Among the five factors under consideration, Hong Kong ranks inside the top 10 for workforce development, efficiency, and technology and infrastructure.

In terms of sub-factors, Hong Kong ranks top on technological framework (under technology and infrastructure), practices (under efficiency), and education and training (under workforce development). It also ranks inside the top 10 on talent (under workforce development), societal attitudes (under values) and regulatory framework (under governance).

The Government said that WDAIR 2026 recognises Hong Kong as one of the world’s most competitive economies for digital and AI development. It highlighted that Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan sets out a vision for the city’s development as an international centre for innovation and technology, one that has the full backing of the central authorities.

It iterated that Hong Kong will foster new industrialisation with regard for local circumstances, advance the Artificial Intelligence+ Initiative on all fronts, enhance computing infrastructure, support small-and-medium-sized enterprises in their adoption of AI, and empower different sectors of the economy through AI technology.

In terms of upstream research, the Government will build on the “dual base” advantages of the city’s InnoHK Research Clusters and State Key Laboratories, and advance the development of the Hong Kong Microelectronics Research & Development Institute, the Hong Kong Artificial Intelligence Research & Development Institute and the Life & Health Technology Research Institute.

Meanwhile, the Government will accelerate the development of national strategic emerging industries and foster new quality productive forces, including through establishing Hong Kong’s first national manufacturing innovation centre.

It will also enhance the artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystem on multiple dimensions, including computing power, funding and risk management. Construction of the Sandy Ridge Data Facility Cluster is underway and the cluster is expected to be fully operational by 2032 or earlier, providing computing power of 180,000 peta-floating point operations per second, equivalent to 36 times Hong Kong’s current computing power.

The Government has also launched an AI Subsidy Scheme to support the industry in using high-performance computing power for frontier research, and is optimising the Digital Transformation Support Pilot Programme to provide matching subsidies to support more small and medium enterprises in applying AI and cybersecurity solutions.

In addition, the Government will continue to build digitally-led public services. The “iAM Smart” platform has achieved the goal of a single portal for online government services, with daily usage exceeding 220,000 interactions. The platform provides access to more than 1,400 online services.

Meanwhile, the AI Efficacy Enhancement Team is driving government departments to apply AI technology. It has so far facilitated 30 projects involving 13 departments.

Going forward, the Government will aim to promote closer collaboration with the industrial, academic, research and investment sectors, consolidate and enhance Hong Kong’s competitive edge in the global market, and provide more convenient, efficient and reliable public services.

articles.title: New COVID-19 vaccines to arrive
articles.excerpt: The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health stated today that the first shipment of the new…
articles.fullText:
The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health stated today that the first shipment of the new batch of Spikevax XFG vaccine for individuals aged 12 or above is expected to arrive in Hong Kong in December.

In a statement in response to comments from a medical organisation regarding a lack of stock of COVID-19 vaccines and concerns about low COVID-19 vaccination rates, the CHP clarified that market supply will resume and private doctors will be able to order from pharmaceutical companies as usual.

It added that the temporary absence of COVID-19 vaccinations for adults is normal during this transitional period while awaiting new vaccine production and delivery.

The CHP had earlier announced that the shelf life of the LP.8.1 vaccine for children and adults would expire in mid-July and early September respectively, noting that producing and shipping vaccines with updated ingredients takes time.

Starting October 29, the CHP has been providing the Spikevax XFG mRNA vaccine to children aged 6 months to 11 years.

The Government has set up a total of 75 COVID-19 vaccination venues across Hong Kong, including Specialist Out-patient Clinics and Family Medicine Clinics in public hospitals, private clinics, Maternal and Child Health Centres.

Since patients co-infected with seasonal influenza and COVID-19 are at a higher risk of severe complications and death, the CHP has consistently recommended that priority groups receive both seasonal influenza vaccination and COVID-19 vaccination booster to reduce the risk of serious illness and death.

Eligible individuals can receive both COVID-19 and influenza vaccinations at all current vaccination venues, leading the CHP to conclude that there is currently no need to expand the number of sites.

Furthermore, according to a survey conducted by the medical organisation concerned, nearly 40% of the doctors surveyed do not proactively remind patients to receive COVID-19 vaccination.

The CHP expressed concern about this and urged healthcare professionals to proactively remind patients of the importance of receiving COVID-19 vaccination in a timely manner.

Even if their clinics do not provide vaccination services, healthcare professionals can still provide patients with information about the Government's COVID-19 Vaccination Programme, the CHP said.

The CHP added that it will continue to strengthen publicity and education to encourage priority groups to receive COVID-19 vaccination as soon as possible once the COVID-19 vaccines are available.

articles.title: International police academy opens
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong Police Force held the opening ceremony of the Hong Kong International Academy of Policing today, with over…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong Police Force held the opening ceremony of the Hong Kong International Academy of Policing today, with over 400 local and overseas representatives attending the milestone event.

Speaking at the ceremony, Chief Executive John Lee noted that security challenges are increasingly complex and borderless, making strong international connectivity vital to global security and prosperity. He stated that the academy will deepen international police exchanges.

“It will do so through training programmes, police leadership forums and other outreach initiatives. The target is to train some 1,000 officers each year, including about 200 overseas law enforcement personnel.”

“By bringing law enforcement leaders together, it will strengthen Hong Kong's international partnerships. Stronger partnerships will, in turn, reinforce Hong Kong's role as a "super connector" and "super value-adder" – a place that links people and expertise across jurisdictions,” he added.

Commissioner of Police Chow Yat-ming pointed out that the academy is committed to formalising long-term ties with leading institutions worldwide. Uniting their expertise modernises police training and bolsters the collective capability to stay ahead of complex global challenges, he noted.

The initiative aligns with the National 15th Five-Year Plan to participate in the high-quality joint construction of the Belt & Road initiative. It also ties in with the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government's policy direction to promote high-level external co-operation.

The academy provides training programmes for overseas law enforcement agencies, particularly those from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, countries along the Belt & Road and the Middle East region. Its ultimate goal is to become a world-class training base and exchange platform for policing talent.

The academy will co-ordinate more than 20 hallmark programmes spanning two major categories. This includes hallmark training programmes focusing on key professional fields such as strategic command and leadership for policing, control tactics application, counter-terrorism and crisis management, criminal investigation, and protection and security.

These programmes aim to build a professional exchange platform for overseas law enforcement agencies and partners. This will promote mutual learning through shared experiences, knowledge-sharing and pragmatic collaboration in the field of public security.

There are also police leadership forums which focus on issues including emerging crime trends, smart policing, cross-border law enforcement co-operation and corporate governance. The forums will invite global police leaders, experts and scholars to Hong Kong to build a police dialogue platform with a national perspective, Hong Kong characteristics and international influence.

This platform will serve to deepen strategic mutual trust and expand co-operation networks.

At the opening ceremony, a representative from the Hong Kong Police Force signed Memoranda of Understanding with representatives from the police academies of Cambodia and Saudi Arabia. The agreements aim to deepen bilateral police training exchanges and lay a solid foundation for jointly addressing future transnational law enforcement challenges.

articles.title: Exco green lights part two of the Northern Link
articles.excerpt: The government and the MTR Corporation on Tuesday signed the project agreement for the full Northern Link project, as the…
articles.fullText:
The government and the MTR Corporation on Tuesday signed the project agreement for the full Northern Link project, as the Executive Council approved the financial arrangement for the second part of the plan.

Exco greenlit part one of the project in July last year.

This means that the main line and the spur line – expected to be commissioned simultaneously by 2034 – have fully entered the construction stage.

The cost is estimated to be about HK$54.8 billion for part two of the project, while the entire project is estimated to cost about HK$86.2 billion – 28 percent lower than the initial forecast, due to the shortened construction period and cost-saving benefits.

Exco agreed to grant a total of eight sites located in Ngau Tam Mei Area, San Tin Area, Kwu Tung North Area and the proposed Au Tau New Development Area to the railway operator for residential and commercial development.

A fixed lump sum will be deducted from the land premium of the sites to help fund the MTR in carrying out part two of the project.

The railway operator, for its part, said the estimated capital cost for the Northern Link is the most expensive one among its works.

It emphasised that it had been financially sound in recent years, and that it increased cash flow by issuing bonds.

The MTR said it does not rule out the possibility of raising capital through ways other than bond issuance.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.excerpt: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in…
