As companies look to accelerate innovation with artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and advanced modeling, the primary challenge is connecting new technologies to reliable data, scientific expertise, and the practical realities of bringing products to market. For specialty chemicals manufacturer Lubrizol, digital transformation is all about giving researchers the tools to test ideas faster, make better-informed decisions, and develop more sustainable materials without compromising performance.

Girish Rao, vice president of information technology at Lubrizol, says the company is building a digital foundation that connects business processes, modern data platforms, and cloud infrastructure to support its research and development (R&D) teams. Their goal is to combine decades of accumulated technical data with the deep expertise of chemists and engineers who understand customer needs as well as the physical constraints of their work. Data scientists can help identify patterns, test new hypotheses, and model possibilities before researchers conduct physical experiments. But, Rao emphasizes, “it’s not about replacing scientific judgment; it is about giving our scientists better tools.”

Scientists, data scientists, and IT teams approach problems from different perspectives, prioritizing experimental validity, model performance, and platform security and scalability, respectively. By bringing these groups together in “fusion teams,” Lubrizol aligns them around shared objectives, starting with small pilots to build trust.

“Once the trust is built between the team members and they know what value they’re about to create,” Rao says, “things go a lot better.” Cloud infrastructure also gives the company flexibility to access computing resources and modern tools without making the substantial investments required to build and maintain its own data centers.

These capabilities could prove especially valuable in advancing sustainability. Digital modeling can help researchers evaluate more formulations, explore materials such as starch and corn-based alternatives, and assess trade-offs across a product’s life cycle. Promising a material in a laboratory is only the first step. Scaling production while meeting performance expectations, regulatory requirements, and financial constraints is still a tightrope walk, but AI’s ability to model multiple variables could help teams navigate those competing demands.

Looking to the future, Rao expects AI, automation, advanced modeling, digital twins, and connected data to converge as laboratories become more intelligent and manufacturing plants more efficient. The opportunity, he suggests, lies in bringing these capabilities together responsibly and at scale. “It’s not just a single technology. I think it’s the combination of all of these, and it’ll be the ability to connect all these processes that are going to generate tremendous amounts of data.”

This webcast is produced in partnership with Infosys.

This content was produced by Insights, MIT Technology Review’s custom content arm, not its editorial staff. It was researched and written by humans, with any AI tools that may have been used limited to production processes under human oversight.

articles.title: The climate case for AI has not been made
articles.excerpt: This week, as countries meet in Antalya, Turkey for the United Nations climate conference, one topic likely to dominate the…
articles.fullText:
This week, as countries meet in Antalya, Turkey for the United Nations climate conference, one topic likely to dominate the conversation is artificial intelligence. The host has already called on countries to commit to ensuring that AI is designed, powered, and deployed in ways that support climate action.

But so far, industries around the world aren’t doing nearly enough to harness the technology to actually drive down the greenhouse-gas emissions heating up the planet, despite some very optimistic claims from AI companies.

In 2024, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman declared that AI would unleash “astounding triumphs,” including “fixing the climate.” The year before, in a 2023 op-ed , the head of sustainability at Google and her coauthor wrote that AI could reduce global emissions 5% to 10% by 2030.

Some academic researchers have examined these AI-related climate claims. A peer-reviewed study published last year, led by researchers at the London School of Economics’ Grantham Research Institute and the firm Systemiq, estimated that AI could help cut global emissions by the equivalent of 3.2 to 5.4 billion tons of carbon dioxide annually by 2035—roughly on par with the US’s annual energy-related emissions on the high end, even after subtracting AI’s own energy footprint. Those potential gains are mostly concentrated in three sectors: power, meat and dairy, and vehicles.

But projections like these are only as good as our willingness to test them against present-day reality. So is there evidence that the largest companies in these three sectors are beginning to integrate AI in line with the study’s projections, and if so, do the results match expectations? Or is the 2035 number still mostly aspirational?

Companies across these sectors have announced plenty of initial efforts to incorporate AI into various business practices. But an AI-assisted review of public information from significant market actors in each sector, conducted and reviewed by the second author of this piece, found that few have announced they’re pursuing the specific emissions-reducing routes that informed the projections in the study—and fewer still claim they’ve used them to achieve meaningful climate progress.

The power sector is where the earlier study’s underlying math is most concrete: AI-driven forecasting of supply and demand could increase the amount of renewable electricity that reaches the grid from already-built solar and wind facilities by up to 20%, which could prevent an estimated 1.8 billion tons of emissions a year.

Yet of the grid operators reviewed in China, the United States, and Europe, only one deployed a known meaningful, working AI program of this sort, according to the analysis. A partnership between the UK’s National Grid ESO and Open Climate Fix halved the grid operator’s solar-forecast error (the difference between the amount of incoming sunlight predicted and the amount that actually reaches solar panels), avoiding hundreds of thousands of tons of carbon dioxide a year. Beyond this example in the UK, though, many other grid operators in the EU, the US, and China had little to show in the public record in terms of the AI integration envisioned by the study.

The meat and dairy sector offers the starkest contrast between technology readiness and market reality. To achieve the 2035 emission reductions anticipated in the earlier study, AI would need to close the taste and cost gap between traditional proteins and alternative ones, such as lab-grown or plant-based burgers and milk substitutes.

In one of the clearest efforts to achieve this, the AI and food tech company NotCo recently formed a joint venture with Kraft Heinz using its platform Giuseppe , which analyzes plant molecular data to pinpoint combinations replicating the taste, texture, and smell of animal products.

But few other alternative-protein companies had such a deeply integrated way of using AI in product development, the AI-assisted review suggests. Meanwhile, the sector seems to be facing more fundamental problems, including stubbornly slow mainstream consumer adoption and declining funding levels. Most notably, venture capital flowing into cultivated meat fell from a $989 million peak in 2021 to around $83 million last year.

The transportation sector offers some hopeful examples of the type of AI integration necessary to achieve the study’s projections, particularly among battery manufacturers and ride-sharing platforms. CATL—which controls roughly 40% of the global market for electric-vehicle batteries—launched an AI system trained on more than 100,000 battery design cases and 600 terabytes of test data. It cut the time needed to screen candidate materials by two orders of magnitude, according to the company. Independent researchers also found that the ride-sharing platform Didi Chuxing was able cut per-trip emissions 16% on average by using AI-optimized routing to minimize detours.

There’s another big problem in the climate case for AI, though: Oil and gas companies are also interested in these tools for many reasons, including the potential to increase production of fossil fuels . Technology firms that committed to sustainability goals in the past should answer questions about how their tools could be used to boost old, dirty energy as well as clean, renewable energy.

Finally, it’s also worth noting that integrating AI is just the first step, and it remains unclear to what degree the technology can accelerate the sorts of improvements and innovations envisioned. AI also does little to shorten the standard paths to certifying, permitting, building, packaging, marketing, and selling any resulting products, facilities, or services.

The findings of the analysis, carried out by Anthropic’s Claude Code, were reviewed against public documents and media accounts to ensure their accuracy. It is possible that some companies and utilities in these industries are pursuing AI-assisted applications that would fit into the initial study’s scenarios but haven’t yet been disclosed publicly.

Greater and better-targeted AI integration and efficiency gains in these three sectors may well materialize, bringing the 2035 projections closer to reality. But it won’t happen without deliberate and sustained efforts to ensure that AI delivers more environmental benefits than harms.

Notably, so far the rapid adoption of AI models and buildout of data centers has driven a huge increase in energy consumption and emissions, and this has led major tech companies like Microsoft, Google, and others to fall well off track in their corporate climate goals. At this point it would be surprising if the sector even manages to zero out its climate pollution: Emissions associated with global data centers (which may handle AI as well as non-AI computing tasks) could exceed 300 million tons annually in 2035, according to the IEA’s base forecast .

Industry leaders must implement the technology in the ways that promise to do the most to drive down emissions. Corporate customers should select models with the lowest environmental impacts and opt to work with the AI developers doing the most to reduce their climate footprint. And states and regions need to do more to incentivize or require all these companies to operate in more responsible ways.

The need has never been more apparent.

Mary Nichols is distinguished counsel at the UCLA School of Law and the former chair of the California Air Resources Board.

Jeremy Tamanini is the founder of Dual Citizen, a sustainability research and advisory firm.

articles.title: HK stocks slip as mainland steadies on policy pledge
articles.excerpt: Mainland stocks ended higher on Monday, tracking gains in regional peers, while Beijing called for more efforts to stabilise the…
articles.fullText:
Mainland stocks ended higher on Monday, tracking gains in regional peers, while Beijing called for more efforts to stabilise the market.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index inched down 32 points, or 0.1 percent, to end the day at 24,448 on turnover of HK$173.71 billion.

The tech index dropped 37 points, or 0.9 percent, to 4,040 while the China enterprises index fell 13 points, or 0.2 percent, to 8,260.

On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index rose 11 points, or 0.32 percent, to close at 3,660 on turnover of 682.53 billion yuan while the blue-chip CSI300 index inched up 0.1 percent.

The Shenzhen Component Index fell 30 points, or 0.27 percent, to 11,145, on turnover of 800 billion yuan while the ChiNext Index inched down six points, or 0.27 percent, to close at 2,458 on turnover of 402 billion yuan.

Shanghai's tech-focused Star50 index gained 0.3 percent.

Shanghai's gains followed a pledge by the State Council on Friday to improve mechanisms to stabilise the capital market and enhance the stock market's inherent stability, state television CCTV reported.

"China's economic data and equity performance have again breached policymakers' pain threshold, prompting fresh equity market support measures," analysts at Societe Generale said in a note.

"These may put a floor under sentiment, but sustained upside requires stronger corporate profits, hence better domestic demand and reflation – still elusive without more forceful fiscal support."

China's producer inflation accelerated to its fastest rate in nearly four-and-a-half years in October as higher global oil prices raised manufacturing costs, even as consumer inflation cooled amid weak domestic demand, data showed on Monday.

China's goods exports are expected to have surged by a third in October, a poll showed, a helpful offset to weak domestic demand even as a year-to-date trade surplus of more than US$1 trillion risks further antagonising trading partners.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei advanced 1,340 points, or 2.33 percent, to close at 58,775, recouping part of Friday's six percent slump.

The broader Topix climbed 110 points, or 2.97 percent, to 3,818.

In Seoul, the Kospi closed down 40 points, or 0.81 percent, at 5,018, the benchmark's lowest level in nine months, in a choppy trading session led by a slump in battery makers while a rebound in chipmakers capped losses.

The Kospi's losses came amid news that Nvidia chief Jensen Huang's daughter, Madison, cancelled a planned visit to Seoul for an Nvidia conference that was set to begin on Monday, according to companies she had been scheduled to meet.

Her cancellation came as her father admitted on Sunday to having had an affair.

Nvidia's shares tumbled more than six percent in Frankfurt trading, extending last week's selloff and pushing the stock to fresh multi-month lows.

At those levels, the chipmaker stood to lose about US$270 billion from its closing price on Friday, according to LSEG Datastream.

"The market's probably telling you now this does no favours to the stock whatsoever in a time when there's a lot of conjecture as to the build-out of data centres," said Chris Weston, head of research at brokerage Pepperstone in Melbourne.

But Weston said he did not think Huang, whom he described as the "godfather of AI", would be replaced.

"If we genuinely thought he was going to step down ... the stock would be down – it would be an absolute bloodbath, to be honest,” he said. (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: China slams 'baseless' claims it spied on Nvidia boss
articles.excerpt: Beijing rejected on Monday claims that it had spied on Jensen Huang, chief executive of US chip giant Nvidia, calling…
articles.fullText:
Beijing rejected on Monday claims that it had spied on Jensen Huang, chief executive of US chip giant Nvidia, calling the allegations "baseless".

"We have responded to this matter previously. The narrative of a so-called Chinese spy is entirely baseless vilification and smearing," Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesman Guo Jiakun said at a regular briefing.

He was speaking after Nvidia's board announced it had opened a probe into media reports alleging "a foreign intelligence effort" and Huang's acknowledgement that he had an affair with a woman.

Late last month, The New York Times reported that US intelligence officials concluded that Alice Huang, a Chinese executive linked to a Singapore-based data centre company called Megaspeed, had been funnelling information to Beijing.

The executive, also known as Huang Le, developed a close relationship with the 63-year-old Nvidia boss, the Times said.

In a message to company employees released on Sunday, the Nvidia chief acknowledged having an affair and apologised to his family and company staff.

"I was unfaithful to my wife," he said.

"My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

Jensen Huang is a huge figure in the artificial intelligence revolution and a close informal adviser to US President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly spoken out against regulating the industry so as not to let China gain the upper hand in the AI race.

The issue of AI is likely to arise during Trump's planned talks with President Xi Jinping this month at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen.

Asked whether the Nvidia chief would be joining his trip to Asia, which includes the Apec summit in Shenzhen next week, Trump said: "I don't know but I'll certainly take him."

Trump said Huang was "a fine person, but you never know what's going on. I'm sure – I hope everything's fine. He's done such an incredible job." (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Trump says Shenzhen talks with Xi and Putin likely
articles.excerpt: US President Donald Trump on Sunday said he expects to meet with President Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin…
articles.fullText:
US President Donald Trump on Sunday said he expects to meet with President Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in Shenzhen scheduled for November 18-19.

"Well, I'm going to be going to China," he said, "and one of the meetings I think will be with President Putin and President Xi, and that'll be interesting."

He added: "We'll talk a lot of things, including denuclearisation, but we'll be talking a lot of things. We're trying to end the war in Iran."

The Kremlin said on October 21 that this first of its kind trilateral meeting is "being prepared".

This followed a Wall Street Journal report that Putin wanted the three-way talks to broker a peace deal to end the conflict between Russia and Ukraine. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Hong Kong must widen surgical robotics access: FS
articles.excerpt: Financial Secretary Paul Chan has urged the surgical robotics industry to move beyond proving technical precision and focus on widening…
articles.fullText:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan has urged the surgical robotics industry to move beyond proving technical precision and focus on widening access to care, as Hong Kong seeks to become a global hub for medical-device innovation.

Speaking at the inaugural Surgical Futures Forum organised by Hong Kong-based surgical robotics company Cornerstone Robotics, Chan said the field had spent 25 years proving its technical capability.

The next task, he said, was to broaden access so more surgeons could use robotic systems and more patients could benefit.

"Design and cost remain major barriers. Today's mainstream systems are built for the best-resourced hospitals. Their price, their footprint and their training requirements limit where they can be installed and how widely they can be used," he said.

"That helps explain why global penetration remains below five percent. If we believe innovation should serve humanity, progress in surgical robotics must mean more than better technology — it must mean reaching more patients because behind these barriers are countless people still waiting to benefit."

Chan said the clearest sign of momentum came in September, when global medtech company Medtronic announced a strategic investment of about US$700 million in Cornerstone Robotics and secured distribution rights for Cornerstone’s surgical system in selected international markets.

He described the commitment from a global medical-technology leader as a powerful endorsement of Hong Kong’s innovation sector.

"This partnership shows that technology developed here can earn the confidence of industry leaders and, through collaboration, reach international markets," he said, calling it a milestone for both companies and another example of Hong Kong innovation going global.

The finance chief also cited a Hong Kong-developed robotic platform now installed at a leading surgical training centre in Strasbourg, France, as evidence that the city’s medtech sector is ready to train surgeons from around the world.

Beyond individual companies, he pitched Hong Kong as an end-to-end support system for medical-device innovation, spanning long-term patient capital, biotech fundraising, regulation, clinical data and cross-boundary trials.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Death toll mounts to 14 in Shanxi fire
articles.excerpt: The death toll from a fire at a building in Taiyuan, capital of northern Shanxi province, has risen to 14…
articles.fullText:
The death toll from a fire at a building in Taiyuan, capital of northern Shanxi province, has risen to 14, local authorities said on Monday.

The fire broke out at the building in the city's Yingze District at 4.59pm on Sunday, with the fire department saying the building is on Liuxiang South Road.

The death toll update followed an earlier report that 38 people had been sent to hospitals, with five of them being declared dead. (Xinhua)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Chinese inflation spikes at plants and cools in shops
articles.excerpt: China's producer inflation accelerated to its fastest pace in nearly four-and-a-half years while consumer inflation cooled in October, data showed…
articles.fullText:
China's producer inflation accelerated to its fastest pace in nearly four-and-a-half years while consumer inflation cooled in October, data showed on Monday, reflecting persistent cost pressures from higher oil prices despite weak domestic demand.

Global oil prices remained elevated during much of last month, raising costs for coal mining, oil and natural gas extraction processing, chemicals and other energy-intensive sectors, a key driver of producer-price inflation.

Those upstream price pressures have yet to fully feed through to consumers amid soft demand conditions.

The producer price index climbed by 5.7 percent from a year earlier, compared with a five percent increase in September, beating economists' forecasts for a 5.3 percent gain in a poll, data from the National Bureau of Statistics showed.

The consumer price index rose by 0.7 percent year on year, after a 0.9 percent rise in September, to come in just below economists' expectations for a 0.8 percent increase.

On a monthly basis, the CPI matched forecasts for an unchanged outcome after edging up 0.2 percent in September.

While the world's second-largest economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter, buoyed by resilient exports, weak household demand has continued to constrain consumer spending.

Ongoing trade tensions and an increasingly uncertain global outlook are also clouding the outlook for exports.

External shocks are having a greater impact, while the imbalance between robust supply and weak domestic demand remains pronounced, said an official at China's state planner last month.

China's struggling stock market, where AI-related stocks have tumbled from lofty valuations on concerns about AI demand and export restrictions targeting China, could further weigh on consumer spending.

Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, eased to 0.8 percent in October from one percent in September, offering a gauge of underlying price pressures in the economy. (Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Hang Seng Index climbs amid tech caution
articles.excerpt: Asian markets and US equity futures made a steady start on Monday, wobbling into positive territory after a wild week…
articles.fullText:
Asian markets and US equity futures made a steady start on Monday, wobbling into positive territory after a wild week in which doubts about demand for computer chips sent tech-heavy markets in Asia into some of their steepest falls in years.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index opened up 143 points, or 0.59 percent, at 24,625.

The China enterprises index was 51 points, or 0.62 percent, higher at 8,325 while the tech index rose 41 points, or 1.02 percent, to 4,119.

Up north, the Shanghai Composite Index opened up nine points, or 0.27 percent, at 3,659.

The Shenzhen Component Index rose 97 points, or 0.87 percent, to 11,273 while the ChiNext Index was 29 points, or 1.19 percent, up at 2,494.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei opened 526 points, or 0.92 percent, higher at 57,960, and its gains gained momentum to put the 225 benchmark 1,946 points higher at one stage before noon.

In Seoul, the Kospi was the odd one out, opening 25 points, or 0.5 percent, lower at 5,034 before nudging up to be 87 points in positive territory at one stage before lunch.

Earnings reports due this week from US tech companies such as CoreWeave, Applied Materials and Cisco Systems are set to put the profitability of AI ambitions to the test amid the massive costs of the build-out.

"The markets are far from being out of the woods yet," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com.

"Following last week's midterm elections that have led to increased regulatory risk and an overall underwhelming earnings season that's seen Magnificent Seven companies miss earnings expectations, the momentum remains skewed to the downside."

Elsewhere, Brent crude fell to US$97.49 per barrel after US President Donald Trump on Sunday said he was highly unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran as long as talks to end the conflict progress.

A blowout jobs report on Friday showed US employers added 165,000 jobs last month, more than twice economists' expectations and bolstering the case for the US Federal Reserve to raise interest rates in December.

A US CPI reading due on Tuesday could further cement expectations for a hike next month.

Market expectations for an increase of at least 25 basis points at the central bank's December meeting moved up to nearly 80 percent in the wake of the report, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.

Comments from officials also supported views for a rate hike, with New York Fed president John Williams saying US economic growth has remained remarkably resilient in the face of successive shocks but inflation is too high and it is essential to bring it back to two percent.

That helped the greenback to notch its biggest single-day gain in five months. The dollar index, which tracks the greenback against a basket of currencies of other major trading partners, last traded at 102.2. (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Lopez double fires Barcelona to top of La Liga
articles.excerpt: Fermin Lopez struck twice to help Barcelona come from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 and move three points clear…
articles.fullText:
Fermin Lopez struck twice to help Barcelona come from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 and move three points clear at the top of La Liga.

The Spanish champions lead second place Real Madrid, who beat Valencia 3-0 on Saturday, with Atletico third, now five points behind.

Giuliano Simeone fired Atletico ahead in a high-octane start, before Lopez pulled Barca level shortly before the interval at the Metropolitano stadium.

The 23-year-old Spain international netted the winner after 66 minutes when Lamine Yamal slipped him in, helped Barca triumph despute not being at their best.

Last season Atletico defeated Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals and also in the Copa del Rey, but the Catalans earned some measure of revenge here.

"Coming off last season, when they beat us... we knew what they were going to offer – a very difficult game," Lopez told Movistar.

"It got tricky for us in the first half with their goal, but I think we knew how to come back and we had a great match."

Atletico captain Koke said his team would not let the defeat, their first in La Liga since September 5, upset them.

"I think the team had a really great first half. We had chances to kill off the game and we didn't take, them," said Koke.

"That's football – it's about being clinical, and they were more clinical than we were.

"But there's nothing to criticise the team for, we have to keep going like this because there's still a long way to go in La Liga."

Earlier on, fourth-place Real Betis earned a 2-0 win at Elche, while Real Sociedad, fifth, defeated Rayo Vallecano 1-0.

Villarreal beat Getafe 2-0 to move eighth and Celta Vigo and Levante shared a goalless draw. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Norris wins Brazil; Mercedes take constructors' title
articles.excerpt: Lando Norris picked his way through the rainstorms on Sunday to claim a second consecutive victory for McLaren in the…
articles.fullText:
Lando Norris picked his way through the rainstorms on Sunday to claim a second consecutive victory for McLaren in the Sao Paulo Grand Prix as Mercedes clinched the constructors' championship and a famous title double.

The 26-year-old outgoing 2025 world champion came home 14.6 seconds clear of Red Bull's four-time champion Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar to record his 14th career victory and the 50th podium.

Verstappen started from 21st on the grid and delivered another bravura drive while George Russell finished fourth, after starting fifth and spinning in the pitlane, for Mercedes ahead of teammate Kimi Antonelli, who finished fifth, seven days after becoming the youngest champion.

The 20-year-old had started from the front row alongside pole-sitter Norris and endured a difficult race, but it was enough to ensure that Mercedes outscored Ferrari to take a ninth teams' title.

"That was a very tough race," said Norris.

"It was difficult with the launches off the line, a lot of challenges, going to slicks in the wet and so tough when you are pushing! But I kept it cool and made no mistakes and it is nice to be on the top step again."

Verstappen said: "It was a challenging race! The first laps were so important. We were strong on the inters, but then it was not so good but starting P21 and finishing on the podium is a good result."

Hadjar, having taken his third podium of the year and led a Grand Prix for the first time, added: "That was so difficult. The switching from inters to softs and then back again! Very tricky to drive and then more rain."

The race began with a spectacular opening lap as Antonelli, with an excellent start, led into the Senna Esses as Norris struggled from his 20th pole and Lawson moved up to third in the Curva do Sol.

Behind them, Lewis Hamilton and Verstappen made light of their back-of-the-grid starts and were ninth and 10th within two laps as plumes of spray rose throughout the field.

By lap six, Norris had recovered to pass Liam Lawson while Antonelli was 5.1 seconds clear and instructed to keep his tyres cool. All were on intermediates as the track began to dry with heavy rain forecast.

Verstappen and Antonelli delayed their stops, allowing Norris to take advantage of his earlier stop to warm his tyres and, when Antonelli spun at the start of lap 20 on cold rubber, he took the lead.

On lap 50, Norris pitted again, returning third behind McLaren teammate Oscar Piastri, who let him by, before he took second when Hadjar pitted on lap 51, leaving the 2025 champion 7.4 seconds behind his successor.

Antonelli came in again on lap 55, handing Norris the lead. Again. He rejoined fifth behind Russell, with the Red Bulls second and third. It began drizzling and then intensified into rain.

Norris pitted on lap 63 for intermediate tyres, followed by Verstappen and the rest, with Antonelli released into the exit path of Franco Colapinto and Hamilton spinning - as conditions worsened in the final laps. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Alcaraz downs Shelton to win Paris Masters
articles.excerpt: Carlos Alcaraz gained a measure of revenge on Ben Shelton on Sunday as the seven-time Grand Slam champion beat the…
articles.fullText:
Carlos Alcaraz gained a measure of revenge on Ben Shelton on Sunday as the seven-time Grand Slam champion beat the American 7-6 (7/5), 7-5 to win the Paris Masters for the first time.

In defeating the man who ended his US Open title defence earlier this season, the 23-year-old claimed the ninth 1000-level title of his career.

Unlike their five-set quarter-final epic in New York two months ago, the clash in Paris lasted just under two hours.

"For me it's really special that finally I just got to play great tennis," Alcaraz told reporters. "I went far in the tournament, lifting the trophy at the end.

"I would say this week I took a step forward mentally. I had a lot of really tough moments.

"I'm just really happy that I controlled my emotions, controlled my thoughts every moment, every single match," he added in reference to his quarter-final win against Taylor Fritz in which he saved two match points.

Coming into Paris on the back of winning the 500-level title in Vienna, Alcaraz has won his last nine matches.

"Probably these two last weeks have been the best I've played since my comeback," Alcaraz added of his return from a wrist injury that caused him to miss the French Open and Wimbledon.

Ahead of the ATP Finals, which run November 15-22 in Turin, world number three Alcaraz now holds five tour-level titles this year – only the injured Jannik Sinner has more with six.

In Italy, he will next be seeking a first coronation at the season-ending Finals.

For world number four Shelton, it was a first defeat in a Masters final after winning his two previous appearances in showpiece matches at that level – both coming in the last two editions of the Canadian Open.

An entertaining first set which drew a multitude of admiring gasps from the crowd went the distance despite both players enjoying some success on the other's serve.

In the tie-break, a Shelton error at 4-4 followed by a leaping backhand smash by Alcaraz brought up two set points.

The first came and went when Alcaraz thundered the ball into the top of the net cord and the expectant arena froze in time as it rose and fell in seeming slow motion, only to land on the Spaniard's side of the court.

Alcaraz was not to be denied a second time, however, as Shelton overcooked a forehand on the next point to cede the opener.

At 2-2 in the second set, Shelton let out a bellow of frustration after missing a groundstroke at 15-30 on Alcaraz's serve, but the American could smile at the end of the game as a double fault and missed forehand produced the first break of the match.

Alcaraz had said after booking his spot in the final that his reflexes would need to be "ten out of ten" when facing Shelton's serve and they were just that three games later as he levelled the set at four-all.

A deft exchange of angled drop shots ended by an Alcaraz winner down the line brought the Spaniard's finger to his ear and the crowd again to their feet as Shelton suddenly found himself serving to keep the final alive.

He did so at the first time of asking but when required to serve again to force a breaker, Shelton cracked as Alcaraz again pounced to seal the title with a flicked backhand winner.

"It's all about the little details. The difference in our match in the US Open was the little details, and same here," 24-year-old Shelton said.

"I've learned so much, and it's the position that I want to be in.

"Playing in the US Open final against (Alexander) Zverev, playing the finals here against Carlos, now going to Turin and get to line up against the eight best players in the world."

After winning two French Opens and now the Paris Masters, former world number one Alcaraz is undefeated in title matches in the city, excluding the Olympic Games which do not carry ranking points.

In the earlier doubles final, French pair Quentin Halys and Pierre-Hugues Herbert upset second seeds Neal Skupski and Christian Harrison as the wildcards triumphed 7-6 (7/3), 6-7 (4/7), 10-8. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Man Utd fight back to draw with Villa; Chelsea stunned
articles.excerpt: Manchester United rescued an incredible 4-4 draw against Aston Villa as two stoppage-time goals gave Michael Carrick renewed hope of…
articles.fullText:
Manchester United rescued an incredible 4-4 draw against Aston Villa as two stoppage-time goals gave Michael Carrick renewed hope of avoiding the sack, while Chelsea suffered a shock 1-0 loss at Sunderland on Sunday.

United boss Carrick was seconds away from heading into the international break on the back of another devastating defeat that would surely have led to his dismissal.

But Carrick's side struck twice in the six minutes of additional time through Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu to leave their manager's future still uncertain.

United are in the relegation zone and have not won in their last eight Premier League matches, so it is far from sure that Carrick will survive the axe.

He had earned a stay of execution when United's hierarchy allowed him to remain in charge despite last weekend's loss at Chelsea.

United responded by ending a nine-match winless run in all competitions as they came from two goals down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday.

But United, who have only three wins in 15 games this season, were back in turmoil when they fell 2-0 down against Villa in the first four minutes at Old Trafford.

Alysson struck in the first minute with a shot that squirmed under United keeper Senne Lammens.

Nicolas Jackson slotted in the second three minutes later after a weak save from Lammens pushed the ball into his path.

Bruno Fernandes got one back with a 16th-minute penalty after Boubacar Kamara fouled Matheus Cunha before former Villa midfielder Youri Tielemans slammed in United's 44th-minute equaliser.

Villa's John McGinn converted a 48th-minute penalty following Diogo Dalot's clumsy challenge on Alysson.

Leon Goretzka poked in Villa's fourth from close-range after United's Leny Yoro headed against his own crossbar in the 53rd minute.

Yet Zirkzee's stoppage-time finish gave United hope and Dorgu headed their dramatic equaliser in the final seconds after a weak punch from Villa keeper Zion Suzuki.

Carrick wore a bewildered look on his face as he walked down the tunnel towards an uncertain future, with United next in action at Liverpool on November 22.

"Making it hard for ourselves. The goals are coming from individual mistakes. We need to tighten up," Carrick said.

"But I thought we were the better team. If we get one, then anything can happen. We never gave up and never stopped believing."

Chelsea arrived at the Stadium of Light hoping to bolster their bid to qualify for the Champions League via a top-four finish.

Instead, they departed red-faced after an embarrassing loss to third-bottom Sunderland, who celebrated a league victory for only the second time this season.

Fifth-placed Chelsea have already been beaten four times in 10 league matches under former Real Madrid boss Xabi Alonso.

Chelsea were rocked in the 36th minute when Enzo Le Fee converted a penalty after Brian Brobbey was up-ended by Levi Colwill.

"We were not creating enough chances in the final third against the low block. We were not controlling and sustaining the attack there," Alonso said.

Liverpool got back on track with a 3-1 win at lowly Crystal Palace.

The Reds had been beaten by Arsenal and Fenerbahce before arriving in south London, sparking pointed questions about Andoni Iraola in the former Bournemouth manager's first season in charge.

But Alexis Mac Allister headed Liverpool in front from Dominik Szoboszlai's cross after 40 minutes.

Florian Wirtz bagged Liverpool's second with a composed finish from Bradley Barcola's cross in the 54th minute.

Alexander Isak finished off Wirtz's pass in the 89th minute to wrap up fourth-placed Liverpool's much-needed victory after a two-game losing streak.

Eddie Nketiah's stoppage-time penalty after a foul by Milos Kerkez was no consolation for bottom of the table Palace.

Brighton extended their superb start to the season, climbing to second place with a 2-0 win against Brentford at the Amex Stadium.

Diego Gomez put Brighton ahead early on before Brentford striker Igor Thiago was sent off.

Pascal Gross doubled Brighton's advantage with a 42nd minute penalty.

The Seagulls' sixth win in their last seven league games lifted them within five points of champions Arsenal, who beat Hull on Saturday.

Bournemouth striker Evanilson maintained his hot streak with a goal in a 2-1 win at Ipswich. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Fake recycling scheme alert issued
articles.excerpt: The Environmental Protection Department (EPD) today urged the public to stay alert against a fraudulent "Renewable Resource Recovery Incentive Scheme"…
articles.fullText:
The Environmental Protection Department (EPD) today urged the public to stay alert against a fraudulent "Renewable Resource Recovery Incentive Scheme" which falsely claims to offer subsidies for recycling.

The department noted it has recently received public enquiries regarding a recycling subsidy scheme purportedly launched in partnership with a commercial enterprise. It advised citizens not to believe the circulating publicity poster or any related information.

The EPD clarified that it has never jointly launched any project named the "Renewable Resource Recovery Incentive Scheme" with any organisations. It has also never authorised any individual or entity to use its name or logo for such publicity.

Upon review, the department confirmed that both the EPD and enterprise logos featured on the poster are fake. The EPD has reported the incident to Police.

The department reminded members of the public not to trust posters, links or messaging apps from unknown sources, and to avoid participating in suspicious recycling subsidy activities. Citizens should also refrain from disclosing personal data or financial information to unverified parties.

Anyone who has provided personal information or conducted transactions in connection with the fraudulent scheme should contact Police as soon as possible.

articles.title: Robot loan applications open
articles.excerpt: The Digital Policy Office (DPO) today announced that applications are now open for the "Robots in the Community" Pilot Programme…
articles.fullText:
The Digital Policy Office (DPO) today announced that applications are now open for the "Robots in the Community" Pilot Programme, allowing eligible organisations to borrow robots for demonstrations and performances at free community events. Applications are free of charge and will close on November 20.

By loaning a humanoid robot named "Smart Bot" at no cost for events hosted by community groups, the scheme enables the public to interact with it first-hand. This direct engagement aims to enhance public understanding of embodied artificial intelligence (AI).

Eligible applicants include Hong Kong companies, societies, district organisations, welfare agencies, and Legislative Council or District Council members' offices that serve the public or local residents. Proposed community events under this application round must take place between December 15, 2026, and February 28, 2027.

At these events, "Smart Bot" can perform dancing and kung fu. It can also act as a popular science ambassador to share knowledge of embodied AI and other digital technologies with participants.

The DPO has introduced various initiatives under the "Smart Silver" Digital Inclusion Programme to assist people in need, particularly the elderly, understand and use digital products and services. The "Robots in the Community" Pilot Programme will be the latest addition to this campaign.

Click here for details.

articles.title: Liu overpowers Eala for HK Open crown
articles.excerpt: Claire Liu of the United States powered to victory at the Hong Kong Tennis Open on Sunday, dismantling Philippine sensation…
articles.fullText:
Claire Liu of the United States powered to victory at the Hong Kong Tennis Open on Sunday, dismantling Philippine sensation Alexandra Eala 6-3, 6-0 for her maiden tour-level singles title.

Liu, who entered the WTA 250 event ranked 102nd in the world, added the SAR trophy to a cabinet which already includes challenger-level titles she won in Paris in 2022 and in Barranquilla in September this year.

The pair found themselves locked in a fierce battle at Victoria Park early on, trading blistering shots to go level at 3-3 in the opening set.

After the second-seeded Eala received medical treatment on her right knee, Liu began to pull away convincingly, capitalising on costly errors from her opponent to claim the opener in 38 minutes while overcoming a strong show of support from Filipino fans in the crowd.

The second set proved to be a far more straightforward affair, with Liu breaking serves and wearing out a visibly shaken-up Eala to take the title in dominant fashion.

"This week in general has been really fun," Liu told reporters after her win.

"But it's also been mentally really tough... last tournament of the year, it's a really big push.

"I was just trying to take it one day at a time, and I found myself in the finals."

She also spoke about having to shake off nerves prior to the championship match.

"You really want to win no matter what," she added. "But I think I was just trying to make it like it's just one other match, and yeah, it worked out."

Defeat denied a second major career title for Eala, who was bidding to add to her historic triumph in Washington DC in August that saw her become the first Filipina player to reach and win a WTA 500 final.

Still, Eala spoke highly of the support shown to her in the SAR.

"The fans are amazing, and they add another dimension to my job and to my life that beforehand I could not even imagine," Eala said.

"Thanks to them I'm able to have such special experiences and create such amazing memories, so I'm super, super happy for their support."

In the doubles final, Japan’s Miyu Kato and Chinese Taipei’s Chan Hao-Ching claimed the title, beating Talia Gibson and Maddison Inglis of Australia 6-4, 6-4.
_____________________________
Last updated: 2026-11-08 HKT 21:01

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Springboks carry out demolition of Azzurri
articles.excerpt: South Africa picked up where they left off in the Nations Championship by dismantling injury-hit Italy 66-7 in Turin on…
articles.fullText:
South Africa picked up where they left off in the Nations Championship by dismantling injury-hit Italy 66-7 in Turin on Saturday to claim a fourth consecutive bonus-point victory.

A Springboks squad boasting more than 1,000 caps ran in nine tries at the Allianz Stadium.

The victory put the world champions alone on top of the Southern Hemisphere standings with a perfect 20 points and +140 points difference following big home wins against England, Scotland and Wales in July.

South Africa face France in Paris next Friday before a trip to Ireland as they look to claim a place in the inaugural Nations Championship final at Twickenham at the end of the month.

The Azzurri will hope to bounce back in their final two home games.

They face Argentina in Genoa next Saturday before welcoming Fiji to Udine on November 21.

In Cardiff, Wales beat Japan 28-21 on Saturday to claim their second win of the inaugural Nations Championship.

Wales entertain New Zealand next weekend eyeing an unlikely first victory over the All Blacks since 1953.

Eddie Jones's Japan have just one win from four fixtures in the tournament.

Meanwhile, in Edinburgh, Scotland captain Sione Tuipulotu was left lamenting his side's ill-discipline following a 43-21 defeat by New Zealand at Murrayfield.

Ewan Ashman became the first Scotland player to score a hat-trick of tries against New Zealand, the hooker's treble coming before half-time to give the hosts hope of a first win in this fixture.

The All Blacks only led 24-21 at the break but Scotland failed to score a point in a second half where Tuipulotu was sent to the sin-bin. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Arsenal extend lead as Forest topple Man City
articles.excerpt: Manchester City suffered a third consecutive Premier League defeat at the hands of Nottingham Forest on Saturday, allowing Arsenal to…
articles.fullText:
Manchester City suffered a third consecutive Premier League defeat at the hands of Nottingham Forest on Saturday, allowing Arsenal to stretch their lead at the top of the table to six points.

Enzo Maresca's men desperately needed a victory at the City Ground to keep pace with the in-form champions, who have taken 27 points from a possible 30, but lost 3-1.

City had a mountain to climb after finding themselves 2-0 down in the 18th minute following goals from defender Jair Cunha and forward Liam Delap.

The visitors were much improved after the break and Rayan Cherki cut the deficit with an emphatic strike into the roof of the net.

But Delap restored Forest's two-goal advantage in the 73rd minute, rifling home with his left foot past the outstretched hand of Gianluigi Donnarumma to earn his side breathing room.

Forest manager Oliver Glasner sprinted down the touchline to celebrate with his team, who had not managed to score a single Premier League goal at home before Saturday.

City, who won their first seven league games under new manager Maresca, know that even if they close the gap to Arsenal, it might ultimately all be in vain.

The Etihad club are still waiting to discover their fate after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules — with a huge points deduction one potential punishment.

Earlier, Arsenal made hard work of beating struggling Hull to underline their title credentials on the eve of the international break.

Captain Martin Odegaard finally broke the deadlock for the champions and title favourites in the 72nd minute.

Arsenal, who bossed possession at the Emirates, had a claim for a penalty in the closing minutes of the first half after Kai Havertz had his shirt pulled by Nobel Mendy.

But VAR ruled that the German forward was in an offside position in the build-up.

Frustration mounted as the second half unfolded, but Odegaard came to Arsenal's rescue, scoring his first goal since early September with a poacher's finish.

Noni Madueke cut in from the right before unleashing a left-footed shot that Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis spilled and Odegaard fired home from close range.

Arsenal manager Arteta praised his players but wants them to be more clinical after they recorded a third 1-0 win in four league games.

"We can still be much better, and we will improve in many phases, and we will get certain relationships to a different level that will be even more efficient," he said.

"That's the next step, to have bigger margins and when we have them, the opportunities, put them away to make sure that we don't have to hang in there the last few minutes."

In the early kick-off, Leeds struck in the 79th minute through substitute Noah Okafor to end Tottenham's three-match winning run.

The major talking point in the first half was a challenge by Leeds defender Jayden Bogle on Spurs winger Mathys Tel, which was reviewed for a potential red card by VAR officials before eventually being cleared.

Tel had to leave the field shortly before half-time.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi, disappointed by his team's second-half showing, refused to be drawn on the incident, which was not reviewed on the pitchside monitor by referee John Brooks.

"In the first situation of Mathys Tel I didn't see, I can't say nothing," he told TNT Sports after the 1-0 defeat.

He added: "I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR and if they didn't take the right decision, I don't know, but we have confidence."

Elsewhere, Jacob Murphy put Newcastle on course for a much-needed win with a spectacular strike in the 80th minute at Craven Cottage but substitute Rodrigo Muniz levelled just three minutes later to earn a 1-1 draw.

Forest's win against City means Michael Carrick's Manchester United will kick off against Aston Villa on Sunday in the relegation zone. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: $10 meals fight social isolation
articles.excerpt: For many elderly residents and caregivers navigating the daily challenges of isolation and limited mobility, preparing a hot, nutritious meal…
articles.fullText:
For many elderly residents and caregivers navigating the daily challenges of isolation and limited mobility, preparing a hot, nutritious meal can feel like an insurmountable hurdle.

But at Shek Pai Wan Estate in Southern District, a novel community dining initiative is providing a vital lifeline, transforming a local children and youth services centre into a hub of warmth, nutrition and connection.

Run by the Aberdeen Kai-fong Welfare Association since March, the Community Dining Hall offers meals for just $10, enticing caregivers and vulnerable residents to make the trip to the centre.

“Everyone gets a good meal. That is wonderful,” said resident Leung Wah-fuk, adding that the no-MSG dishes are both delicious and healthy, which is vital for the elderly.

Fellow resident Leung Wai-chun echoed that sentiment, noting that the support is a genuine blessing for those who find it difficult to walk to the market or manage cooking alone.

Real impact
While filling daily nutritional needs is crucial, the programme’s true impact lies in its power to forge connections and spot individuals who might otherwise slip through the cracks.

Aberdeen Kai-fong Welfare Association Chief Executive Nora Ng emphasised that the target users are high-risk or hidden groups, including elderly residents living alone, caregivers, and families looking after children with special needs.

“Providing hot meals is not our main focus,” Miss Ng said. “Reaching out to high-risk or hidden groups is our main objective.”

Smart resources
This outreach-first philosophy is underpinned by smart resource allocation. Principal Assistant Secretary for Labour & Welfare (Children) Kevin Li explained that the project optimises the use of integrated children and youth services centres during their non-peak hours.

“We leverage the rich social welfare experience and manpower resources of social welfare organisations," Mr Li said.

He added that since these non-governmental organisations historically provide a wide spectrum of services - from rehabilitation to family assistance - they can quickly redeploy their resources to provide appropriate follow-up support for those identified through the dining initiative, embodying the policy goals of early identification, early intervention and sustained support.

Citywide vision
Since its launch, the pilot scheme has yielded positive results, having served more than 4,000 meals, reached nearly 400 hidden or high-risk individuals, and completed close to 350 case assessments.

Mr Li said that the programme serves as a model that effectively reduces social isolation while seamlessly catching those with hidden welfare needs.

What began as a local pilot is now blossoming into a citywide vision, newly backed by the Policy Address. Moving forward, the Government will reach out to integrated children and youth services centres across Hong Kong to invite them to join the initiative, ensuring that more isolated households feel valued, supported and truly seen.

articles.title: China icebreakers set off for Antarctica
articles.excerpt: China held a departure ceremony in Sanya, Hainan, on Saturday to mark the start of its 43rd Antarctic scientific expedition…
articles.fullText:
China held a departure ceremony in Sanya, Hainan, on Saturday to mark the start of its 43rd Antarctic scientific expedition.

Organized by the Ministry of Natural Resources, the mission will upgrade China's polar research stations and logistics network and carry out comprehensive, multidisciplinary surveys and monitoring in Antarctica.

It will also pursue priority research at the frontiers of polar science, test and apply domestically developed equipment, and deepen bilateral and multilateral cooperation in science and logistics support.

The expedition is supported by the icebreakers Xuelong and Xuelong 2, along with another vessel.

More than 600 team members from over 100 domestic institutions are participating, and the team is expected to return home in April. (Xinhua)

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: France's Gehri, Russia's Isakova win HK triathlon leg
articles.excerpt: France’s Nils Serre Gehri produced a dramatic late surge to win the men’s individual title at the World Triathlon Cup…
articles.fullText:
France’s Nils Serre Gehri produced a dramatic late surge to win the men’s individual title at the World Triathlon Cup Hong Kong on Saturday, while Russia’s Diana Isakova continued her strong run of form by claiming the women’s race.

Gehri, who won the U23 title in Pontevedra, Spain, in September, clocked 50 minutes and 14 seconds.

He overtook Australia’s Callum McClusky right at the finish line to seal the victory, with Spain’s David Castro Fajardo rounding out the podium in third.

Hong Kong, China’s Nicholas Tsang finished 58th in 54 minutes and 44 seconds.

In the women’s race, Isakova arrived in Hong Kong fresh from a World Cup win in Rome and made it back-to-back victories, finishing in 55 minutes and 39 seconds.

Luxembourg’s Jeanne Lehair took second, followed by Huang Anqi of the national team.

Hilda Choi was the top finisher among Hong Kong triathletes in 37th place, with Cade Wright 39th and Bailee Brown 50th.

The roughly 24-kilometre course began along the Central and Wan Chai waterfront, with athletes opening with a 750-metre swim in Victoria Harbour.

They then tackled an 18.5-kilometre bike leg past Expo Drive, the International Finance Centre and the Central Piers before closing with a five-kilometre run to the finish line on Lung Wo Road.

The mixed team relay is scheduled for Sunday.

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: He Lifeng in video talk with Bessent amid Cuba row
articles.excerpt: Vice-Premier He Lifeng, who is leading China's economic and trade affair talks with the United States, held a video call…
articles.fullText:
Vice-Premier He Lifeng, who is leading China's economic and trade affair talks with the United States, held a video call on Friday with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Trade Representative Jamieson Greer.

The two sides held candid, in-depth and constructive exchanges on implementing the important consensus reached between the two heads of state at their meetings in Beijing and Washington and the outcomes of economic and trade consultations, and on key economic and trade issues of mutual concern.

The Chinese side expressed serious concern over recent US economic and trade restrictions against China.

Both sides agreed that under the strategic guidance of the two heads of state, they would further leverage the China-US economic and trade consultation mechanism, continuously strengthen cooperation and properly manage differences so as to promote the stable and positive development of bilateral economic and trade relations, and contribute to building a constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity.

News of the video call came as the Ministry of Commerce said on Saturday that China firmly opposes US unilateral sanctions on Chinese enterprises as the move violates international law and the basic norms of international relations.

A spokesperson for the ministry made the remarks in response to a media query that the US Department of State had announced sanctions on two Chinese enterprises and that this was reportedly the first time the United States has imposed sanctions on Chinese companies over so-called Cuba-related reasons.

In recent days, the ministry official said, the US side has escalated sanctions and suppression against China and introduced multiple discriminatory restrictions, which have seriously harmed the rights and interests of Chinese enterprises, deviated from the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, and undermined the stability of China-US economic and trade relations.

China urges the US side to correct its wrongdoings as soon as possible, the official said, noting that China reserves the right to take necessary measures to safeguard its legitimate rights and interests. (Xinhua)

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: Everton in fifth heaven in comeback win over Coventry
articles.excerpt: David Moyes said Thierno Barry had proved his point after the Everton striker's double inspired a 3-1 win against Coventry…
articles.fullText:
David Moyes said Thierno Barry had proved his point after the Everton striker's double inspired a 3-1 win against Coventry on Friday.

Moyes's side trailed to Yann Gboho's goal early in the second half at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

But Barry proved too hot for Coventry to handle, netting twice in the space of just five minutes to turn the game in Everton's favour.

Barry has already reached 10 goals this season, surpassing his total for the entire 2025-26 campaign.

That miserable first season with Everton following his move from Villarreal is quickly becoming a distant memory of the in-form 24-year-old, who has six goals in his last seven appearances in all competitions.

"We gave away a really poor goal but the reaction from there was really good. Important that Thierno Barry got another couple of goals tonight which was huge for us," Moyes said.

"He can smile at me now and say I told you so and that's good. We always liked him and we want him to keep scoring."

Barry had been known for squandering chances that seemed impossible to miss last season, but he has been far more clinical this term.

"He's missed quite a few chances but tonight he got important goals for us," Moyes said after he equalled Harry Catterick's Everton record 592 games in charge.

"He's becoming an important piece for us and he's got 10 goals for us which is really good."

Among Premier League players, only Manchester City striker Erling Haaland has scored more goals than Barry in all competitions this season.

"I'm very happy because I'm a fan of him. I watch a lot of videos of him and try and do the things he does," Barry said.

"If I can stay with him until the end to get the Golden Boot I will try."

Everton are up to fifth place following their third successive win in all competitions.

"We got a performance and we got a result but I have to say Coventry made it really difficult for us. In the end we got the goals which mattered," Moyes said.

Coventry boss Frank Lampard was left frustrated with a pair of rejected penalty appeals that could have turned the match in his side's favour.

Lampard, who managed Everton from January 2022 to January 2023, said: "Big decisions affected the game, clearly.

"VAR looked at them. The James Tarkowski hair pull on Caleb Yirenkyi, then Vitaliy Mykolenko on Taiwo Awoniyi, I think he gets contact on the edge of the box which is a penalty.

"The second goal for them comes off the player's hand. If you're going to check the angles, there is an angle where it flicks in off his hand. VAR looked at it and decided not.

"The last touch to score is off the hand, in my opinion. I've seen a conclusive angle so I can disagree." (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Pakistani to be first foreign astronaut on Tiangong
articles.excerpt: A Pakistani astronaut will join the Shenzhou-24 crewed flight mission as a payload specialist, the China Manned Space Agency said…
articles.fullText:
A Pakistani astronaut will join the Shenzhou-24 crewed flight mission as a payload specialist, the China Manned Space Agency said on Saturday.

After completing a short on-orbit flight, the Pakistani astronaut will return to Earth aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft.

The mission will mark the first joint flight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space programme.

The Shenzhou-23 spacecraft carried the Hong Kong SAR's first astronaut, Lai Ka-ying, as part of a three-strong crew to the Tiangong space station in May. (With contributions from Xinhua)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: North Korean orphans fast tracked into state care to stem declining birth rate
articles.excerpt: Orphanages are now supplied more regularly after shift toward birth-friendly policies.
articles.fullText:
Read a version of this story in Korean
North Korea is attempting to address its decreasing birth rate by improving the conditions of state-run orphanages while increasing crackdowns on illegal abortions, residents in the country told Radio Free Asia.
The total fertility rate for North Korea is estimated to be 1.59 children per woman of childbearing age according to key statistical indicators from South Korea’s Ministry of Data and Statistics. This is well below the replacement fertility rate of 2.1 required to maintain the population.
The rate may be even lower than estimated, a 2025 report by the Washington-based Stimson Center’s 38 North project said.
Orphanages and nurseries were previously poorly supplied, meaning that taking in more children was difficult, but government policies have improved the situation, with supplies of milk, food, clothing and shoes flowing in more regularly, the residents said.
School children arrive to pay their respects before the statues of late North Korean leaders Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il at Mansu Hill in Pyongyang on Sept. 9, 2023.
(Kim Won Jin/AFP) “Recently, authorities have been more quickly sending orphaned children or children born to unmarried women to nurseries or orphanages,” a resident of the country’s northeastern province of North Hamgyong, who requested anonymity for security reasons, told RFA. “The residents’ reaction to this is generally positive.”
The resident talked about a situation where an unmarried woman from Kyongwon county, on the border with China, had to give up her child because of the difficulty raising it alone. The child was quickly accepted into an orphanage in October.
Though the resident did not specify how long it took to place the child, another resident, from nearby South Hamgyong province, told RFA that in another case, in the coastal city of Tanchon, it took about a month.
“In September, in Tanchon, a 6-year-old child became an orphan after his mother, who had been raising him alone, died of illness,” the South Hamgyong resident said on condition of anonymity to speak freely. The child “went to an orphanage after about a month.”
Supplies meeting demand
The government’s apparent priority on supplying nurseries and orphanages has come after a series of child-friendly policies were enacted including the Childcare Law of 2022 and the Law on Preferential Treatment for Multi-Child Families of 2025. Authorities actively encourage childbirth and child-rearing, including by pushing propaganda messaging that “having many babies is patriotism.”
A woman receives the "Communist Mother's Honor Award" during the Fifth National Mothers' Convention in Pyongyang, North Korea, Dec. 4, 2023.
(KCNA via KNS/AFP) The country’s leader Kim Jong Un famously was brought to tears in 2023 when he publicly discussed the declining birth rate at the National Mothers’ Conference in December 2023.
“Putting our efforts into raising the birth rate together with mothers is a critical revolutionary undertaking that cannot be resolved by the power of our Party and government alone,” he said at the event.
Sources in RFA reports after that incident explained that women were reluctant to marry and have kids because they wanted to focus on their own happiness.
Abortion crackdown
Another way the government has been trying to prevent a declining birth rate is to punish doctors who perform abortions .
By law, abortion is illegal in North Korea, but in practice, some doctors accept payment to perform the procedure in secret.
But these days, those doctors are harder to find, the North Hamgyong resident said.
“There are women who come home pregnant after serving in the military, and they try to get rid of the baby quickly before it is seen by others,” the North Hamgyong resident said. “But recently, abortion procedures have not been easy, so many end up giving birth.”
Unwanted pregnancies happen often in North Korea because sex education is non-existent, the North Hamgyong resident said. But even if the mother gives birth, administrative hurdles and societal pressure make it very difficult to raise the child. This is because it is impossible to register the child without the father, and because of the stigma surrounding unwed mothers.
Many unwed mothers are finding creative ways to put their children born out of wedlock in orphanages without having any official record of the birth, the South Hamgyong resident said. “In late September in Tanchon, a resident found a baby wrapped in a sling in a neighborhood alley and took it to the community center.”
Students attend class in North Korea, April 2, 2018.
(KCNA via Reuters) However, it was later revealed that the person who took the child to the community center was actually the maternal uncle of the woman who had given birth, the South Hamgyong resident said. Since the fact that the unmarried woman had given birth might become a major obstacle to marriage if known to the outside world, the uncle had resorted to a workaround for his niece.
The South Hamgyong resident said that the woman did not intend to become pregnant, and had tried to get an abortion but she could not find any doctor willing to provide one.
Edited by Yi Yongin in Korean and Eugene Whong in English.

articles.title: Ferrari boss lays down law to Hamilton, Leclerc
articles.excerpt: Ferrari team chief Fred Vasseur on Friday said both of his quarrelling drivers had been reminded that the Italian team…
articles.fullText:
Ferrari team chief Fred Vasseur on Friday said both of his quarrelling drivers had been reminded that the Italian team always comes first following a meeting at Interlagos.

Speaking to reporters at a scheduled news conference following opening practice at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, Vasseur confirmed that he met seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc to discuss their clash and performance in Mexico last Sunday.

"The guidelines are always the same," said Vasseur. "They are two competitors with a fighting spirit for sure, but they need to have respect for each other.

"But mainly, and firstly, they need to respect the brand, the team, the people working at home, the people working on track. I think we are putting a lot of effort on this and the message was clear -- and will stay clear."

Hamilton, who started from his first pole for the team, had made clear after the Mexican race that he felt Leclerc had been over-aggressive on the opening lap when they tangled and ran off track, wrecking Ferrari's hopes of victory.

The British driver called for serious discussions and confirmed on Thursday that he remained frustrated and would not stop speaking his mind on the issues.

The drivers had not met since the Mexico event as Leclerc returned to Monaco for the birth of his first child.

Vasseur deflected claims, from Hamilton and others, that Leclerc races harder against his team-mates than others by citing his aggressive pass of four-time champion Max Verstappen of Red Bull in Texas.

"If you have a look at what Charles did in Austin in the first sector, everybody said it was magic," he said. "The line is fine between the two, but he didn't crash into the other car."

Vasseur added: "For sure, in this situation, we failed collectively because we were one and two and we didn't win the race at the end. That means that it's clear that we failed and we have to react.

"But the conclusion of the meeting yesterday (Thursday) evening was a clear reminder that the Ferrari is coming first, is coming first for the brand, for the employees, for the Tifosi, and this we have to keep it in mind."

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: US markets close mixed as tech stocks push back
articles.excerpt: US technology stocks bounced back on Friday from their worst drubbing in more than a year, but the Nasdaq Composite…
articles.fullText:
US technology stocks bounced back on Friday from their worst drubbing in more than a year, but the Nasdaq Composite Index posted a fourth consecutive weekly decline as investors sifted for clues about what comes next in the AI trade.

Gains within technology were broadly shared, with the semiconductor index rallying and Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices and Sandisk rebounding.

The broad revival underscores investor faith in the AI buildout that has driven US stock indexes to dozens of record closes this year, despite a shakeout that began with a US long-term Treasury yield spike in August and the stock volatility of the past month.

“We still think AI is the dominant theme in this bull market,” said Keith Lerner, chief investment officer at Trust Advisory Services in Atlanta. “We are still giving technology the benefit of the doubt.”

The S&P 500 climbed 24.70 points, or 0.34 percent to end the session at 7,378.43. The Nasdaq gained 264.42 points, or 1.09 percent, to 24,579.42, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 237.33 points, or 0.46 percent, to 51,285.73.

Lerner said he views the selloff this week, which has taken the Nasdaq into correction territory denoting a 10 percent decline from its peak a month ago, as likely offering a longer-term buying opportunity for many investors.

“AI has gone on trial several times in this cycle and come away with an innocent verdict,” said Adam Turnquist, chief cross-asset strategist for LPL Financial in Charlotte, North Carolina. Referring to the US midterm election results that spurred heavy selling in AI stocks, he said, “This week we saw a little bit of a knee-jerk reaction.”

US nonfarm payrolls increased more than expected in October and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1 percent, suggesting the labour market remained resilient. Traders added to bets that the Federal Reserve could hike rates as soon as next month, with a 78 percent chance of a December move compared with a 70 percent chance seen earlier, according to LSEG.

"Those are strong numbers,” said Joe Saluzzi, co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading in Chatham, New Jersey. But he asked, “Will the Fed want to raise interest rates in the face of a market which is teetering?"

Tesla and SpaceX were among technology shares bouncing back from Thursday’s plunge. Among other stock movers, software firm Atlassian dropped after reporting first-quarter results. Airbnb climbed after the vacation rental platform raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth forecast.

Oil prices were slightly lower, adding to bullish sentiment for riskier assets, and were on track for sharp weekly declines. The S&P 500 energy index was on track for a double-digit weekly percentage drop. (Reuters)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: HK rebuts 10-nation statement
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today expressed strong dissatisfaction with and firm opposition to a so-called joint statement…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today expressed strong dissatisfaction with and firm opposition to a so-called joint statement issued by ten countries, namely the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Japan, Italy, Australia, Canada, the Netherlands, and New Zealand in relation to the sentencing in the “conspiracy to commit collusion” case of Wong Chi-fung, which deliberately distorted facts and smeared the Hong Kong SAR.

The Government pointed out that the statement disregards facts, blatantly interferes with its judicial power and power of independent adjudication exercised in accordance with the law, and maliciously smears the Law of the People’s Republic of China on Safeguarding National Security in the city (the Hong Kong National Security Law (HKNSL)).

It strongly urges the countries concerned to immediately cease interfering in Hong Kong matters, which are purely China’s internal affairs.

The Government stated that Hong Kong is a society underpinned by the rule of law and has been consistently fulfilling its constitutional duty to safeguard national security in accordance with the law, upholding the principles that laws must be observed and strictly enforced to bring offenders to account.

Wong Chi-fung pleaded guilty to the charge of “conspiracy to commit collusion with foreign countries or with external elements to endanger national security” under the HKNSL. The court, acting in strict accordance with the law and judicial procedures, based on objective facts and sufficient evidence, has delivered a sentence independently and impartially, fully manifesting the spirit of the rule of law in Hong Kong.

The Government stressed that everyone is equal before the law. Regardless of their political stance, background or status, anyone who breaks the law must be held legally accountable. Attempting to distort criminal judgments handed down in accordance with the law into actions targeting “political expression” or “political participation” is purely political manipulation deliberately intended to confuse the public and distort right and wrong.

It pointed out that the rights and freedoms enjoyed by Hong Kong residents in accordance with the law are fully protected by the Constitution, the Basic Law, and the HKNSL, among others. However, all rights and freedoms must be exercised within the legal framework and cannot be used as a pretext for engaging in acts that endanger national security.

It is each and every sovereign state’s inherent right to enact laws safeguarding national security. Not only is this in accordance with international law and international relations based on the Charter of the United Nations, but is also an international practice. Many Western countries, including the UK and the US, maintain extensive and strict national security legal frameworks, and will absolutely not allow their citizens to collude with external forces to endanger their own national security.

There are numerous cases in the countries concerned where their own citizens as well as foreign nationals have been prosecuted on charges such as “foreign agent” and “foreign interference”, not to mention instances of arbitrary arrest and malicious prosecution. The groundless attacks by the countries concerned on Hong Kong’s rule of law and judicial system, or their attempts to interfere with the city's work in safeguarding national security in accordance with the law through political pressure, only demonstrate their hypocritical double standards, which are utterly ugly and despicable.

The Government urges the countries concerned to stop making irresponsible and misleading remarks, and to cease interfering in any form in the operation of judicial proceedings of the HKSAR and Hong Kong affairs, which are purely China’s internal affairs. Any attempt to shake the determination of the Hong Kong SAR Government to safeguard national security is bound to be in vain and will never succeed.

articles.title: Summit connects 3,300 youth
articles.excerpt: ​The Home & Youth Affairs Bureau today hosted the third edition of the Youth Development Summit - Hong Kong …
articles.fullText:
​The Home & Youth Affairs Bureau today hosted the third edition of the Youth Development Summit - Hong Kong .

Under the theme “Pioneering New Horizons, Venturing into the Future”, the summit gathered officials responsible for youth policies from various regions, alongside experts and leaders of different sectors as guest speakers.
