The event attracted over 3,300 young people registered to participate, including over 700 from the Chinese Mainland and 35 overseas countries such as the United States, Laos, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, Nigeria and Rwanda, enabling them to exchange views and engage in mutual learning on issues of concern to young people.

Chief Executive John Lee said in his opening remarks that the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government will actively take forward youth development initiatives under Hong Kong's Five-Year Plan, enhance youth development opportunities, and nurture a new generation of young people with an affection for the country and Hong Kong, who are empowered with a global perspective as well as an ambitious and positive mindset.

He added that the Government will continue to expand young people’s international exposure through exchanges, internships and learning experiences, and will work with schools and different sectors of the community to cultivate an environment where young people can unleash their potential and shine on the global stage.

At the session on “Shaping the Future with Youth” held this morning, Secretary for Home & Youth Affairs Alice Mak delivered a keynote speech and shared the vision of the city under Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan in enhancing youth development opportunities, and supporting young people in pursuing their dreams. She highlighted key Government measures and initiatives on youth development that foster a conducive environment for local young people to thrive, and to unleash their full potential.

She noted that the Government would continue to develop the Youth Development Summit as a flagship brand, convening young minds from around the world for exchange year after year. She encouraged young people to step into the new horizons and become the backbone of our long-term economic and social development, and the driving force that will shape our future.

Chief Secretary Chan Kwok-ki officiated at the summit and delivered opening remarks. He also hosted a welcome dinner yesterday for officials, guests, and speakers from the Chinese Mainland and overseas visiting Hong Kong for the summit.

articles.title: More new jobs added in US as unemployment eases
articles.excerpt: US nonfarm payrolls increased more than expected in October and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1 percent, suggesting the labour…
articles.fullText:
US nonfarm payrolls increased more than expected in October and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1 percent, suggesting the labour market remained resilient and giving the Federal Reserve more scope to focus on inflation stemming from the Middle East conflict.

Payrolls jumped by 165,000 jobs last month after an upwardly revised 60,000 gain in September, the US Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said on Friday.

Economists polled by Reuters had forecast payrolls advancing 65,000 after a previously reported 29,000 increase in September.

Estimates ranged from 35,000 to 125,000 jobs.

Economists estimated the economy needed to create at least 40,000 jobs per month to keep up with growth in the working-age population. The so-called breakeven rate has declined from roughly 150,000 in 2024 because of the smaller labour force.

The unemployment rate declined from 4.2 percent in September.

Historically low layoffs and a recent jump in job openings have raised the prospect of labour market tightening.

But economists and US central bank officials have maintained that the labour market poses no inflation risk. Some economists have argued that a shrinking supply of workers amid an immigration crackdown and retirements is the primary driver of the relatively low unemployment rate.

Meanwhile, Canada's unemployment rate went up to a six-month high in October and the economy lost a few thousand jobs as the private sector and full-time employment saw declines, data showed on Friday.

The unemployment rate edged up to 6.7 percent in October from 6.5 percent in the prior month, Statistics Canada said. The last time it was higher than this level was 6.9 percent jobless rate in April.

The economy lost a net of 4,700 jobs in the month, taking the total size of the jobs the economy lost this year to 46,000 overall.

The October report highlights a continued weakness in the labour market in Canada that has failed to post any job gains on average this year as trade tensions between the US and Canada worsened and businesses hunkered down to save costs. (Reuters)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: The Download: a humanoid cleans house and Samsung builds for the AI boom
articles.excerpt: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in…
articles.fullText:
This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

I watched a humanoid robot clean my apartment. It felt like a taste of the future.

—Grace Huckins

When I saw an X post about a new humanoid-robot cleaning service in San Francisco, I immediately signed up for the waitlist. I wanted my apartment to feel like The Jetsons , even if just for an hour.

The device that arrived at my building belongs to Tau Robotics, a local startup. Its long-term goal is to make autonomous cleaning robots a reality, but the technology isn’t quite there yet. For now, humans pilot the robots remotely, watching them work through onboard cameras.

There were some unexpected challenges along the way, but also moments that felt like a glimpse of the future.

Find out how well the machine cleaned my home—and how close we are to truly autonomous domestic robots .

A visit to Samsung’s massive new semiconductor hub

Generative AI models depend on stacks of specialized memory chips. To meet soaring demand, Samsung is building a vast new semiconductor manufacturing campus in Pyeongtaek, South Korea.

I visited the sprawling campus south of Seoul, where three fabs already operate around the clock, a fourth is coming online, and thousands of workers are racing to build a fifth.

Step inside the vast chipmaking complex powering the AI boom .

—Michelle Kim

articles.title: Former Macao lawmaker jailed 12.5 years
articles.excerpt: Former Macao lawmaker Au Kam-san was jailed for 12-and-a-half years on Friday in the territory's first national security case. That…
articles.fullText:
Former Macao lawmaker Au Kam-san was jailed for 12-and-a-half years on Friday in the territory's first national security case.

That came after the court convicted him on one count of subverting state power, two counts of establishing links with organisations, groups or individuals outside the Macao SAR to endanger national security, and one count of breach of secrecy.

The Court of First Instance said the proceedings carefully assessed all the evidence and found most of the indictment facts proven.

Au did not dispute most of the basic facts and admitted colluding and conspiring with overseas organisations, it said.

The court said he had long personally helped hostile overseas organisations collect, prepare and openly spread political advocacy aimed at subverting state power, as well as false and clearly distorted images and information.

That was done, it said, to stir hatred among Macao residents against the Central People's Government and seek to overthrow the fundamental system under China's Constitution.

On the secrecy charge, Au, as a Legislative Assembly member, leaked secret contents from a closed-door committee meeting in 2021 to an overseas organisation, risking very serious consequences.

The Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office said national security is a red line that must not be crossed.

In an article, it criticised Au for long colluding with external forces under the banners of so-called "democracy" and "freedom" to engage in anti-China, destabilising activities in Macao, seriously endangering national security and harming Macao's prosperity and stability.

It says the judgement forcefully upholds the authority of the rule of law, adding that anyone or any organisation that dares to endanger national security will be severely punished by law.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Peruvian scholar hails Lima-Shanghai shipping link
articles.excerpt: A Peruvian expert on Asian affairs urged Apec member economies to take a page from China when formulating policies to…
articles.fullText:
A Peruvian expert on Asian affairs urged Apec member economies to take a page from China when formulating policies to stimulate the economy, pointing to exports and foreign investment as two key drivers.

World leaders are expected to gather in Shenzhen in the coming days, as the southern Chinese tech hub gets set to host the Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting.

On the eve of the summit, Shenzhen Media Group spoke with Carlos Aquino, an expert on China-Latin America ties who has been involved in Apec matters for years.

The director of the Centre for Asian Studies at Peru's National University of San Marcos also advises his government on Apec proceedings.

In an interview with Shenzhen TV, he explained how scholars like him contribute to the bloc.

"Within Apec, there is an Apec Study Centers Consortium. Every year scholars from Apec economies will meet. We give some ideas to officers, and the officers... apply those policies to the economy," he said.

He said Apec could come in handy for nations looking to grow their economies but unsure about where to start.

"For example in Peru, we have industries, but we don't know how to sell... to a market. So within the Apec framework, we can ask for help – economic help, economic cooperation to the whole economies.

"And we have already asked China, Japan, Korea. They sent an adviser, so they tell us how to produce something, or how to sell to those markets."

Last year, Peru's exports reached a record US$90 billion, up 60 percent from 2021.

More than a third of its exports went to China, its largest trading partner, while the United States ranked second at 11 percent.

"The engine of growth of Asian economy has been trade and investment. And also in Peru, that is happening. So we are learning from Asia that to grow the economy, you have to export and also [bring in] investment."

Ties between China and Peru took a big step forward in 2024, when President Xi Jinping visited Lima and inaugurated the Chancay port, north of the capital.

Aquino said the port, built and owned by Chinese shipping giant Cosco, has cut shipping costs between the two countries by 20 percent.

Other South American countries also stand to benefit, he believed.

"Colombia, Ecuador, Chile can bring the goods to Chancay Port and send [them] to China. So it's having a huge change not only for Peru, but also for the whole of Latin America," Aquino said.

"And you know, we are thinking of building a bi-oceanic railway between Chancay and Brazil. Perhaps if that is the case, Brazilian goods also will go cheaper to China."

He said that, as a result of Chancay, Peruvian exports to China jumped by 39 percent in the first seven months of this year.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Record 400-plus HK firms join Shanghai import expo
articles.excerpt: A record high of more than 400 Hong Kong businesses are taking part in the China International Import Expo in…
articles.fullText:
A record high of more than 400 Hong Kong businesses are taking part in the China International Import Expo in Shanghai hoping to use the event as a launchpad for entry into the mainland market.

Among the first-time exhibitors is a Hong Kong accounting firm, which has seen a 30-percent surge over the past year in mainland clients seeking to expand overseas.

Man Law, CEO of the firm's greater China division, told RTHK that venturing abroad was no longer just a trend, but a practical necessity for managing risks and driving growth.

The expo, he said, is an ideal stage to highlight Hong Kong's role as a springboard for international growth, particularly through tax incentives.

"Suppose you have set up an office and hired staff in Hong Kong," Law said.

"When expanding into Southeast Asia or investing in other foreign markets, you can take advantage of the double taxation avoidance agreements signed between Hong Kong and many countries.

"At their peak, tax savings could exceed 50 percent."

Another first-time exhibitor is a craft brewery that is working up a thirst at the expo for its award-winning, Hong Kong-made beer.

The brewery's marketing director said the brand aims to tap the mainland market, confident that its craft beers will be competitive as many mainland consumers have a strong appetite for Hong Kong products.

The event has also drawn local academic institutions, including the Hong Kong Polytechnic University.

PolyU vice-president Zheng Zijian said the university, which has established 12 research institutes on the mainland over the past three years for incubation programmes, has brought innovation projects such as robots and food technology to the expo.

The institution, he stressed, has benefited from the mainland's comprehensive domestic industrial chain and robust support from local governments.

“Our practice over the past few years is to take the path of deep integration with the mainland and contribute to integration with the country's talent, science and technology, and education,” Zheng said.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Second domestically built cruise ship set to sail
articles.excerpt: The nation's second domestically-built large cruise ship, Adora Flora City, was delivered in Shanghai on Friday. The cruise ship, which…
articles.fullText:
The nation's second domestically-built large cruise ship, Adora Flora City, was delivered in Shanghai on Friday.

The cruise ship, which features distinctive Chinese-style characteristics, is scheduled to launch its inaugural season from the Nansha International Cruise Home Port in Guangzhou.

Adora Flora City was built by Shanghai Waigaoqiao Shipbuilding, a subsidiary of China State Shipbuilding Corporation, with construction beginning in August 2022.

Compared with China's first domestically-built large cruise ship, Adora Magic City, the overall construction efficiency improved by 20 percent, according to project figures.

The new ship is larger, with more advanced onboard equipment. Its gross tonnage has increased by 6,400 tonnes to 141,900 tonnes, and its total length has increased by 17.4 metres to 341 metres.

It has 2,130 guest cabins and can accommodate 5,232 passengers at full capacity.

Large cruise ships are among the most complex giant system engineering projects in the global industrial system, said Chen Gang, on-site chief commander and chief designer of the country's domestically built large cruise ship project.

Adora Flora City has up to 25 million parts and drives the development of about 1,500 upstream and downstream supporting suppliers, reflecting the country's comprehensive industrial strength and advanced manufacturing level, he added.

After delivery, Adora Flora City will conduct trial voyages and carry out various preparatory tasks before its scheduled maiden voyage. It is due to arrive at the Nansha International Cruise Home Port on November 12, with its inaugural season set to begin 10 days after that. (Xinhua)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: GBA offers limitless opportunities for lawyers: Lam
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Justice Paul Lam has called on legal practitioners from the two SARs to obtain Greater Bay Area (GBA)…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Justice Paul Lam has called on legal practitioners from the two SARs to obtain Greater Bay Area (GBA) practice qualifications to tap into the area's limitless opportunities.

The GBA lawyers’ scheme – which allows those qualified to practise in nine mainland cities – was regularised in September after a six-year pilot run.

Speaking at the Second Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Lawyers Forum that was held during the Legal Week on Friday, Lam said more than 700 legal practitioners from Hong Kong and Macao have so far obtained the qualification.

“The Greater Bay Area has the characteristic of ‘one country, two systems and three jurisdictions’," he said.

"Greater Bay Area lawyers with dual practice qualifications will serve as pioneers."

Lam noted that the GBA is among the areas with the highest degree of openness and strongest economic vitality in the country.

Hong Kong, he said, will step up the closer interface of rules and laws on the safeguards of the rule of law in the GBA, as laid out in its inaugural five-year plan.

With more than 900 participants attending the event at the Convention and Exhibition Centre in Wan Chai in-person or online, the minister urged them to take the chance to understand the latest GBA developments, grasp new opportunities and expand into new fields.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Bournemouth stay perfect in Europa League
articles.excerpt: Bournemouth extended their perfect Europa League record on Thursday as they came from behind to win 3-1 at 10-man Sparta…
articles.fullText:
Bournemouth extended their perfect Europa League record on Thursday as they came from behind to win 3-1 at 10-man Sparta Prague, while Ruben Amorim's AC Milan suffered a third defeat in four matches.

Gambian Ebrima Singhateh ran from his own half to score a fine individual goal as Sparta took the lead in the Czech Republic after Bournemouth midfielder Lewis Cook hit the post with a first-half penalty.

Sparta had Tobias Guddal sent off before half-time and Bournemouth equalised through Tyler Adams on 57 minutes.

Evanilson steered the Cherries ahead nine minutes from time and Rayan bagged a late third as Bournemouth's substitutes fired the newcomers to a fourth successive victory in Europe.

Marco Rose's side have won each of their past seven matches in all competitions ahead of a Premier League trip to Ipswich this weekend.

"It's a big achievement and we have to continue, we need to stay alert, sharp," Rose told TNT Sports.

"It's up to us to use this momentum. Everyone tries to beat us, if we get in a comfort zone just a little bit we get in trouble."

Milan lost 2-0 at home to Ferencvaros as the Hungarians kept pace with Bournemouth, maintaining their 100 percent record in Europe.

Haiti international Lenny Joseph struck twice in the second half at San Siro to earn Ferencvaros a deserved win over the seven-time European champions despite having Bamidele Yusuf sent off.

"We gifted opportunities, made stupid errors. We were not prepared to play football tonight," Amorim told Sky Sport.

"I don't want to lie to my players. We cannot play like this in front of our own fans. It was a very poor performance."

Milan are languishing outside the top 24 with just three points at the halfway stage of the league phase.

"I won't give up on this competition. As long as we're not mathematically out of it, we'll keep fighting," Amorim added.

Benfica top the standings ahead of Bournemouth on goal difference after a 3-1 win at home to Lech Poznan, with Rafa Silva, Gianluca Prestianni and Georgiy Sudakov on the scoresheet for the Portuguese giants.

Bayer Leverkusen dropped their first points as they lost 1-0 at home toa Marseille team that had lost their first three matches.

Crystal Palace snatched a 1-1 draw at home to Hoffenheim as Japanese midfielder Daichi Kamada levelled in stoppage time.

Alexander Prass gave Hoffenheim an early lead at Selhurst Park and Palace lost Adam Wharton to a second yellow card before Kamada rescued a point for Pierre Sage's struggling side.

Palace, last season's Uefa Conference League winners, have five points from four outings in the Europa League but sit in the Premier League's relegation zone, just behind Manchester United on goal difference.

Sunderland, who have more points in Europe than the Premier League, saw their unbeaten Europa League start ended in a 2-0 home loss to Dinamo Zagreb.

Celtic picked up their first points with a thrilling 3-2 win over Besiktas as Camilo Duran came off the bench and netted twice for Martin O'Neill's side in Glasgow.

Teun Koopmeiners and Randal Kolo Muani netted for Juventus in their 2-1 win at AZ Alkmaar, lifting the Italians up to 10 points.

In the Conference League, Brighton edged past Getafe 1-0 in Spain courtesy of a second-half Malick Yalcouye header.

The Seagulls are two points behind the leading quartet of Lugano, Panathinaikos, Twente and Monaco, who have won all three of their games.

Four-time European champions Ajax thrashed Midtjylland 6-1 in Denmark, while Hearts remain without a win after losing 3-1 away to Thun. (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: LIV Golf league to shut down after five years
articles.excerpt: The rebel LIV Golf tour will shut down after five years that rocked the global game, saying on Thursday that…
articles.fullText:
The rebel LIV Golf tour will shut down after five years that rocked the global game, saying on Thursday that an effort to relaunch after losing its original Saudi backers has been scrapped.

The announcement follows reports that BC Partners Credit, the lead investor in "LIV 2.0," had withdrawn from the project after struggling to convince several star players to fully commit to the league going forward.

In a statement, LIV Golf said only that attempts to implement its Restructuring Support Agreement with BC Partners had foundered.

"Despite extensive discussions, the relevant parties were ultimately unable to reach a consensual resolution of certain outstanding terms of the Transaction contemplated by the RSA," LIV Golf said. "In light of the current circumstances, we believe shifting toward an orderly wind-down is the most responsible path forward for the League at this time."

The statement confirmed LIV attorney Matthew Williams's statements in a 13-minute hearing in bankruptcy court in New Jersey on Thursday.

The once free-spending Saudi-backed league that had turned the golf world upside-down by luring superstars away from the traditional PGA Tour will begin liquidating its remaining assets on Monday, the court heard.

Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) had poured an estimated US$5 billion into the tour since 2022, before abruptly pulling the plug earlier this year.

LIV formally filed for bankruptcy protection in September, though officials vowed to relaunch as "LIV 2.0" next season with a shorter schedule and reduced prize money, and equity stakes in the league for players.

BC Partners Credit had pledged an initial funding commitment of a potential US$300 million.

But several former LIV stars including Jon Rahm publicly announced their decisions to withdraw from the new version of the tour in recent weeks. Several others were believed to be on the fence.

Even Bryson DeChambeau – arguably the breakaway circuit's biggest name, who continued to back the tour – did not publicly commit to returning. (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: International community condemns Joshua Wong’s 10-year ‘foreign collusion’ sentence
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong democracy activist has been in prison since age 23 and is expected to be released around 2036 at…
articles.fullText:
Read a version of this story in Mandarin
After a Hong Kong court sentenced pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong to 10 years in prison Thursday for foreign collusion, international lawmakers, activists, and rights organizations condemned the decision saying it violates human rights.
Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong gets 10 more years under security law
Wong, 30, is one of the most internationally recognizable faces of the now-quashed democracy movement in the city. He was among 45 Hong Kong opposition politicians and pro-democracy activists who were convicted of “conspiracy to commit subversion” under the city’s draconian 2020 National Security Law for taking part in a democratic primary in the summer of 2020. Wong in September pleaded guilty to “conspiracy to endanger national security with foreign or external forces.”
On Thursday, Judge Tam Yiu-ho of the Hong Kong High Court ruled that the case constituted a “serious offense” under the security law, which carries a starting sentence of 13 years. It was later reduced to 10 years in light of his guilty plea.
Wong had already been serving a four-year-and-eight-month sentence for the subversion charge and had been due for release in January, but under the current decision, he will not be released until 2036, when he is 40 years old.
Louis Lee, Joshua Wong's friend, shows a photograph with Joshua Wong in a book published by a pro-democracy student activist group Scholarism in Hong Kong, on Aug. 20, 2026.
(Chan Long Hei/AP) The sentence was “utterly shameless,” Chinese democracy activist Wang Dan, who was a student leader in the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests and who now lives in exile in the United States, said in a statement.
“For a regime that claims to be powerful to pursue and persecute a young student in this manner only highlights its insecurity and brutality,” said Wang. “Joshua Wong campaigned and advocated for Hong Kong’s freedom. If that is considered a crime, then the real criminals are the authorities who forced a young person onto the streets in the first place.”
International condemnation
Joshua Wong’s pro-democracy activities are not criminal, Phil Robertson, Director of the Bangkok-based rights group the Asia Human Rights and Labour Advocates, said in a statement.
“It’s supremely ironic that China, one of the biggest practitioners of transnational repression in the world, has now sentenced Joshua Wong to 10 years in prison for daring to seek international solidarity to resist that repression,” Robertson said. “Holding meetings with international activists and foreign government officials, talking to the global media, and mounting petition drives are the day to day work of human rights activists, and shouldn’t be criminalized.”
Wong is a hero and the charges against him have no standing, U.S. representative John Moolenaar, Chair of the House Select Committee on China, said in a statement.
“Joshua only pleaded guilty to the baseless charge of foreign collusion because of the CCP’s systematic erosion of Hong Kong’s judicial independence,” he said, using the abbreviation for the Chinese Communist Party. “In return, the CCP has effectively sentenced him under its repressive National Security Law.”
Moolenaar said the sentencing showed China’s “complete disregard” for universal rights.
Hong Kong protest leader Joshua Wong, 22, speaks as thousands of protesters surrounding the police headquarters in Hong Kong on June 21, 2019.
(Paula Bronstein/Getty Images) “Joshua and Hong Kong need the international community’s support now more than ever,” he said. “He should be immediately released and reunited with his family.”
Taiwan’s Mainland Affairs Council, or MAC, issued a statement after the sentencing, strongly condemning Hong Kong authorities for continuing to infringe upon the basic human rights under the guise of national security.
The MAC statement said the Hong Kong government’s renewed heavy sentencing under the National Security Law is a continued political prosecution of pro-democracy figures, including Wong, who has been detained for more than 2,000 days since 2020.
The statement called on Beijing and Hong Kong authorities to stop using national security as a pretext to suppress pro-democracy activists and to immediately release those detained for exercising their basic rights.
“Domestic support” for “overseas operations”
The charges allege that between July 1 and November 23, 2020, Wong conspired with Nathan Law, another prominent pro-democracy figure who was in exile overseas, and others to request foreign governments or organizations to impose sanctions, blockades, or other actions deemed hostile by the authorities on China and Hong Kong.
The judge held that after the Hong Kong National Security Law came into effect, Nathan Law continued to push for sanctions overseas, while Wong shared related content through foreign media and social media platforms, attracting the attention of foreign governments and providing support from Hong Kong for overseas initiatives. The judge rejected the defense’s claim that Wong’s role was limited, believing that Wong and Law collaborated and that their roles were equally important.
The defense previously argued that the severity of this case was far less than other national security cases; Wong was only 23 years old when he committed the crime and has been deprived of his freedom for nearly six years, while the prosecution only brought charges after many years. The defense suggested a sentence of about four and a half years and hoped that the court would allow Wong the opportunity to take care of his parents in the future, but this was not accepted by the court.
Steve Li Kwai-Wah, chief superintendent at Hong Kong Police Force's national security department, speaks to the media at the High Court in Hong Kong, Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026.
(Chan Long Hei/AP) The sentence reflected the seriousness of the case, Hong Kong Police National Security Department Chief Superintendent Steve Li Kwai-Wah said to reporters outside the court. He called on Nathan Law to return to Hong Kong and surrender.
Hong Kong and Beijing have consistently stated that their law enforcement actions are based on evidence and law, and are unrelated to the defendant’s political stance, asserting that the Hong Kong National Security Law is necessary to restore stability in Hong Kong.
Undermining freedom
Wang said that Wong’s harsh sentencing reveals that China cares little about human rights.
Student activist Joshua Wong talks on the phone after walking out of the Wanchai police station in Hong Kong on Jan. 16, 2015. A Hong Kong court sentenced Joshua Wong to 10 years in jail on November 5, 2026, for foreign collusion, extending the activist's prison term beyond the six years he has already served.
(Philippe Lopez/AFP) “This decision once again tears away the CCP’s mask, proving that it is a regime determined to be an enemy of universal values and the ideals of freedom,” he said. “Ten years – a person’s youth – spent entirely behind bars; Joshua Wong has paid such a high price. He is a hero of our times and the pride of Hong Kong. I hope everyone remembers him, follows his situation, speaks out on his behalf, and prays for him.”
Edited by Eugene Whong.

articles.title: Overseas university heads eye NM
articles.excerpt: The World Class University Presidents Forum was held at the Hong Kong University of Science & Technology on November 4…
articles.fullText:
The World Class University Presidents Forum was held at the Hong Kong University of Science & Technology on November 4 and 5, drawing presidents and senior management from around 50 world-leading institutions.

The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government is dedicated to transforming the city into an international education hub, a vision that includes developing three university towns within the Northern Metropolis (NM).

This initiative has garnered significant attention from participating universities, with university presidents from the UK, Spain and South Africa expressing interest in exploring various models of participation.

Stuart Croft, University of Warwick Vice Chancellor & President, said the Hong Kong SAR Government is being very strategic, future-oriented and globally oriented.

"With the whole concept of economic growth being driven with universities, with industry, facilitated by government, the triple helix model, where else in the world is there something of this scale and ambition?"

Professor Croft predicted that over the next decade, the world's top universities will transform their partnership model to embedding activities.

"That is what is going to make the difference, and of course the Northern Metropolis gives a fantastic opportunity for Hong Kong universities to build that embedding process, possibly earlier, possibly more deeply than elsewhere in the world, " he said.

In the latest QS Asia University Rankings, Hong Kong has five universities in Asia’s top ten.

Mosa Moshabela, Vice Chancellor & Principal of the University of Cape Town in South Africa noted that Hong Kong’s high concentration of top-tier universities, paired with its convenient transport and lifestyle, promotes student and faculty mobility while bolstering the "Study in Hong Kong" initiative.

"I think it can really offer a good place for brain circulation. For my university, for example, it would be of interest for students and faculty to come in, especially for a relatively short stay of six months. A relatively short stay would be really good for exposure, in-depth exposure to what's happening in Hong Kong, especially if it is linked to industry."

Participating presidents also highlighted the flow of talent, which they said tends to gravitate toward places with strong innovation and research ecosystems.

They expressed hope that the Hong Kong SAR Government would proactively offer incentives to attract and retain talent and support the development of the university town project.

articles.title: Legal Week concludes
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong Legal Week 2026, themed “Collaboration & Innovation: Legal Synergy for a Shared Future” concluded today. Comprising a series…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong Legal Week 2026, themed “Collaboration & Innovation: Legal Synergy for a Shared Future” concluded today.

Comprising a series of events over five consecutive days, this year’s Legal Week demonstrated Hong Kong’s role as an international legal hub by attracting more than 6,000 registrants from over 50 jurisdictions. Participating both online and offline, they held in-depth discussions spanning various topics.

The Fourth Legal Forum on Interconnectivity & Development was held yesterday.

Supported by the Legal Affairs Department of the Liaison Office of the Central People’s Government in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the forum was co-organised by the Department of Justice and the Office of the Commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the Hong Kong SAR.

Deputy Director of the Liaison Office of the Central People’s Government in the Hong Kong SAR Yuan Gujie and Commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the Hong Kong SAR Cui Jianchun delivered welcome remarks.

This was followed by Counsellor of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Wang Chen and Chief Judge of the High Court Jeremy Poon delivering keynote speeches.

The forum featured two keynote sessions exploring Hong Kong’s role as an all-round international dispute resolution hub and its position in the country’s development of foreign-related rule of law.

The Second Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) Lawyers Forum, themed “Rule of Law & Legal Innovation in the GBA: Bridging Legal Talents, Fostering Synergy”, was held today, ending the week on a high note.

A leader from the Ministry of Justice, Wang Limin, delivered opening remarks and a keynote speech on the topic of supporting Hong Kong’s and Macau's legal sectors to integrate into and serve the development of China’s rule of law.

Secretary for Justice Paul Lam, Director-General of the Department of Justice of Guangdong Province Chen Xudong and Chief of Office of the Secretary for Administration & Justice of the Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region Chang Cheong all delivered opening remarks.

Mr Lam said that the GBA has unique advantages under “one country, two systems and three jurisdictions”, adding that dual-qualified GBA lawyers are pioneers who turn the differences among the three jurisdictions’ legal systems into institutional strengths.

He outlined that the GBA lawyers' scheme has been regularised from September, and that more than 700 legal practitioners from Hong Kong and Macau have obtained the relevant practising qualifications to date.

Mr Lam urged Hong Kong legal professionals to enrol in the GBA Legal Professional Examination so as to join the team of GBA lawyers as soon as possible and seize opportunities. This is also one of the objectives set out in Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan.

In a thematic sharing session, representatives from the GBA Lawyers Organization, the Law Society of Hong Kong, and the Hong Kong Bar Association exchanged insights on topics including the regularisation of the GBA lawyers' scheme, the integration of GBA legal talent and professionals, and the role of Hong Kong legal practitioners in GBA dispute resolution.

In a subsequent panel discussion, top GBA and Mainland lawyers drew on their practical experiences to explore how dual-qualified GBA lawyers can capitalise on the unique advantages of “one country, two systems and three jurisdictions” across fields such as cross-boundary commercial litigation, lawtech and green finance, to facilitate Mainland enterprises in “going global”.

The afternoon session brought together renowned Hong Kong, Mainland and Macau mediators to explore the interface of different regulatory frameworks in the GBA through the staging of a mock mediation conducted under the GBA Cross-Boundary Disputes Mediation Model Rules.

Deputy Secretary for Justice Cheung Kwok-kwan highlighted in his closing remarks that the establishment of the Task Force on Expediting the Alignment of Rules & Mechanisms in Guangdong, Hong Kong & Macao, announced in the Chief Executive’s 2026 Policy Address, will allow him to co-ordinate with relevant bureaus on ways of advancing the alignment of rules and mechanisms within the GBA. He said the task force should be established early next year.

Mr Cheung explained that the task force will draw up a list of matters relating to the alignment of rules and mechanisms, with a view to commencing relevant work with the Mainland at an early stage.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo quits international football
articles.excerpt: Cristiano Ronaldo announced his intention to retire from the Portugal national team on Thursday in a social media post, bringing…
articles.fullText:
Cristiano Ronaldo announced his intention to retire from the Portugal national team on Thursday in a social media post, bringing to an end one of the most illustrious international careers in the history of football.

The 41-year-old said he would "hand back the number 7 shirt" after the November international break.

Ronaldo captained the team to their first major trophy at Euro 2016 and helped them win the 2019 and 2025 Nations Leagues.

"It was not an easy decision, because there are decisions that are not made only with the head. They are also made with the heart," said Ronaldo.

"If I ever made you happy, if one of my goals ever made you hug someone, forget a worry or feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it."

Ronaldo thanked his family, the Portuguese people and the teammates, coaches and staff he worked with over his 23-year career with national team.

"Portugal will always be a part of me," he captioned the announcement video.

Ronaldo has made 234 appearances for Portugal and scored 146 goals. He holds the all-time record for international appearances and for international goals. (Reuters)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Kane 'feels right at home' with Bayern extension
articles.excerpt: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane has signed a contract extension with Bayern Munich until June 30, 2029, the Bundesliga club…
articles.fullText:
Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane has signed a contract extension with Bayern Munich until June 30, 2029, the Bundesliga club said on Thursday.

The England captain joined Bayern from Tottenham Hotspur in 2023 and has since helped the German side win two Bundesliga titles, the German Cup and two German Super Cups.

The 33-year-old striker has scored 156 goals in 161 appearances in all competitions for Bayern and capped his prolific spell in Munich by winning the Ballon d'Or last week.

He was the first Englishman to win the prestigious award since Michael Owen in 2001.

"I feel right at home at FC Bayern," Kane said in a statement.

"I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich. We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager.

"It makes me very proud to be part of this club. My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. I'm now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club."

Kane has frequently been linked with a move back to England, where he remains 47 goals shy of Alan Shearer's Premier League record of 260 goals.

However, the striker said in August that the Premier League no longer holds the same appeal for him as he is focused on his career in Germany.

"Since joining us in 2023, he has achieved extraordinary things with his goals, his influence on the game and as a role model both on and off the pitch," Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen said.

"His contract extension is a commitment to FC Bayern and to a story that is far from over."

Bayern did not disclose financial details of the agreement. However, German media reported that the extension is the most lucrative contract in the club's history and part of a long-term commitment to the England captain.

Kane has finished as the Bundesliga's top scorer in each of his seasons with Bayern and was named Germany's Footballer of the Year in 2026.

He has also won the European Golden Shoe twice, awarded to Europe's leading league goalscorer, and captained England to a third-place finish at this year's World Cup. (Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Djokovic to miss ATP Finals after early Paris exit
articles.excerpt: Novak Djokovic crashed out of the Paris Masters on Wednesday after the 24-time Grand Slam champion lost 2-6, 6-3, 6-3…
articles.fullText:
Novak Djokovic crashed out of the Paris Masters on Wednesday after the 24-time Grand Slam champion lost 2-6, 6-3, 6-3 to Australian qualifier Rinky Hijikata in the second round.

The shock defeat by the world number 83 ended the 39-year-old Serb's hopes of qualifying for the ATP Finals later this month.

Speaking in the mixed zone after the loss, Djokovic told reporters his plan for the next few weeks was "just rest".

"I'm looking forward to it," the 39-year-old added.

After sailing through the first set, Djokovic soon found himself in a battle with the Australian qualifier.

Hijikata broke Djokovic in the eighth game of the second frame before serving out to force a decider.

The third set ground on until the Serb cracked serving at 3-3 to hand his unfancied opponent a chance at victory, which he duly took with a second break to seal the match in style.

Djokovic, a seven-time champion in Paris, said he felt "disappointment obviously, losing a match that I felt like I was dominating for the first set".

But he heaped praise on Hijikata for the way he responded.

"He was switched on, I wasn't serving as well and he was just playing out of his mind honestly. He was not missing and keeping the ball low and just a terrific performance," Djokovic said. (AFP)

Edited by Nazvi Careem

articles.title: HK global education role grows
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Education Choi Yuk-lin spoke today at the World Class University Presidents Forum 2026, highlighting Hong Kong's growing strength…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Education Choi Yuk-lin spoke today at the World Class University Presidents Forum 2026, highlighting Hong Kong's growing strength, global voice and strategic vision as a premier international higher education hub. The two-day forum in Hong Kong concludes today.

Addressing the audience, Ms Choi noted that the forum gathered leaders and university presidents representing more than one-third of the world's top 50 universities. "Assembling such a distinguished constellation of global academic leadership strongly reaffirms Hong Kong's standing as an international education hub and significantly enhances the city's discourse power in the global educational arena," she said.

Ms Choi emphasised that Hong Kong's institutional strength is firmly rooted in academic excellence, robust national support and open connectivity. Citing the latest QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027, she pointed out that Hong Kong continues to set regional benchmarks with five local universities securing places among Asia's top 10.

Serving as a vital bridge between East and West, Hong Kong offers a fertile ecosystem characterised by internationalisation and diversification to bring global talent together, she said. The education chief added that the forum forms part of a strategic series of signature initiatives promoting the “Study in Hong Kong” brand worldwide, alongside major events like February’s Asia-Pacific Association for International Education Conference and Exhibition.

Elaborating on the forum's theme, "Higher Education Reimagined: Innovating for the Future", Ms Choi stressed that no matter how the global landscape evolves, universities remain fundamentally tied to economic development, societal well-being and human progress. She noted that world-leading institutions must stand at the forefront to guide this transformation as Hong Kong's educational landscape evolves.

The vision is being physically realised through the development of the Northern Metropolis University Town. The Education Bureau pointed out that under the "One Town, Five Elements" framework, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government is building a holistic campus ecosystem integrating higher education, advanced research, market innovation, vibrant living spaces and top-tier talent.

Positioned at the gateway to the Chinese Mainland, the University Town will foster deep industry-academia-research integration, linking academic research directly with industry capabilities to serve national development under the 15th Five-Year Plan.

articles.title: Student assessment report released
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong Examinations & Assessment Authority (HKEAA) has submitted the 2026 Territory-wide System Assessment (TSA) report to the Education…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong Examinations & Assessment Authority (HKEAA) has submitted the 2026 Territory-wide System Assessment (TSA) report to the Education Bureau, the Government announced today.

The report said that the performance of Primary 3 and Secondary 3 students in the three major subjects ­– Chinese Language, English Language and Mathematics – remained generally steady this year, aligning closely with results from previous assessments.

The Education Bureau welcomed the findings, noting that schools broadly agree that the TSA report provides practical data and analysis regarding student performance. Combined with internal assessment results, this information enables schools to tailor their curriculum plans and instructional strategies to enhance learning effectiveness, fully reflecting the "Assessment for Learning" ethos.

Expressing its gratitude to the school sector, the bureau commended educators for continuously adopting diversified teaching strategies to cater to the varied needs of students and raise instructional effectiveness.

The HKEAA will soon distribute school-level data directly to primary and secondary schools for feedback on learning and teaching. Meanwhile, the bureau will host thematic seminars on "Promoting Assessment for Learning" next month to support schools in making effective use of assessment data to enhance outcomes.

articles.title: Myanmar opposition forces hopeful that U.S. strategy could bring about peace
articles.excerpt: Washington’s framework includes peacemaking to increase regional influence and provide access to rare earths.
articles.fullText:
Updated at 11:30 a.m. ET on Nov. 4, 2026.
Read a version of this story in Burmese
Armed ethnic groups and members of Myanmar’s shadow government are hoping that a recently made public U.S. strategy for their country decrease fighting and bring about peace with the military-backed government, the organizations told Radio Free Asia.
The U.S. State Department recently released an Integrated Country Strategy document for Myanmar that outlines Washington’s aims to use diplomacy to promote peace in the volatile Southeast Asian country, potentially providing access to rare earth deposits dominated by China.
The policy document lays out four mission goals, which include protecting U.S. citizens, addressing trade deficits, promoting peace, and increasing U.S. regional influence through engagement.
Lwe River network, Mekong Tributary, with clusters of rare earth mines in Shan State, Myanmar, Nov. 11, 2025.
(Planet Labs via Reuters) To achieve these goals, dealing with Myanmar’s military-backed government – headed by the same people who ousted the previous government in a coup in 2021 – cannot be avoided. Washington initially shunned engagement with the military after the coup and imposed sanctions on its most senior leaders, but has since softened its stance, rolling back some sanctions and even holding high level talks in September 2026.
A U.S. State Department spokesperson on Tuesday explained the shift to RFA.
“The Administration has been evaluating how to calibrate Washington’s policy towards Burma to achieve regional stability, and also make progress on key U.S. priorities and has determined that wholesale disengagement with the authorities in Naypyidaw countered U.S. strategic interests in Burma and the region. We are pursuing a policy that welcomes dialogue with all stakeholders involved in the conflict as we encourage Burma to make progress on key U.S. priorities, including addressing scam centers, improving the domestic operating environment for U.S. businesses, and building towards a genuine peace process that stabilizes the country.”
Riot police man a barrier in front of the Yangon City Hall on Feb. 6, 2021, in Yangon, Myanmar.
(Getty Images) David Gum Awng, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs for the National Unity Government, or NUG, a shadow government made up of former government officials who were ousted in the 2021 coup, told RFA he understood the realities of the situation.
“The NUG respects and acknowledges that the U.S. government is actively engaging in Myanmar affairs and formulating a strategy aimed at peace, economy, and regional stability. The NUG will continue to engage in discussions with the U.S. government, Congress, and the international community including relevant partner nations.
We will also continue to urge that the U.S. government’s policies and practical actions towards Myanmar support the democratic and federal aspirations of the Myanmar people, address the root causes of the conflict, and lead toward an inclusive political resolution. International engagement in Myanmar affairs should not prolong the military dictatorship, but should aim to bring about genuine political change based on the will and rights of the people after escaping from this bad system.”
Kyaw Ni, Deputy Minister of Home Affairs and Immigration for the NUG, shared his opinion that amidst the policies of superpower nations, one must strive to achieve benefits for one’s own country.
“In this policy shift of a superpower nation, small countries suffer a lot, so a country undergoing revolution like Burma suffers even more. It is likely to be affected. Since these are superpower nations, they write policies based on their own interests. So our public also has to struggle among these policies to reach our desired revolutionary goal without harming the interests of our country, our people, and our revolution.”
The Chin National Front (CNF) soldiers in an undated photo.
(Chin Information Center) Salai Htet Ni, spokesperson for the Chin National Front, an armed ethnic rebel group, said the U.S. government needs to understand the underlying problems in Myanmar politics and get deeply involved.
“The U.S. government needs to understand the military junta’s unjust violence and killing of the people. They need to consider that. On our part, if they can perform first-stage actions like humanitarian aid for war refugees and addressing violent attacks and killings, we would welcome the U.S. involvement even more.”
Another ethnic armed group, — the Karen National Union — said U.S. involvement might reduce the amount of internal fighting, spokesperson Saw Kler Say told RFA on Wednesday.
“The new U.S. strategy could bring about changes or have a specific impact on our country from a military perspective. Firstly, it might lead to a situation where the military junta is compelled to stop its attacks targeting the civilian population.
Secondly, the U.S. might take steps — or offer recommendations — aimed at halting the ongoing internal conflicts. Politically, we also believe they are likely envisioning a political landscape that is acceptable to all parties—one that would include both the detained opposition leaders and the revolutionary forces.
To achieve sustainable peace in Myanmar by 2030, the first step must be to cease attacks targeting the civilian population. The next step involves reaching a consensus on a dialogue process aimed at ending internal conflicts; only through such a mutually agreed-upon framework can a ceasefire be attained.
In addition to these measures, all detained opposition leaders and political prisoners must be released. Without these actions, I believe that any dialogue will be extremely difficult. If detained political prisoners are excluded, meaning the process fails to be truly all inclusive, then a successful outcome may well be entirely impossible.
Regarding the emergence of a federal democracy in Myanmar, the new U.S. strategy presents both positive opportunities and concerning risks. On one hand, it could potentially lead to a genuine transition toward a federal democracy—for instance, by facilitating the abolition of the 2008 Constitution and the drafting and adoption of a new federal constitution. On the other hand, there is a risk that if the discourse is driven solely by U.S. interests, the path toward the federal democracy we envision could be diverted, creating significant challenges."
Representatives of the Kachin Independence Army and the Arakan Army responded that they were not ready to comment.
Arakan Army soldiers in an undated photo.
(Arakan Army) The Arakan Army’s Khaing Thukha asked that questions be channeled through official emails.
Hla Thein, spokesperson for the Union Solidarity and Development Party – formed by former military officers – told RFA that the U.S. strategy document is constructive for mutual interest and should be welcomed.
“Big nations becoming interested in our country, interested from a positive and beneficial perspective, should be welcomed no matter what. We have no permanent friends and no permanent enemies. If they come to cooperate fairly for our country’s interest, our people’s interest, and national interest, we will warmly welcome them.”
RFA attempted to contact Khaing Khaing Soe, spokesperson for the military government’s presidential office, but received no reply.
Col. Saw Kyaw Nyunt, spokesperson for the 7 EAO Alliance of ethnic armed organizations that have individually signed a Nationwide Ceasefire Agreement with the military, said the shift in U.S. attitude might be due to an understanding of Myanmar’s needs.
“In attempting to restart the peace process, international support and assistance are needed. The shift in attitude by the U.S. toward the peace process is likely because they realized that peace is urgently needed due to Myanmar’s reality. By 2030, which is in three or four years, seeking ways to build sustainable peace during that period can be viewed as assessing and speaking on our country’s needs.”
Salai Shein Tun, a secretariat member of the Chin National League for Democracy Party, which won a single seat in Myanmar’s parliament in the 2020 general election, told RFA that the new U.S. policy might face challenges from competitors.
“Speaking of challenges, the challenge from China as a big power is strong. Inside Myanmar and within ethnic regions, the challenge is also strong. In areas bordering neighboring China, they approach with a Chinese style model, whereas looking at the western side, in Chin, Kachin, and Rakhine states, they emphasize federalism. The country they connect with is India … Areas connected with neighboring China do not talk about federalism. Discussions will take quite a bit of effort when those following the Chinese model want to negotiate with the domestic groups that follow the federal model.”
According to the Integrated Country Strategy document, the released text was approved by the Trump administration on Aug. 31, 2026, before the mid-September secret visit to Naypyidaw by Michael Vance, the assistant secretary of state for intelligence and research.
Vance also led at least 12 U.S. government officials during a second round of talks with Myanmar military government officials in Tokyo in the second week of October.
Edited by Eugene Whong.
Update includes comments from Saw Kler Say.

articles.title: Top Uni presidents forum opens
articles.excerpt: The World Class University Presidents Forum 2026 opened today on the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology campus. The…
articles.fullText:
The World Class University Presidents Forum 2026 opened today on the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology campus.

The two-day forum, themed “Higher Education Reimagined: Innovating for the Future”, brings together in Hong Kong presidents and senior leadership figures from around 50 world-leading universities to explore strategic directions for the development of global higher education.

As a premier event in the global education community fully supported by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government and hosted by the HKUST, the forum highlights Hong Kong’s unique strengths and its pivotal status as a bridge connecting the Chinese Mainland with the global higher education system.

Officiating at the opening ceremony, Acting Chief Executive Chan Kwok-ki noted in his speech that higher education has long been a vital pillar of Hong Kong’s success and a cornerstone of its role as a hub for global talent and academic exchange.

He highlighted that Hong Kong is the only city in the world to host five universities in the global top 100 – a testament to the strength of its higher education sector, which is further underscored by the latest QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027.

The Hong Kong SAR Government will continue to align closely with national strategies, accelerate the integrated development of education, technology and talent, and further consolidate Hong Kong’s status as an international hub for post-secondary education through initiatives such as the development of the Northern Metropolis University Town.

Several heavyweight interuniversity co-operation signing ceremonies took place during the event, marking important strategic co-operation agreements between leading institutions and organisations at home and abroad. These included a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on deepening collaboration between Central South University and Monash University; an MOU between Zhejiang University and the HKUST on establishing a joint innovation centre; a Trilateral Joint Seed Fund agreement among the University of Warwick, Nanyang Technological University and Shanghai Jiao Tong University; and a student exchange agreement between Trinity College Dublin and Nanjing University, marking a new milestone in global higher education and research collaborative innovation.

Today’s topics include “The University and the Century Ahead”, “Educating the Human: The Generation Shaping the Intelligent Age”, and “From Ideas to Innovation: Universities Driving the Future Economy”.

A number of prominent leaders from the political, business and academic sectors addressed the forum either in person or via video message, including the eighth Secretary-General of the United Nations Ban Ki-moon, President of the 43rd session of the General Conference of UNESCO Khondker M Talha, President of the China Association of Higher Education Lin Huiqing, HKUST Council Chairman Harry Shum, and HKUST President Nancy Ip.

articles.title: Analysts: China could erode Taiwan’s hold on remote Pratas Island without invasion
articles.excerpt: Restricting supplies could give Beijing leverage, but forcing a withdrawal would risk a wider crisis.
articles.fullText:
China could cut off supplies to Taiwan-controlled Pratas Island, but forcing Taipei to abandon the remote outpost would require a sustained operation that might be too risky for Beijing, analysts told Radio Free Asia.
The tiny atoll known as Dongsha Island in Chinese lies more than 400 kilometers (250 miles) from Taiwan’s main island, about 260 kilometers (160 miles) from the Chinese mainland in the northern South China Sea.
The island’s isolation makes maintaining access by sea and air central to sustaining the coast guard and military personnel stationed there.
Beijing likely has the power to cut Pratas off completely, but such a move might not be necessary at all, Benjamin Blandin, a maritime security expert and visiting research fellow at Taiwan’s Institute for National Defense and Security Research, told RFA.
“China could achieve significant strategic benefits without imposing a complete blockade or forcing an immediate Taiwanese withdrawal,” said Blandin.
For Beijing, the potential gains could include regulating selected activities or compelling Taiwan to negotiate access, Blandin said. Such restrictions could erode Taipei’s authority even while Taiwanese personnel remained on the island.
A map showing the location of Taiwan-controlled Pratas Island in the northern South China Sea.
(RFA) But disrupting deliveries and making the outpost impossible to sustain are different objectives, Sylwia M. Gorska, a doctoral candidate in international relations at Britain’s University of Central Lancashire, told RFA.
“Making Taiwan’s presence unsustainable would require much more extensive restrictions, particularly given the island’s existing air and maritime supply options,” Gorska told RFA.
The portion of the atoll above sea level features an air strip and two piers.
Both analysts cautioned that recent encounters near Pratas do not establish that Beijing has decided to cut the island off, though these encounters have sharpened concerns about access.
Posturing coast guards
Taiwan’s coast guard on Sunday accused China of “harassment” after a Chinese coast guard ship on Saturday went into a restricted area of water near the atoll. A Taiwan coast guard vessel got as close as 1 nautical mile and asked the Chinese ship to leave.
Taipei called on China to “immediately cease” its acts of harassment, after what it said was the 13th such incursion near Pratas Island this year.
China maintains that the atoll is within its sovereign territory and called the incident a “routine law enforcement patrol.”
It was the third Pratas-related incident between the two countries in October alone, with similar incidents occurring Oct. 18 and Oct. 1.
A Taiwan coast guard patrol vessel, right, sailing near a China coast guard ship in waters south of Kinmen, Taiwan, July 8, 2026.
(Taiwan Coast Guard/AFP) Such encounters challenge Taiwan’s authority, the analysts said, but the more consequential test would involve Chinese ships issuing instructions to Taiwanese supply missions, then enforcing compliance.
Blandin identified three potentially overlapping stages: normalizing China’s maritime presence, asserting jurisdiction, and establishing effective control over access.
Demands for identification, inspections or course changes would indicate a move toward exercising authority, he said, adding that repeated obstruction of deliveries, personnel rotations or emergency evacuations would provide stronger evidence of an isolation campaign.
“The distinction between challenging Taiwan’s maritime authority and actively preventing the replenishment of its outposts is fundamental,” Blandin said.
Gorska said requirements for advance authorization or compulsory inspections would signal an attempt to regulate access. Persistent obstruction of successive deliveries, particularly alongside interference with flights, would indicate a more extensive effort to isolate Pratas.
“The principal concern is that Beijing may eventually seek to enforce the authority it is currently asserting, thereby transforming jurisdictional claims into restrictions on access,” she said.
Keeping supplies moving
Taiwan has strengthened its local patrol capabilities. Its coast guard said in September that a wharf renovation had been completed on July 1, allowing newly built 100-ton patrol boats to be stationed at Pratas alongside regular deployments of larger patrol ships nearby.
Those improvements strengthen the response around the atoll but do not guarantee security along its supply routes, Gorska said.
Larger reserves would give Taiwan more time to respond to disrupted deliveries, while maintaining maritime and air transport would provide flexibility. Blandin said sea transport would remain important for substantial quantities of equipment and provisions, with aircraft offering a complementary option when conditions permitted.
The outpost at Pratas atoll, as of Oct. 4, 2020.
(Planet Labs) Escorting deliveries could help preserve access, but repeated Chinese obstructions would force difficult decisions about how far Taiwan should go to challenge them.
Taipei could deploy additional coast guard vessels, improve surveillance or involve military assets more directly, Blandin said. Each option would have to be weighed against the risk of escalation.
“Beijing’s main challenge would be sustaining those restrictions without losing control over the level of confrontation,” Gorska said.
Stopping an individual delivery leaves room to retreat or negotiate, she said. Repeatedly preventing escorted ships or aircraft from reaching Pratas would carry substantially greater risks and could provoke a wider cross-Strait crisis.
Lessons from the Philippines
The Philippines’ efforts to supply its outpost aboard the grounded BRP Sierra Madre at Second Thomas Shoal offer a comparison, although the geography, logistical needs and security arrangements differ.
Blandin said Manila’s persistence in continuing deliveries, along with documenting and publicizing confrontations, offered lessons for Taiwan. Defensive equipment, surveillance and proportionate responses could improve resilience, but none would guarantee access against sustained interference.
Gorska said practical arrangements to prevent dangerous encounters also carried a political challenge: communication should not become an acceptance of Beijing’s claimed authority to approve deliveries.
A Taiwanese coast guard handles a machine gun at a fort on the Pratas Islands in the South China Sea in a file photo from January 2000.
(Reuters) The comparison has another major limit. The Philippines has a mutual defense treaty with Washington, and U.S. defense guidelines explicitly include armed attacks on Philippine coast guard vessels in the South China Sea within those commitments. Taiwan has no equivalent treaty.
The Taiwan Relations Act treats efforts to determine Taiwan’s future through nonpeaceful means, including boycotts or embargoes, as a matter of grave concern to the United States. It does not specify a U.S. military response to interference with supplies to Pratas.
That uncertainty would factor into Beijing’s calculations, Gorska said.
For Blandin, China’s ability to deploy ships around Pratas is only the beginning.
“The central question is therefore not simply whether China possesses the capabilities to isolate Pratas, but whether it could sustain such an operation and convert maritime coercion into lasting territorial control at an acceptable political, military and diplomatic cost.”
Edited by Eugene Whong.

articles.title: 5 HK universities in Asia's top 10
articles.excerpt: The Education Bureau said today that Hong Kong’s higher education institutions had delivered a stellar performance in the “World University…
articles.fullText:
The Education Bureau said today that Hong Kong’s higher education institutions had delivered a stellar performance in the “World University Rankings: Asia 2027” published by Quacquarelli Symonds (QS), an international higher education research organisation.

The bureau said that overall the sector had once again demonstrated outstanding international competitiveness and academic excellence within Asia.

It added that the results reflect the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government’s sustained commitment to investing resources and its proactive initiatives in supporting higher education development, which have consolidated the city’s position as an international post-secondary education hub.

In the latest rankings, the University of Hong Kong retained the top spot in Asia.

A total of five Hong Kong universities are among Asia’s top 10, with three of these ranking in the top five: besides the University of Hong Kong, City University of Hong Kong ranked fourth, with the Chinese University of Hong Kong sitting in fifth.

Eight local universities improved their rankings this year, with all 11 ranked Hong Kong institutions featuring among the top 500 in Asia. The bureau said this demonstrates a comprehensive elevation in the quality of Hong Kong’s higher education.

At the same time, Hong Kong universities continue to lead Asia in key indicators such as academic reputation, employer reputation, internationalisation, and research impact.

The bureau also highlighted that the World Class University Presidents Forum 2026 will be inaugurated tomorrow.

A premier international education event, the forum brings together university presidents, distinguished scholars, and international education leaders from dozens of world-class institutions to deliberate on issues such as talent cultivation in the intelligent era, the role of technology and innovation in driving the future economy, and universities’ responses to major global challenges.

The Hong Kong SAR Government said it will continue to support local universities in reaching new heights and enhance the international leadership of Hong Kong’s higher education sector through various policies and measures. These include advancing the development of the Northern Metropolis University Town, attracting top international research talent and students, and deepening cross-boundary and international academic collaborations.

articles.title: Telling infrastructure stories well
articles.excerpt: Jointly launched by the Development Bureau and the Construction Industry Council, the “Hong Kong Infrastructure NO. 1” campaign seeks to…
articles.fullText:
Jointly launched by the Development Bureau and the Construction Industry Council, the “Hong Kong Infrastructure NO. 1” campaign seeks to deepen public understanding of the city’s infrastructure projects.

Through guided tours, interactive workshops, exhibitions and tailored teaching materials, the campaign shares professional engineering knowledge in an engaging and accessible way, allowing young people to explore careers in the construction industry.

Awe-inspiring visit
A group of primary school pupils toured the education centre at Plant Number 3 of the Kai Tak District Cooling System, where they learnt about the climate challenges facing Hong Kong and how the cooling system works.

Interactive exhibits helped the pupils understand the technology behind the system, while a tour of the plant’s core facilities gave them a close-up view of its large-scale machinery and extensive network of pipes.

The facility completely defied the expectations of Primary 5 pupil Horace Tang.

“I was amazed by the sheer size of the plant and its enormous pipes,” he said.

“I think the district cooling system is remarkable because it helps reduce carbon emissions and save energy. The tour has inspired me to become an engineer in the future.”

Hands-on learning
The initiative focuses on three key areas: education, public engagement and media promotion.

On the education front, the campaign organises guided tours and engineering visits, while also providing a dedicated resource centre, interactive workshops and tailored learning and teaching materials.

The construction-themed materials integrate science, technology, engineering, the arts and mathematics, allowing students to explore subjects such as urban planning in an engaging and practical manner.

Moving beyond classroom concepts, students actively design their own communities within strict special limits and specific guidelines.

Secondary 3 pupil Chui Ki-hin said the workshop transformed his understanding of urban planning.

“I used to think urban planning was simple - that you could just arrange buildings like building blocks and connect the necessary utilities,” he said.

“However, after taking part in the workshop, I realised that it is much more complicated and that there are many constraints to consider.”

Even producing a small model required considerable thought and effort.

“It took me about 45 minutes just to complete this small model. I can only imagine how much more challenging it is to plan a real city.”

International recognition
Apart from its education initiatives, the campaign reaches the community through videos, social media content, exhibitions, quizzes and other public engagement activities.

The campaign’s impact has resonated far beyond Hong Kong. At the 23rd International Business Awards, the promotional initiative triumphed across 10 different categories - capturing six Gold and three Silver awards, as well as one Bronze.

“The aim is to use interesting and heartfelt stories to help the public more easily understand the advanced technologies adopted in infrastructure projects that we see in everyday life, and appreciate the craftsmanship spirit of our construction industry professionals,” Principal Assistant Secretary for Development (Works) Chris Ng said.

He added that Hong Kong’s global standing in engineering would not be possible without the commitment and expertise of industry professionals.

Construction Industry Council General Manager - Corporate Communications Hanks Lee said the trickiest part of the campaign was figuring out how to share professional engineering know-how in a down-to-earth and lively way.

“With the wholehearted support of the industry providing invaluable experience, practical examples and on-site assistance, we were able to tell the story of Hong Kong’s infrastructure.”

Looking ahead, the Development Bureau will continue to leverage digital and innovative media to showcase the technological advancement and professionalism of the construction industry. Through these efforts, it aims to deepen public understanding of the vital role infrastructure plays in Hong Kong’s economic, social and livelihood development, while attracting more young people to join the industry and carry forward the spirit of striving for excellence.

articles.title: U.S. to China after demolition report: ‘End interference in Tibetan religious life’
articles.excerpt: Demolition of monks’ quarters aimed at reducing their population and making assimilation easier, sources tell RFA.
articles.fullText:
The U.S. government Thursday urged China to stop interfering with Tibetan religious freedom after sources in eastern Tibet told Radio Free Asia that Chinese authorities began demolishing monks’ quarters at a monastery there.
Authorities on Oct. 25 and 26 began demolishing about 200 monks’ residences at Dza Sershul Thekchen Dargyeling Monastery in Sershul County in the Kardze (Ganzi in Chinese) Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, sources there told RFA, speaking on the condition of anonymity for security reasons.
“Everything is over now,” the source said. “We are losing everything.”
A U.S. State Department spokesperson told RFA on Thursday that the demolitions in Sershul reflect broader Chinese government efforts to bring spiritual institutions, religious education, and monastic life under government control.
“We call on Beijing to end its interference in Tibetan religious life,” the spokesperson said. “Tibetan Buddhists should have the right to practice their faith freely, educate their clergy and choose their religious leaders, including the Dalai Lama and the Panchen Lama, without government interference,” the spokesperson said, referring to Beijing’s past and likely future interference with the established succession customs of the two most important figures in Tibetan Buddhism.
The demolition in Sershul is not isolated, but part of a larger campaign to reduce monk populations at Tibetan religious institutions. RFA reported in August that authorities resumed demolition of the Larung Gar Buddhist Academy. Activists noted the timing – China’s new Ethnic Unity and Progress Law – had just come into effect the previous month.
The law focuses on reshaping ethnic identity, changing the legal framework around language, expanding state oversight of religion, and extending the law’s reach beyond China’s border.
Dza Sershul Thekchen Dargyeling Monastery in an undated photo.
(Citizen photo) The source in Tibet said that authorities are planning further restrictions that would prevent monks from staying at the monastery after the demolitions.
“Tibetan religion and culture are being destroyed,” the source told RFA, adding that there is little recourse for those opposed to the demolitions.
“No matter how much local people speak out, the authorities do not listen,” the source said. “They do not remember, they ignore us. We have no solutions and we don’t know what will happen.”
RFA contacted the relevant county-level officials in Sershul for comment, but the official who answered the phone did not respond to RFA’s questions and hung up.
Promoting “ethnic unity”
The demolitions and reductions of the monk population are clearly intended to assimilate Tibetans so that they accept Chinese identity, Tenzin Lekshay, spokesperson for the Central Tibetan Administration, or CTA, the Tibetan government-in-exile based in Dharamsala, India, told RFA.
“This is a mask used by the Chinese government under the recently enacted Ethnic Unity Law to assimilate Tibetans and destroy Tibetan religion, culture, and language,” he said. “This is not the first time. We have also seen young monks forcibly expelled from monasteries and sent to China’s colonial boarding schools .”
Though Beijing claims the boarding schools are aimed at providing education to a scattered population, critics have noted that their actual goal is assimilation.
“We strongly condemn the Chinese government’s continued attempts to shut down monasteries and schools established by Tibetans while claiming its authority over Tibet and seeking to eradicate Tibetan national identity,” Tenzin Lekshay said. “It is time for the Chinese government to acknowledge and trust that Tibetan religion and culture are beneficial to China and the world and that the destruction of Tibetan religion and culture will have negative consequences for both China and the world.”
He said that the Chinese government’s actions, which violate international law, would undermine Beijing’s ambition to establish itself as a global leader.
The entrance to Dza Sershul Thekchen Dargyeling Monastery in an undated photo.
(Citizen photo) Tibetan monasteries are central to preserving Tibetan culture and religious identity, Sangay Kyab, Chinese liaison officer at the Tibet Bureau, the CTA’s representative office in Geneva, Switzerland, told RFA.
“Tibetan culture and religion are central to the identity of the Tibetan people.
